questions.text: Sometimes when she feels lost, the author will ______.
options: A. open the window at night
B. lie down in bed to have a dream
C. try to bring back a sense of home
D. go to Los Angeles to visit her mom
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Sometimes when I feel lost, I lie down and shut my eyes, and I go home.'可知，作者感到迷茫时会躺下闭上眼睛，在心中回到家，即努力唤起家的感觉。A晚上开窗是她在家时的习惯而非迷茫时的行为；B躺下做梦想象不准确，是回到家的感觉而非做梦；D去洛杉矶看妈妈无依据，她是在心中回家。

questions.text: What is the author's purpose of writing this passage?
options: A. To express how much she is attached to her home.
B. To declare how much she loves her first house.
C. To describe the state of her family.
D. To look back on her childhood.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕'家对我意味着熟悉感和怀旧'展开，作者详细描述了第一个家的各个房间和回忆，最后说迷茫时闭上眼睛就回家，表达了对家的深深依恋。B宣称多爱第一栋房子过于狭隘，文章不仅是爱房子更是爱家的感觉；C描述家庭状态不是主要目的；D回顾童年只是部分内容，核心是对家的依恋。

items.title: 2013 四川 阅读E
items.passage: Fear may be felt in the heart as well as in the head, according to a study that has found a link between the cycles of a beating heart and the chance of someone feeling fear. Tests on healthy volunteers found that they were more likely to feel a sense of fear at the moment when their hearts are contracting and pumping blood around their bodies, compared with the point when the heartbeat is relaxed. Scientists say the results suggested that the heart is able to influence how the brain responds to a fearful event, depending on which point it is at in its regular cycle of contraction and relaxation. Sarah Garfinkel at the Brighton and Sussex Medical School said, "Our study show for the first time that the way in which we deal with fear is different depending on when we see fearful pictures in relation to our heart." The study tested 20 healthy volunteers on their reactions to fear as they were shown pictures of fearful faces. Dr. Garfinkel said, "The study showed that fearful faces are better noticed when the heart is pumping than when it is relaxed. Thus our hearts can also affect what we see and what we don't see — and guide whether we see fear." To further understand this relationship, the scientists also used a brain scanner to show how the brain influences the way the heart changes a person's feeling of fear. "We have found an important mechanism by which the heart and brain 'speak' to each other to change our feelings and reduce fear" Dr. Garfinkel said. "We hope that by increasing our understanding about how fear is dealt with and ways that it could be reduced, we may be able to develop more successful treatments for anxiety disorders, and also for those who may be suffering from serious stress disorder."

questions.text: What is the finding of the study?
options: A. One's heart affects how he feels fear.
B. Fear is a result of one's relaxed heartbeat.
C. Fear has something to do with one's health.
D. One's fast heartbeats are likely to cause fear.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Fear may be felt in the heart as well as in the head, according to a study that has found a link between the cycles of a beating heart and the chance of someone feeling fear.'可知，研究发现心跳周期与感受到恐惧的概率之间存在联系，即心脏会影响人感受恐惧的方式。B恐惧是心跳放松的结果与原文相反；C恐惧与健康有关过于笼统；D心跳快可能导致恐惧不准确，原文是心脏收缩时更容易感到恐惧，而非心跳快导致恐惧。

questions.text: The study was carried out by analyzing ______.
options: A. volunteers' heartbeats when they saw terrible pictures
B. the time volunteers saw fearful pictures and their health conditions
C. volunteers' reactions to horrible pictures and data from their brain scans
D. different pictures shown to volunteers and their heart-brain communication
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'The study tested 20 healthy volunteers on their reactions to fear as they were shown pictures of fearful faces.'和第五段'the scientists also used a brain scanner to show how the brain influences...'可知，研究通过分析志愿者对恐惧面孔图片的反应以及脑部扫描数据来进行。A仅提到心跳不全面；B健康状况不是分析重点；D心脑交流是研究发现而非分析对象。

questions.text: Which of the following is closest in meaning to "mechanism" in Paragraph 6?
options: A. Order
B. System
C. Machine
D. Treatment
questions.explanation: 根据第六段'by which the heart and brain "speak" to each other to change our feelings and reduce fear'可知，mechanism指心脑相互'对话'以改变情绪、减少恐惧的方式和系统。order命令、machine机器、treatment治疗均不符合语境。system意为'系统、机制'，与mechanism最接近。

questions.text: This study may contribute to ______.
options: A. treating anxiety and stress better
B. explaining the cycle of fear and anxiety
C. finding the key to the heart-brain communication
D. understanding different fears in our hearts and heads
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'we may be able to develop more successful treatments for anxiety disorders, and also for those who may be suffering from serious stress disorder.'可知，这项研究有助于开发更有效的焦虑症和严重应激障碍治疗方法，即更好地治疗焦虑和压力。B解释恐惧焦虑循环不是最终目标；C找到心脑交流的关键是研究内容而非贡献；D理解心中和脑中的不同恐惧过于笼统。

items.title: 2013 天津 阅读A
items.passage: Guide to Stockholm University Library Our library offers different types of studying places and provides a good studying environment. Zones The library is divided into different zones. The upper floor is a quiet zone with over a thousand places for silent reading, and places where you can sit and work with your own computer. The reading places consist mostly of tables and chairs. The ground floor is the zone where you can talk. Here you can find sofas and armchairs for group work. Computers You can use your own computer to connect to the wi-fi specially prepared for notebook computers. You can also use library computers, which contain the most commonly used applications, such as Microsoft Office. They are situated in the area known as the Experimental Field on the ground floor. Group-study places If you want to discuss freely without disturbing others, you can book a study room or sit at a table on the ground floor. Some study rooms are for 2-3 people and others can hold up to 6-8 people. All rooms are marked on the library maps. There are 40 group-study rooms that must be booked via the website. To book, you need an active University account and a valid University card. You can use a room three hours per day, nine hours at most per week. Storage of Study Material The library has lockers for students to store course literature. When you have obtained at least 40 credits, you may rent a locker and pay 400 SEK for a year's rental period. Rules to be Followed Mobile phone conversations are not permitted anywhere in the library. Keep your phone on silent as if you were in a lecture and exit the library if you need to receive calls. Please note that food and fruit are forbidden in the library, but you are allowed to have drinks and sweets with you.

questions.text: The library's upper floor is mainly for students to _________.
options: A. read in a quiet place
B. have group discussions
C. take comfortable seats
D. get their computers fixed
questions.explanation: 根据Zones部分The upper floor is a quiet zone with over a thousand places for silent reading可知，上层是安静区，有超过一千个默读座位，主要供学生在安静的地方阅读。B进行小组讨论是底层的功能；C坐舒适的座位不是主要功能；D修理电脑错误。

questions.text: Library computers on the ground floor _________.
options: A. help students with their field experiments
B. contain software essential for schoolwork
C. are for those who want to access the wi-fi
D. are mostly used for filling out application forms
questions.explanation: 根据Computers部分you can also use library computers, which contain the most commonly used applications, such as Microsoft Office可知，底层的图书馆电脑安装有最常用的软件如Microsoft Office，即包含学业所需的软件。A帮助学生做实地实验错误，Experimental Field是区域名称；C供想连接Wi-Fi的人使用错误，Wi-Fi是自己电脑用的；D主要用于填写申请表错误。

questions.text: What condition should be met to book a group-study room?
options: A. A group must consist of 8 people
B. Three-hour use per day is the minimum
C. One should first register at the university
D. Applicants must mark the room on the map
questions.explanation: 根据Group-study places部分To book, you need an active University account and a valid University card可知，预订小组学习室需要有效的大学账户和校园卡，即首先要在大学注册。A小组必须由8人组成错误，学习室有不同容量；B每天使用3小时是最低限度错误，是每天最多3小时；D申请者必须在地图上标记房间错误，地图上已标记所有房间。

questions.text: A student can rent a locker in the library if he _________.
options: A. can afford the rental fee
B. attends certain courses
C. has nowhere to put his books
D. has earned the required credits
questions.explanation: 根据Storage of Study Material部分When you have obtained at least 40 credits, you may rent a locker可知，获得至少40学分后可以租用储物柜，即需要获得规定的学分。A能付得起租金不是前提条件；B参加某些课程错误；C没地方放书错误。

questions.text: What should NOT be brought into the library?
options: A. Mobile phones
B. Orange juice
C. Candy
D. Sandwiches
questions.explanation: 根据Rules to be Followed部分food and fruit are forbidden in the library, but you are allowed to have drinks and sweets with you可知，食物和水果禁止带入图书馆，但可以带饮料和糖果。Sandwiches三明治属于食物，禁止带入。A手机可以带入，但要保持静音；B橙汁属于饮料，可以带入；C糖果可以带入。

items.title: 2013 天津 阅读B
items.passage: Last night's meteor shower left many people in the community dissatisfied and demanding answers. According to Gabe Rothschild, Emerald Valley's mayor, people gathered in the suburbs of the city, carrying heavy telescopes, expecting to watch the brightly burning meteors passing through the sky. What they found instead was a sky so brightened by the city's lights that it darkened the light of the meteors passing overhead. "My family was so frustrated," admitted town resident Duane Cosby, "We wanted to make this an unforgettable family outing, but it turned out to be a huge disappointment." Astronomers — scientists who study stars and planets — have been complaining about this problem for decades. They say that light pollution prevents them from seeing objects in the sky that they could see quite easily in the past. They call on people and the government to take measures to fight against it. There is yet a population besides professional and amateur star observers that suffers even more from light pollution. This population consists of birds, bats, frogs, snakes, etc. For example, outdoor lighting severely affects migrating birds. According to the International Dark-Sky Association, "100 million birds a year throughout North America die in crashes with lighted buildings and towers." Countless more animal casualties result from the use of artificial lighting. Clearly, people enjoy the benefits of lighting their evenings, but some scientists think it can be harmful for humans, too. They worry that exposure to light while sleeping can increase a person's chances of getting cancer. Emerald Valley is only one community that is becoming aware of the negative effects of light pollution. For years, Flagstaff, Arizona, has enforced lighting regulations in its city in order to assist astronomers at the Lowell Observatory. Similar efforts have been made worldwide, and a movement is underway to remind us to turn off lights when we are not using them, so that other creatures can share the night.

questions.text: It happened last night that _________.
options: A. the city's lights affected the meteor watching
B. the meteors flew past before being noticed
C. the city light show attracted many people
D. the meteor watching ended up a social outing
questions.explanation: 根据第一段What they found instead was a sky so brightened by the city's lights that it darkened the light of the meteors passing overhead可知，昨晚发生的事情是城市的灯光照亮了天空，使头顶流星的光线变暗了，即城市灯光影响了观看流星。B流星在被注意到之前就飞过了错误；C城市灯光秀吸引了很多人错误；D观看流星变成了一次社交活动错误。

questions.text: What do the astronomers complain about?
options: A. Meteor showers occur less often than before
B. Their observation equipment is in poor repair
C. Light pollution has remained unsolved for years
D. Their eyesight is failing due to artificial lighting
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Astronomers... have been complaining about this problem for decades. They say that light pollution prevents them from seeing objects in the sky that they could see quite easily in the past可知，天文学家抱怨光污染几十年来一直没有解决，使他们无法看到过去很容易看到的天空物体。A流星雨比以前少了错误；B他们的观测设备维修不善错误；D他们的视力因人工照明而下降错误。

questions.text: What is the author concerned about according to Paragraph 4?
options: A. Birds may take other migration paths
B. Animals' living habits may change suddenly
C. Varieties of animals will become sharply reduced
D. Animals' survival is threatened by outdoor lighting
questions.explanation: 根据第四段There is yet a population besides professional and amateur star observers that suffers even more from light pollution. This population consists of birds, bats, frogs, snakes, etc. For example, outdoor lighting severely affects migrating birds... 100 million birds a year throughout North America die in crashes with lighted buildings and towers可知，作者关注的是动物的生存受到户外照明的威胁，每年有大量鸟类因撞上有灯光的建筑和塔楼而死亡。A鸟类可能采取其他迁徙路径不是作者关注的核心；B动物的生活习惯可能突然改变错误；C各种动物将急剧减少过于绝对。

questions.text: Lighting regulations in Flagstaff are put into effect to _________.
options: A. lessen the chance of getting cancer
B. create an ideal observation condition
C. ensure people a good sleep at night
D. enable all creatures to live in harmony
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段For years, Flagstaff, Arizona, has enforced lighting regulations in its city in order to assist astronomers at the Lowell Observatory可知，弗拉格斯塔夫市实施照明法规是为了协助洛厄尔天文台的天文学家，即创造理想的观测条件。A减少患癌症的机会不是直接目的；C确保人们晚上睡个好觉错误；D使所有生物和谐生活过于宽泛。

questions.text: What can we learn from the passage?
options: A. Saving wildlife is saving ourselves
B. Great efforts should be made to save energy
C. Human activities should be environmentally friendly
D. New equipment should be introduced for space study
questions.explanation: 本文探讨了光污染对天文观测、动物和人类健康的负面影响，并呼吁人们在不使用灯时关掉灯，以便其他生物也能共享夜晚，所以我们可以学到人类活动应该是环境友好的。A拯救野生动物就是拯救我们自己只是部分内容；B应该大力节约能源不是核心；D应该为太空研究引入新设备错误。

items.title: 2013 天津 阅读C
items.passage: Poet William Stafford once said that we are defined more by the detours in life than by the narrow road toward goals. I like this image. But it was quite by accident that I discovered the deep meaning of his words. For years we made the long drive from our home in Seattle to my parents' home in Boise in nine hours. We traveled the way most people do: the fastest, shortest, easiest road, especially when I was alone with four noisy, restless kids who hate confinement and have strong opinions about everything. Road trips felt risky, so I would drive fast, stopping only when I had to. We would stick to the freeways and arrive tired. But then Banner, our lamb was born. He was rejected by his mama days before our planned trip to Boise. I had two choices: leave Banner with my husband, or take him with me. My husband made the decision for me. That is how I found myself on the road with four kids, a baby lamb and nothing but my everlasting optimism to see me through. We took the country roads out of necessity. We had to stop every hour, let Banner shake out his legs and feed him. The kids chased him and one another. They'd get back in the car breathless and energized, smelling fresh from the cold air. We explored side roads, catching grasshoppers in waist-high grass. Even if we simply looked out of the car windows at baby pigs following their mother, or fish leaping out of the water, it was better than the best ride down the freeway. Here was life. And new horizons. We eventually arrived at my parents' doorstep astonishingly fresh and full of stories. I grew brave with the trip back home and creative with my disciplining technique. On an empty section of road, everyone started quarreling. I stopped the car, ordered all kids out and told them to meet me up ahead. I parked my car half a mile away and read my book in sweet silence. Some road trips are by necessity fast and straight. But that trip with Banner opened our eyes to a world available to anyone adventurous enough to wander around and made me realize that a detour may uncover the best part of a journey — and the best part of yourself.

questions.text: Why did the author use to take freeways to her parents' home?
options: A. It was less time
B. It would be faster and safer
C. Her kids would feel less confined
D. She felt better with other drivers nearby
questions.explanation: 根据第二段We traveled the way most people do: the fastest, shortest, easiest road和第三段Road trips felt risky, so I would drive fast, stopping only when I had to. We would stick to the freeways可知，作者过去走高速公路是因为它更快、更安全。A花更少时间不全面；C她的孩子会感觉不那么受限制错误，孩子讨厌限制，但走高速公路不是因为这个；D有其他司机在附近她感觉更好错误。

questions.text: The author stopped regularly on the country roads to _________.
options: A. relax in the fresh air
B. take a deep breath
C. take care of the lamb
D. let the kids play with Banner
questions.explanation: 根据第五段We had to stop every hour, let Banner shake out his legs and feed him可知，作者在乡间小路上定期停下来是为了照顾小羊Banner，让它伸伸腿并喂它。A在新鲜空气中放松不是主要目的；B深呼吸错误；D让孩子们和Banner玩不是停车的主要原因。

questions.text: What does the author discover from the trip according to Paragraph 6?
options: A. Freeways are where beauty hides
B. Getting close to nature adds to the joy of life
C. Enjoying the beauty of nature benefits one's health
D. One should follow side roads to watch wild animals
questions.explanation: 根据第六段We explored side roads, catching grasshoppers in waist-high grass. Even if we simply looked out of the car windows at baby pigs following their mother, or fish leaping out of the water, it was better than the best ride down the freeway. Here was life. And new horizons可知，作者从这次旅行中发现亲近自然增加了生活的乐趣，比高速公路上的旅程更好。A高速公路是美丽隐藏的地方错误；C享受自然之美有益于健康不是本段重点；D一个人应该走小路看野生动物过于绝对。

questions.text: Why did the author ask the kids to get out of the car on their way back home?
options: A. To give herself some time to read
B. To order some food for them
C. To play a game with them
D. To let them cool down
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段On an empty section of road, everyone started quarreling. I stopped the car, ordered all kids out and told them to meet me up ahead可知，作者在回家的路上让孩子们下车是因为他们开始争吵，让他们冷静下来。A给自己一些时间读书是她之后做的事，不是直接原因；B给他们点食物错误；C和他们玩游戏错误。

questions.text: What could be the best title for the passage?
options: A. Charm of the Detour
B. The Road to Bravery
C. Creativity out of Necessity
D. Road trip and Country Life
questions.explanation: 本文以诗人William Stafford的话开头，讲述了作者一次绕道旅行的经历，最后总结a detour may uncover the best part of a journey — and the best part of yourself，所以最佳标题是Charm of the Detour（绕行路的魅力）。B勇敢之路只是部分内容；C出于必要的创造力不是核心；D公路旅行和乡村生活过于宽泛。

items.title: 2013 天津 阅读D
items.passage: When asked about happiness, we usually think of something extraordinary, an absolute delight, which seems to get rarer the older we get. For kids, happiness has a magical quality. Their delight at winning a race or getting a new bike is unreserved. In the teenage years the concept of happiness changes. Suddenly it's conditional on such things as excitement, love and popularity. I can still recall the excitement of being invited to dance with the most attractive boy at the school party. In adulthood the things that bring deep joy — love, marriage, birth — also bring responsibility and the risk of loss. For adults, happiness is complicated. My definition for happiness is "the capacity for enjoyment". The more we can enjoy what we have, the happier we are. It's easy to overlook the pleasure we get from the company of friends, the freedom to live where we please, and even good health. I experienced my little moments of pleasure yesterday. First I was overjoyed when I shut the last lunch-box and had the house to myself. Then I spent an uninterrupted morning writing, which I love. When the kids and my husband came home, I enjoyed their noise after the quiet of the day. Psychologists tell us that to be happy we need a mix of enjoyable leisure time and satisfying work. I don't think that my grandmother, who raised 14 children, had much of either. She did have a network of close friends and family, and maybe this is what satisfied her. We, however, with so many choices and such pressure to succeed in every area, have turned happiness into one more thing we've got to have. We're so self-conscious about our "right" to it that it's making us miserable. So we chase it and equal it with wealth and success, without noticing that the people who have those things aren't necessarily happier. Happiness isn't about what happens to us — it's about how we see what happens to us. It's the skillful way of finding a positive for every negative. It's not wishing for what we don't have, but enjoying what we do possess.

questions.text: As people grow older, they _________.
options: A. feel it harder to experience happiness
B. associate their happiness less with others
C. will take fewer risks in pursuing happiness
D. tend to believe responsibility means happiness
questions.explanation: 根据第一段When asked about happiness, we usually think of something extraordinary, an absolute delight, which seems to get rarer the older we get可知，随着年龄增长，人们觉得体验幸福更难了，那种非凡的、绝对的快乐似乎越来越少。B把幸福与他人联系得更少错误；C在追求幸福时会冒更少的风险错误；D倾向于相信责任意味着幸福错误。

questions.text: What can we learn about the author from Paragraph 5 and 6?
options: A. She cares little about her own health
B. She enjoys the freedom of traveling
C. She is easily pleased by things in daily life
D. She prefers getting pleasure from housework
questions.explanation: 根据第五段My definition for happiness is "the capacity for enjoyment"和第六段作者描述自己昨天的小时刻快乐：关上最后一个午餐盒房子里只有自己时欣喜若狂，花一个不受打扰的早晨写作，享受家人回家后的喧闹，可知作者很容易被日常生活中的事情所取悦。A她不太关心自己的健康错误；B她享受旅行的自由错误；D她更喜欢从家务中获得快乐错误，她享受的是写作和家人陪伴。

questions.text: What can be inferred from Paragraph 7?
options: A. Psychologists think satisfying work is key to happiness
B. Psychologists' opinion is well proved by Grandma's case
C. Grandma often found time for social gatherings
D. Grandma's happiness came from modest expectations of life
questions.explanation: 根据第七段She did have a network of close friends and family, and maybe this is what satisfied her可知，祖母虽然没有太多愉快的休闲时间和令人满意的工作，但她有亲密的朋友和家人网络，这让她满足，由此可以推断出祖母的幸福来自对生活的适度期望。A心理学家认为令人满意的工作是幸福的关键不全面，还需要休闲时间；B祖母的案例很好地证明了心理学家的观点错误，恰恰相反；C祖母经常找时间参加社交聚会不是重点。

questions.text: People who equal happiness with wealth and success _________.
options: A. consider pressure something blocking their way
B. stress their right to happiness too much
C. are at a loss to make correct choices
D. are more likely to be happy
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段We're so self-conscious about our "right" to it that it's making us miserable. So we chase it and equal it with wealth and success可知，把幸福等同于财富和成功的人过分强调了他们拥有幸福的权利，这让他们痛苦。A认为压力是阻碍他们的东西错误；C不知所措无法做出正确选择错误；D更有可能快乐错误，拥有财富和成功的人并不一定更快乐。

questions.text: What can be concluded from the passage?
options: A. Happiness lies between the positive and the negative
B. Each man is the master of his own fate
C. Success leads to happiness
D. Happy is he who is content
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Happiness isn't about what happens to us — it's about how we see what happens to us... It's not wishing for what we don't have, but enjoying what we do possess可知，幸福不是希望得到我们没有的东西，而是享受我们确实拥有的东西，即知足者常乐（Happy is he who is content）。A幸福在于积极和消极之间不准确；B每个人都是自己命运的主人不是核心；C成功带来幸福错误，文章说拥有财富和成功的人并不一定更快乐。

items.title: 2013 安徽 阅读A
items.passage: Some people will do just about anything to save money. And I am one of them. Take my family's last vacation. It was my six-year-old son's winter break from school, and we were heading home from Fort Lauderdale after a weeklong trip. The flight was overbooked, and Delta, the airline, offered us $400 per person in credits to give up our seats and leave the next day. I had meetings in New York, so I had to get back. But that didn't mean my husband and my son couldn't stay. I took my nine-month-old and took off for home. The next day my husband and son were offered more credits to take an even later flight. Yes, I encouraged — okay, ordered — them to wait it out at the airport, to "earn" more Delta Dollars. Our total take: $1,600. Not bad, huh? Now some people may think I'm a bad mother and not such a great wife either. But as a big-time bargain hunter, I know the value of a dollar. And these days, a good deal is something few of us can afford to pass up. I've made a living looking for the best deals and exposing the worst tricks. I have been the consumer reporter of NBC's Today show for over a decade. I have written a couple of books including one titled Tricks of the Trade: A Consumer Survival Guide. And I really do what I believe in. I tell you this because there is no shame in getting your money's worth. I'm also tightfisted when it comes to shoes, clothes for my children, and expensive restaurants. But I wouldn't hesitate to spend on a good haircut. It keeps its shape longer, and it's the first thing people notice. And I will also spend on a classic piece of furniture. Quality lasts.

questions.text: Why did Delta give the author's family credits?
options: A. They took a later flight.
B. They had early bookings.
C. Their flight had been delayed.
D. Their flight had been cancelled.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段The flight was overbooked, and Delta, the airline, offered us $400 per person in credits to give up our seats and leave the next day可知，达美航空公司给作者一家积分是因为他们放弃了座位，乘坐了更晚的航班。B他们提前预订错误；C他们的航班延误了错误；D他们的航班取消了错误。

questions.text: What can we learn about the author?
options: A. She rarely misses a good deal.
B. She seldom makes a compromise.
C. She is very strict with her children.
D. She is interested in cheap products.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段But as a big-time bargain hunter, I know the value of a dollar. And these days, a good deal is something few of us can afford to pass up可知，作者是一个一流的杀价者，知道一美元的价值，很少有人能拒绝一笔好交易，所以作者很少错过好交易。B她很少妥协错误；C她对孩子很严格错误；D她对便宜产品感兴趣不准确，她是明智地花钱，不是只对便宜产品感兴趣。

questions.text: What does the author do?
options: A. She's a teacher.
B. She's a housewife.
C. She's a media person.
D. She's a businesswoman.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段I have been the consumer reporter of NBC's Today show for over a decade可知，作者是NBC《今日秀》的消费者记者，即媒体人。A教师错误；B家庭主妇错误；D女商人错误。

questions.text: What does the author want to tell us?
options: A. How to expose bad tricks.
B. How to reserve airline seats.
C. How to spend money wisely.
D. How to make a business deal.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段I tell you this because there is no shame in getting your money's worth和But I wouldn't hesitate to spend on a good haircut... And I will also spend on a classic piece of furniture. Quality lasts可知，作者想告诉我们如何明智地花钱——该省的省，该花的花，让钱花得值。A如何揭露坏伎俩只是部分内容；B如何预订机票座位错误；D如何做商业交易错误。

items.title: 2013 安徽 阅读B
items.passage: The baby is just one day old and has not yet left hospital. She is quiet but alert. Twenty centimeters from her face researchers have placed a white card with two black spots on it. She stares at it carefully. A researcher removes the card and replaces it by another, this time with the spots differently spaced. As the cards change from one to the other, her gaze starts to lose its focus — until a third, with three black spots, is presented. Her gaze returns; she looks at it for twice as long as she did at the previous card. Can she tell that the number two is different from three, just 24 hours after coming into the world? Or do newborns simply prefer more to fewer? The same experiment, but with three spots shown before two, shows the same return of interest when the number of spots changes. Perhaps it is just the newness? When slightly older babies were shown cards with pictures of objects (a comb, a key, an orange and so on), changing the number of objects had an effect separate from changing the objects themselves. Could it be the pattern that two things make, as opposed to three? No again. Babies paid more attention to squares moving randomly on a screen when their number changed from two to three, or three to two. The effect even crosses between senses. Babies who were repeatedly shown two spots became more excited when they then heard three drumbeats than when they heard just two; likewise when the researchers started with drumbeats and moved to spots.

questions.text: The experiment described in Paragraph 1 is related to the baby's _________.
options: A. sense of hearing
B. sense of sight
C. sense of touch
D. sense of smell
questions.explanation: 根据第一段She stares at it carefully和her gaze starts to lose its focus可知，实验中婴儿盯着卡片看，凝视随着卡片变化而变化，所以这个实验与婴儿的视觉有关。A听觉是第二段的实验；C触觉错误；D嗅觉错误。

questions.text: Babies are sensitive to the change in _________.
options: A. the size of cards
B. the colour of pictures
C. the shape of patterns
D. the number of objects
questions.explanation: 根据第一段As the cards change from one to the other, her gaze starts to lose its focus — until a third, with three black spots, is presented. Her gaze returns和第二段changing the number of objects had an effect separate from changing the objects themselves可知，婴儿对物体数量的变化敏感。A卡片大小错误；B图片颜色错误；C图案形状错误。

questions.text: Why did the researchers test the babies with drumbeats?
options: A. To reduce the difficulty of the experiment.
B. To see how babies recognize sounds.
C. To carry their experiment further.
D. To keep the babies' interest.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段The effect even crosses between senses. Babies who were repeatedly shown two spots became more excited when they then heard three drumbeats than when they heard just two可知，研究人员用鼓声测试婴儿是为了进一步研究婴儿对数量变化的敏感性，验证这种效果是否跨感官。A减少实验难度错误；B看婴儿如何识别声音不是主要目的；D保持婴儿兴趣错误。

questions.text: Where does this text probably come from?
options: A. Science fiction.
B. Children's literature.
C. An advertisement.
D. A science report.
questions.explanation: 本文提到了experiment和researchers，是研究人员做了一个实验来检验婴儿对数量变化的敏感性，属于科学研究报告。A科幻小说错误；B儿童文学错误；C广告错误。

items.title: 2013 安徽 阅读C
items.passage: It happened to me recently. I was telling someone how much I had enjoyed reading Barack Obama's Dreams From My Father and how it had changed my views of our President. A friend I was talking to agreed with me that it was, in his words, "a brilliantly written book". However, he then went on to talk about Mr. Obama in a way which suggested he had no idea of his background at all. I sensed that I was talking to a book liar. And it seems that my friend is not the only one. Approximately two thirds of people have lied about reading a book which they haven't. In the World Book Day's "Report on Guilty Secrets", Dreams From My Father is at number 9. The report lists ten books, and various authors, which people have lied about reading, and as I'm not one to lie too often (I'd hate to be caught out), I'll admit here and now that I haven't read the entire top ten. But I am pleased to say that, unlike 42 percent of people, I have read the book at number one, George Orwell's 1984. I think it's really brilliant. The World Book Day report also has some other interesting information in it. It says that many people lie about having read Jane Austen, Charles Dickens, Fyodor Dostoevsky (I haven't read him, but haven't lied about it either) and Herman Melville. Asked why they lied, the most common reason was to "impress" someone they were speaking to. This could be tricky if the conversation became more in-depth! But when asked which authors they actually enjoy, people named J.K. Rowling, John Grisham, Sophie Kinsella (ah, the big sellers, in other words). Forty-two percent of people asked admitted they turned to the back of the book to read the end before finishing the story (I'll come clean: I do this and am astonished that 58 percent said they had never done so).

questions.text: How did the author find his friend a book liar?
options: A. By judging his manner of speaking.
B. By looking into his background.
C. By mentioning a famous name.
D. By discussing the book itself.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段However, he then went on to talk about Mr. Obama in a way which suggested he had no idea of his background at all可知，作者发现朋友撒谎是因为朋友在谈论这本书时暴露了他对奥巴马背景的无知，即通过讨论这本书本身发现的。A通过判断他的说话方式错误；B通过调查他的背景错误；C通过提到一个著名的名字错误。

questions.text: Which of the following is a "guilty secret" according to the World Book Day report?
options: A. Charles Dickens is very low on the top-ten list.
B. 42% of people pretended to have read 1984.
C. The author admitted having read 9 books.
D. Dreams From My Father is hardly read.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段But I am pleased to say that, unlike 42 percent of people, I have read the book at number one, George Orwell's 1984可知，作者不像42%的人，她读过排名第一的《1984》，由此可推断出42%的人假装读过《1984》。A狄更斯在前十名中排名很低错误；C作者承认读过9本书错误；D《我父亲的梦想》几乎没人读错误。

questions.text: By lying about reading, a person hopes to _________.
options: A. control the conversation
B. appear knowledgeable
C. learn about the book
D. make more friends
questions.explanation: 根据第四段Asked why they lied, the most common reason was to "impress" someone they were speaking to可知，人们撒谎说读过书的最常见原因是想给说话的对象留下深刻印象，即显得有知识。A控制对话错误；C了解这本书错误；D交更多朋友不是直接原因。

questions.text: What is the author's attitude to 58% of readers?
options: A. Favorable
B. Uncaring
C. Doubtful
D. Friendly
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段I'll come clean: I do this and am astonished that 58 percent said they had never done so可知，作者坦白自己也会在读完故事之前翻到后面看结局，并且很惊讶58%的人说他们从未这样做过，由此可推断出作者对这58%的人表示怀疑。A赞成的错误；B不关心的错误；D友好的错误。

items.title: 2013 安徽 阅读D
items.passage: The National Gallery Description: The National Gallery is the British national art museum built on the north side of Trafalgar Square in London. It houses a diverse collection of more than 2,300 examples of European art ranging from 13th-century religious paintings to more modern ones by Renoir and Van Gogh. The older collections of the gallery are reached through the main entrance while the more modern works in the East Wing are most easily reached from Trafalgar Square by a ground floor entrance. Layout: The modern Sainsbury Wing on the western side of the building houses 13th-to 15th-century paintings, and artists include Duccio, Uccello, Van Eyck, Lippi, Mantegna, Botticelli and Memling. The main West Wing houses 16th-century paintings, and artists include Leonardo da Vinci, Cranach, Michelangelo, Raphael, Bruegel, Bronzino, Titian and Veronese. The North Wing houses 17th-century paintings, and artists include Caravaggio, Rubens, Poussin, Van Dyck, Velazquez, Claude and Vermeer. The East Wing houses 18th-to early 20th-century paintings, and artists include Canaletto, Goya, Turner, Constable, Renoir and Van Gogh. Opening Hours: The Gallery is open every day from 10am to 6pm (Fridays 10am to 9pm) and is free, but charges apply to some special exhibitions. Getting There: Nearest underground stations: Charing Cross (2-minute walk), Leicester Square (3-minute walk), Embankment (7-minute walk), and Piccadilly Circus (8-minute walk).

questions.text: In which century's collection can you see religious paintings?
options: A. The 13th.
B. The 17th.
C. The 18th.
D. The 20th.
questions.explanation: 根据Description部分It houses a diverse collection of more than 2,300 examples of European art ranging from 13th-century religious paintings to more modern ones by Renoir and Van Gogh可知，13世纪的藏品中有宗教绘画。B17世纪错误；C18世纪错误；D20世纪错误。

questions.text: Where are Leonardo da Vinci's works shown?
options: A. In the East Wing.
B. In the main West Wing.
C. In the Sainsbury Wing.
D. In the North Wing.
questions.explanation: 根据Layout部分The main West Wing houses 16th-century paintings, and artists include Leonardo da Vinci可知，达·芬奇的作品在主西翼展出。A东翼错误；C塞恩斯伯里翼楼错误；D北翼错误。

questions.text: Which underground station is closest to the National Gallery?
options: A. Piccadilly Circus.
B. Leicester Square.
C. Embankment.
D. Charing Cross.
questions.explanation: 根据Getting There部分Nearest underground stations: Charing Cross (2-minute walk), Leicester Square (3-minute walk), Embankment (7-minute walk), and Piccadilly Circus (8-minute walk)可知，查令十字站步行只需2分钟，是最近的地铁站。A皮卡迪利 Circus步行8分钟错误；B莱斯特广场步行3分钟错误；C堤岸步行7分钟错误。

items.title: 2013 山东 阅读A
items.passage: Jimmy is an automotive mechanic, but he lost his job a few months ago. He has a good heart, but always feared applying for a new job. One day, he gathered up all his strength and decided to attend a job interview. His appointment was at 10 am and it was already 8:30. While waiting for a bus to the office where he was supposed to be interviewed, he saw an elderly man wildly kicking the tyre of his car. Obviously there was something wrong with the car. Jimmy immediately went up to lend him a hand. When Jimmy finished working on the car, the old man asked him how much he should pay for the service. Jimmy said there was no need to pay him; he just helped someone in need, and he had to rush for an interview. Then the old man said, "Well, I could take you to the office for your interview. It's the least I could do. Please, I insist." Jimmy agreed. Upon arrival, Jimmy found a long line of applicants waiting to be interviewed. Jimmy still had some grease on him after the car repair, but he did not have much time to wash it off or have a change of shirt. One by one, the applicants left the interviewer's office with disappointed look on their faces. Finally his name was called. The interviewer was sitting on a large chair facing the office window. Rocking the chair back and forth, he asked, "Do you really need to be interviewed?" Jimmy's heart sank. "With the way I look now, how could I possibly pass this interview?" he thought to himself. Then the interviewer turned the chair and to Jimmy's surprise, it was the old man he helped earlier in the morning. It turned out he was the General Manager of the company. "Sorry I had to keep you waiting, but I was pretty sure I made the right decision to have you as part of our workforce before you even stepped into the office. I just know you'd be a trustworthy worker. Congratulations!" Jimmy sat down and they shared a cup of well-deserved coffee as he landed himself a new job.

questions.text: Why did Jimmy apply for a new job?
options: A. He was out of work
B. He was bored with his job
C. He wanted a higher position
D. He hoped to find a better boss
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Jimmy is an automotive mechanic, but he lost his job a few months ago.'可知，Jimmy几个月前失业了，因此申请新工作。B厌倦工作、C想要更高职位、D希望找更好的老板均与原文不符。

questions.text: What did Jimmy see on the way to the interview?
options: A. A friend's car had a flat tyre
B. A wild man was pushing a car
C. A terrible accident happened
D. An old man's car broke down
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'he saw an elderly man wildly kicking the tyre of his car. Obviously there was something wrong with the car.'可知，Jimmy看到一位老人的车出了故障。A朋友的车爆胎错误，不是朋友；B野人推车错误；C发生严重事故错误。

questions.text: Why did the old man offer Jimmy a ride?
options: A. He was also to be interviewed
B. He needed a traveling companion
C. He always helped people in need
D. He was thankful to Jimmy
questions.explanation: 根据第二段老人说的话'It's the least I could do. Please, I insist.'以及Jimmy免费帮他修车的情节可推知，老人是因为感激Jimmy才主动提出送他去面试。A也要去面试错误，老人是总经理；B需要旅伴无依据；C总是帮助有需要的人过于绝对。

questions.text: How did Jimmy feel on hearing the interviewer's question?
options: A. He was sorry for the other applicants
B. There was no hope for him to get the job
C. He regretted helping the old man
D. The interviewer was very rude
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'Jimmy's heart sank. "With the way I look now, how could I possibly pass this interview?" he thought to himself.'可知，听到面试官的问题后，Jimmy心一沉，觉得以自己现在的样子不可能通过面试，即觉得得到这份工作没有希望了。A为其他应聘者难过、C后悔帮助老人、D面试官很粗鲁均不符合原文。

questions.text: What can we learn from Jimmy's experience?
options: A. Where there is a will, there's a way
B. A friend in need is a friend indeed
C. Good is rewarded with good
D. Two heads are better than one
questions.explanation: Jimmy善良地帮助老人修车，不求回报，结果老人正是面试公司的总经理，当场录用了他，体现了善有善报（Good is rewarded with good）。A有志者事竟成强调坚持；B患难见真情强调友谊；D三个臭皮匠顶个诸葛亮强调合作，均不符合故事主旨。

items.title: 2013 山东 阅读B
items.passage: George Gershwin, born in 1898, was one of America's greatest composers. He published his first song when he was eighteen years old. During the next twenty years he wrote more than five hundred songs. Many of Gershwin's songs were first written for musical plays performed in theatres in New York City. These plays were a popular form of entertainment in the 1920s and 1930s. Many of his songs have remained popular as ever. Over the years they have been sung and played in every possible way — from jazz to country. In the 1920s there was a debate in the United States about jazz music. Could jazz, some people asked, be considered serious music? In 1924 jazz musician and orchestra leader Paul Whiteman decided to organize a special concert to show that jazz was serious music. Gershwin agreed to compose something for the concert before he realized he had just a few weeks to do it. And in that short time, he composed a piece for piano and orchestra which he called Rhapsody in Blue. Gershwin himself played the piano at the concert. The audience were thrilled when they heard his music. It made him world-famous and showed that jazz music could be both serious and popular. In 1928, Gershwin went to Paris. He applied to study composition with the well-known musician Nadia Boulanger, but she rejected him. She was afraid that classical study would ruin his jazz-influenced style. While there, Gershwin wrote An American in Paris. When it was first performed, critics were divided over the music. Some called it happy and full of life, to others it was silly and boring. But it quickly became popular in Europe and the United States. It still remains one of his most famous works. George Gershwin died in 1937, just days after doctors learned he had brain cancer. He was only thirty-nine years old. Newspapers all over the world reported his death on their front pages. People mourned the loss of the man and all the music he might have still written.

questions.text: Many of Gershwin's musical works were ________.
options: A. written about New Yorkers
B. composed for Paul Whiteman
C. played mainly in the countryside
D. performed in various ways
questions.explanation: 根据第二段最后一句'Over the years they have been sung and played in every possible way — from jazz to country.'可知，格什温的许多音乐作品以各种可能的方式被演唱和演奏，从爵士乐到乡村音乐。A写关于纽约人的错误；B为Paul Whiteman作曲错误，只是为他的音乐会作曲；C主要在乡村演奏错误。

questions.text: What do we know about the concert organized by Whiteman?
options: A. It attracted more people to theatres
B. It proved jazz could be serious music
C. It made Gershwin leader of the orchestra
D. It caused a debate among jazz musicians
questions.explanation: 根据第三段最后一句'It made him world-famous and showed that jazz music could be both serious and popular.'可知，Whiteman组织的这场音乐会证明了爵士乐既可以是严肃音乐，也可以是流行音乐。A吸引更多人去剧院无依据；C让格什温成为乐团领队错误，他只是弹钢琴；D在爵士乐手中引发辩论错误，辩论在音乐会之前就存在。

questions.text: What did Gershwin do during his stay in Paris?
options: A. He created one of his best works
B. He studied with Nadia Boulanger
C. He argued with French critics
D. He changed his music style
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'While there, Gershwin wrote An American in Paris.'以及最后一句'It still remains one of his most famous works.'可知，格什温在巴黎期间创作了《一个美国人在巴黎》，这至今仍是他最著名的作品之一。B与Nadia Boulanger学习错误，他被拒绝了；C与法国评论家争论错误，只是评论家意见分歧；D改变音乐风格错误。

questions.text: What do we learn from the last paragraph?
options: A. Many of Gershwin's works were lost
B. The death of Gershwin was widely reported
C. A concert was held in memory of Gershwin
D. Brain cancer research started after Gershwin's death
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Newspapers all over the world reported his death on their front pages.'可知，世界各地的报纸都在头版报道了格什温的逝世，即他的去世被广泛报道。A许多作品丢失无依据；C举办纪念音乐会无依据；D脑癌研究在他去世后开始无依据。

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Gershwin?
options: A. Talented and productive
B. Serious and boring
C. Popular and unhappy
D. Friendly and honest
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'He published his first song when he was eighteen years old. During the next twenty years he wrote more than five hundred songs.'以及第三段他在短短几周内创作了《蓝色狂想曲》并因此世界闻名，可推知格什温既有天赋又多产（Talented and productive）。B严肃无聊是部分评论家对某作品的评价而非他本人；C流行但不快乐无依据；D友好诚实文中未提及。

items.title: 2013 山东 阅读C
items.passage: You can't always predict a heavy rain or remember your umbrella. But designer Mikhail Belyaev doesn't think that forgetting to check the weather forecast before heading out should result in you getting wet. That's why he created lampbrella, a lamp post with its own rain sensing umbrella. The designer says he came up with the idea after watching people get wet on streets in Russia. "Once, I was driving on a central Saint Petersburg street and saw the street lamps lighting up people trying to hide from the rain. I thought it would be appropriate to have a canopy built into a street lamp." he said. The lampbrella is a standard-looking street lamp fitted with an umbrella canopy. It has a built-in electric motor which can open or close the umbrella on demand. Sensors then ensure that the umbrella offers pedestrians shelter whenever it starts raining. In addition to the rain sensor, there's also a 360° motion sensor on the fiberglass street lamp which detects whether anyone's using the lampbrella. After three minutes of not being used the canopy is closed. According to the designer, the lampbrella would move at a relatively low speed, so as not to cause harm to the pedestrians. Besides, it would be grounded to protect from possible lightning strike. Each lampbrella would offer enough shelter for several people. Being installed at 2 meters off the ground, it would only be a danger for the tallest of pedestrians. While there are no plans to take lampbrella into production, Belyaev says he recently introduced his creation to a Moscow Department, and insists this creation could be installed on any street where a lot of people walk but there are no canopies to provide shelter.

questions.text: For what purpose did Belyaev create the lampbrella?
options: A. To predict a heavy rain
B. To check the weather forecast
C. To protect people from the rain
D. To remind people to take an umbrella
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'forgetting to check the weather forecast before heading out should result in you getting wet. That's why he created lampbrella'可知，Belyaev发明lampbrella是为了防止人们因为忘记带伞而淋雨，即保护人们不被雨淋。A预测大雨、B查看天气预报、D提醒人们带伞均不是发明目的。

questions.text: What do we know from Belyaev's words in Paragraph 2?
options: A. His creation was inspired by an experience
B. It rains a lot in the city of Saint Petersburg
C. Street lamps are protected by canopies
D. He enjoyed taking walks in the rain
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'he came up with the idea after watching people get wet on streets in Russia'以及他在圣彼得堡街头看到人们在路灯下躲雨的经历可推知，他的发明灵感来自一次亲身经历。B圣彼得堡经常下雨过于绝对；C路灯有伞蓬保护错误，当时没有；D他喜欢在雨中散步无依据。

questions.text: Which of the following show how the lampbrella works?
options: A. motor→canopy→sensors
B. Sensors→motor→canopy
C. motor→sensors→canopy
D. canopy→motor→sensors
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'It has a built-in electric motor which can open or close the umbrella on demand. Sensors then ensure that the umbrella offers pedestrians shelter whenever it starts raining.'可知，传感器（Sensors）先检测到下雨，然后电动机（motor）启动，最后伞蓬（canopy）打开。工作顺序为Sensors→motor→canopy，故选B。

questions.text: What does paragraph 5 mainly tell us about the lampbrella?
options: A. Its moving speed
B. Its appearance
C. Its installation
D. Its safety
questions.explanation: 第五段提到：移动速度相对较低以免伤害行人、接地以防雷击、安装在2米高处只对最高的行人有危险，这些都是在讲lampbrella的安全性（Its safety）。A移动速度只是其中一个方面；B外观不是本段重点；C安装也只是部分内容，核心是安全设计。

questions.text: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
options: A. The designer will open a company to promote his product
B. The lampbrella could be put into immediate production
C. The designer is confident that his creation is practical
D. The lampbrella would be put on show in Moscow
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'insists this creation could be installed on any street where a lot of people walk but there are no canopies to provide shelter'可推知，设计师坚持认为他的发明可以安装在任何行人多但没有遮雨棚的街道上，说明他对自己发明的实用性很有信心。A开公司推广无依据；B立即投入生产错误，目前没有生产计划；D在莫斯科展出错误，只是介绍给莫斯科的一个部门。

items.title: 2013 山东 阅读D
items.passage: Sparrow is a fast-food chain with 200 restaurants. Some years ago, the group to which Sparrow belonged was taken over by another company. Although Sparrow showed no sign of declining, the chain was generally in an unhealthy state. With more and more fast-food concepts reaching the market, the Sparrow menu had to struggle for attention. And to make matters worse, its new owner had no plans to give it the funds it required. Sparrow failed to grow for another two years. Until a new CEO, Carl Pearson, decided to build up its market share. He did a survey, which showed that consumers who already used Sparrow restaurants were extremely positive about the chain, while customers of other fast-food chains were unwilling to turn away from them. Sparrow had to develop a new promotional campaign. Pearson faced a battle over the future of the Sparrow brand. The chain's owner now favored rebranding Sparrow as Marcy's restaurants. Pearson resisted, arguing for an advertising campaign designed to convince customers that visits to Sparrow restaurants were fun. Such an attempt to establish a positive relationship between a company and the general public was unusual for that time. Pearson strongly believed that numbers were the key to success, rather than customers' spending power. Finally, the owner accepted his idea. The campaign itself changed the traditional advertising style of the fast-food industry. The TV ads of Sparrow focused on entertainment and featured original songs performed by a variety of stars. Instead of showing the superiority of a specific product, the intention was to put Sparrow in the hearts of potential customers. Pearson also made other decisions which he believed would contribute to the new Sparrow image. For example, he offered to lower the rent of any restaurants which achieved a certain increase in their turnover. These efforts paid off, and Sparrow soon became one of the most successful fast-food chains in the regions where it operated.

questions.text: Which was one of the problems Sparrow faced before Pearson became CEO?
options: A. The number of its customers was declining
B. Its customers found the food unhealthy
C. It was in need of financial support
D. Most of its restaurants were closed
questions.explanation: 根据第一段最后一句'And to make matters worse, its new owner had no plans to give it the funds it required.'可知，Sparrow面临的问题之一是新老板不打算提供所需资金，即它需要财务支持。A顾客数量下降错误，原文说'no sign of declining'；B顾客觉得食物不健康错误，原文是'chain was generally in an unhealthy state'指经营状态不健康；D大部分餐厅关闭无依据。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "them" in Paragraph 2 refer to?
options: A. Customers of Sparrow restaurants
B. Sparrow restaurants
C. Customers of other fast-food chains
D. other fast-food chains
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'customers of other fast-food chains were unwilling to turn away from them'可知，其他快餐连锁店的顾客不愿意离开它们，them指代前面提到的other fast-food chains（其他快餐连锁店）。A Sparrow的顾客、B Sparrow餐厅、C其他快餐连锁店的顾客均不符合逻辑。

questions.text: For what purpose did Pearson start the advertising campaign?
options: A. To build a good relationship with the public
B. To stress the unusual tradition of Sparrow
C. To learn about customers' spending power
D. To meet the challenge from Marcy's restaurants
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'aruing for an advertising campaign designed to convince customers that visits to Sparrow restaurants were fun. Such an attempt to establish a positive relationship between a company and the general public was unusual for that time.'可知，Pearson发起广告活动的目的是建立公司与公众之间的积极关系。B强调Sparrow的不寻常传统错误；C了解顾客消费力错误，他认为客流量才是关键；D应对Marcy's餐厅的挑战错误，他抵制了品牌重塑为Marcy's的提议。

questions.text: The TV ads of Sparrow ________.
options: A. changed people's views on pop stars
B. amused the public with original songs
C. focused on the superiority of its products
D. influenced the eating habits of the audience
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'The TV ads of Sparrow focused on entertainment and featured original songs performed by a variety of stars.'可知，Sparrow的电视广告以娱乐为核心，以各种明星表演的原创歌曲为特色，即用原创歌曲娱乐公众。A改变人们对流行明星的看法无依据；C专注于产品优势错误，原文说'Instead of showing the superiority of a specific product'；D影响观众饮食习惯无依据。

questions.text: What was Pearson's achievement as a CEO?
options: A. He managed to pay off Sparrow's debts
B. He made Sparrow much more competitive
C. He helped Sparrow take over a company
D. He improved the welfare of Sparrow employees
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'These efforts paid off, and Sparrow soon became one of the most successful fast-food chains in the regions where it operated.'可推知，Pearson作为CEO的成就是让Sparrow成为当地最成功的快餐连锁之一，即使其更具竞争力。A还清债务无依据；C帮助Sparrow收购公司错误，是Sparrow被收购；D改善员工福利无依据。

items.title: 2013 广东 阅读A
items.passage: Imagination and fantasy can play an important role in achieving the things we fear. Children know this very well. Fred Epstein, in his book If I Make It to Five, tells a story he heard from one of his friends about Tom, a four-year-old boy with a cancer in his back bone. He came through several operations and a lot of pain by mastering his imagination. Tom loved to pretend, and he particularly loved to play superheroes. Dr. Epstein explained that it was actually a brilliant way for his young mind to handle the terrifying and painful life he led. The day before his third trip to the operating room, Tom was terribly afraid. "Maybe I could go as Superman," he whispered to his mom. Hearing this, the mother hesitated for a while. She had avoided buying the expensive costume, finally she agreed. The next day Tom appeared as the powerful Superman, showing off through the hospital halls and coolly waving his hand to the people greeting him along the way. And Tom, with the strength of his fantasy, successfully made it through the operation. The power of imagination need not be reserved for children only. We all have the power to use our fantasies to attempt things we never thought possible, to go through those things that seem impossible, and to achieve what we never believed we could. Just as Dr. Epstein puts it, "If you can dream it, you can do it." It doesn't mean that you should dress as a superhero for your next job interview. But, next time you are tested in a way that seems impossible, imagine what it would take to overcome it. Become the person you need to become to win over your challenge and do it in your mind first. So, let your imagination run wild, and dare to dream.

questions.text: What do we know about Tom?
options: A. He was seriously ill
B. He was a dishonest boy.
C. He was crazy about magic
D. He was Dr. Epstein's patient
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Tom, a four-year-old boy with a cancer in his back bone. He came through several operations and a lot of pain'可知，Tom患有脊柱癌，经历了多次手术和痛苦，即病得很重。B不诚实的男孩错误；C对魔法疯狂错误，他喜欢扮演超级英雄；D是Epstein医生的病人错误，故事是Epstein从朋友那里听来的。

questions.text: What can be inferred about Tom's mother?
options: A. She was a rich lady
B. She refused Tom's request
C. She wanted Tom to be a superhero
D. She wanted to get Tom through the pain
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'She had avoided buying the expensive costume, finally she agreed.'可推知，母亲虽然犹豫且戏装很贵，但最终还是同意了，说明她想帮助Tom度过痛苦（通过让他扮演超人获得勇气）。A富有的女士错误，她嫌贵；B拒绝Tom的请求错误，最终同意了；C想让Tom成为超人错误，是Tom自己想扮演超人。

questions.text: When Tom went for the third operation, he ______.
options: A. pretended to be painful
B. acted like a superhero
C. appeared in poor spirits
D. argued with his mother
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'The next day Tom appeared as the powerful Superman, showing off through the hospital halls'可知，Tom第三次手术时扮演了强大的超人。A假装痛苦错误；C精神不佳错误，他表现得很自信；D与母亲争论错误。

questions.text: In the last paragraph, you are advised ______.
options: A. to go through some difficult tests
B. to wake up from your wild dreams
C. to become a powerful person in your mind
D. to wear expensive clothes for job interviews
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Become the person you need to become to win over your challenge and do it in your mind first.'可知，作者建议读者先在心中成为需要成为的人，即在心中成为强大的人。A经历困难测试错误；B从狂热的梦中醒来错误，作者鼓励敢于梦想；D穿昂贵衣服参加面试错误，作者说不意味着要穿成超人去面试。

questions.text: What is the purpose of the passage?
options: A. To tell us an interesting story.
B. To help us make right decisions.
C. To advise us to care about children.
D. To encourage us to use our imagination.
questions.explanation: 文章首段点明'Imagination and fantasy can play an important role in achieving the things we fear'，通过Tom的故事说明想象力的力量，最后一段呼吁'let your imagination run wild, and dare to dream'，全文目的是鼓励读者运用想象力。A讲有趣故事只是手段；B帮助做正确决定无依据；C建议关心孩子偏离主题。

items.title: 2013 广东 阅读B
items.passage: Some people think that success is only for those with talent or those who grow up in the right family, and others believe that success mostly comes down to luck. I'm not going to say luck, talent, and circumstances don't come into play because they do. Some people are born into the right family while others are born with great intelligence, and that's just the reality of how life is. However, to succeed in life, one first needs to set a goal and then gradually make it more practical. And, in addition to that, in order to get really good at something, one needs to spend at least 10,000 hours studying and practicing. To become great at certain things, it'll require even more time, time that most people won't put in. This is a big reason why many successful people advise you to do something you love. If you don't enjoy what you do, it is going to feel like unbearable pain and will likely make you quit well before you ever become good at it. When you see people exhibiting some great skills or having achieved great success, you know that they have put in a huge part of their life to get there at a huge cost. It's sometimes easy to think they got lucky or they were born with some rare talent, but thinking that way does you no good, and there's a huge chance that you're wrong anyway. Whatever you do, if you want to become great at it, you need to work day in and day out, almost to the point of addiction, and over a long period of time. If you're not willing to put in the time and work, don't expect to receive any rewards. Consistent, hard work won't guarantee you the level of success you may want, but it will guarantee that you will become really good at whatever it is you put all that work into.

questions.text: Paragraph 1 mainly talks about ________.
options: A. the reasons for success
B. the meaning of success
C. the standards of success
D. the importance of success
questions.explanation: 第一段提到有人认为成功属于有天赋或出身好的人，有人认为成功主要靠运气，作者承认这些因素确实起作用，全段在讨论成功的原因（reasons for success）。B成功的意义、C成功的标准、D成功的重要性均不是第一段主旨。

questions.text: In Paragraph 2, the underlined word that refers to ______.
options: A. being good at something
B. setting a practical goal
C. putting in more time
D. succeeding in life
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'one first needs to set a goal and then gradually make it more practical. And, in addition to that, in order to get really good at something, one needs to spend at least 10,000 hours'可知，that指代前面提到的'set a goal and then gradually make it more practical'，即设定实际目标。A擅长某事、C投入更多时间、D在生活中成功均不符合指代逻辑。

questions.text: Successful people suggest doing what one loves because ______.
options: A. work makes one feel pain
B. one tends to enjoy his work
C. one gives up his work easily
D. it takes a lot of time to succeed
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'If you don't enjoy what you do, it is going to feel like unbearable pain and will likely make you quit well before you ever become good at it.'以及第二段提到成功需要至少10000小时可推知，成功人士建议做热爱的事是因为成功需要大量时间投入，只有热爱才能坚持。A工作让人痛苦是不热爱的结果而非原因；B人往往喜欢工作过于笼统；C人容易放弃工作是不热爱的表现。

questions.text: What can we infer from Paragraph 4?
options: A. Successful people like to show their great skills.
B. People sometimes succeed without luck or talent.
C. People need to achieve success at the cost of life.
D. It helps to think that luck or talent leads to success.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'It's sometimes easy to think they got lucky or they were born with some rare talent, but thinking that way does you no good, and there's a huge chance that you're wrong anyway.'可推知，人们有时认为别人成功是靠运气或天赋，但这种想法很可能是错的，即有些人的成功并非靠运气或天赋，而是靠努力。A成功人士喜欢炫耀技能错误；C需要以生命为代价获得成功过于绝对；D认为运气或天赋带来成功有帮助错误，作者说这种想法对你没好处。

questions.text: What is the main theme of the passage?
options: A. Having a goal is vital to success.
B. Being good is different from being great.
C. One cannot succeed without time and practice.
D. Luck, talent and family help to achieve success.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕成功需要大量时间和练习展开：第二段提出需要至少10000小时，第三段说做热爱的事才能坚持投入时间，第四段说成功人士付出了巨大代价，最后一段强调需要日复一日长期努力。核心主题是没有时间和练习就无法成功。A有目标对成功至关重要只是部分内容；B优秀和伟大不同不是主题；D运气天赋家庭有帮助是作者承认但非强调的重点。

items.title: 2013 广东 阅读C
items.passage: One day, when I was working as a psychologist in England, an adolescent boy showed up in my office. It was David. He kept walking up and down restlessly, his face pale, and his hands shaking slightly. His head teacher had referred him to me. "This boy has lost his family," he wrote. "He is understandably very sad and refuses to talk to others, and I'm very worried about him. Can you help?" I looked at David and showed him to a chair. How could I help him? There are problems psychology doesn't have the answer to, and which no words can describe. Sometimes the best thing one can do is to listen openly and sympathetically. The first two times we met, David didn't say a word. He sat there, only looking up to look at the children's drawings on the wall behind me. I suggested we play a game of chess. He nodded. After that he played chess with me every Wednesday afternoon — in complete silence and without looking at me. It's not easy to cheat in chess, but I admit I made sure David won once or twice. Usually, he arrived earlier than agreed, took the chess board and pieces from the shelf and began setting them up before I even got a chance to sit down. It seemed as if he enjoyed my company. But why did he never look at me? "Perhaps he simply needs someone to share his pain with," I thought. "Perhaps he senses that I respect his suffering." Some months later, when we were playing chess, he looked up at me suddenly. "It's your turn," he said. After that day, David started talking. He got friends in school and joined a bicycle club. He wrote to me a few times about his biking with some friends, and about his plan to get into university. Now he had really started to live his own life. Maybe I gave David something. But I also learned that one — without any words — can reach out to another person. All it takes is a hug, a shoulder to cry on, a friendly touch, and an ear that listens.

questions.text: When he first met the author, David ______.
options: A. felt a little excited
B. walked energetically
C. looked a little nervous
D. showed up with his teacher
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'He kept walking up and down restlessly, his face pale, and his hands shaking slightly.'可知，David第一次见作者时不安地走来走去，脸色苍白，手微微颤抖，即看起来有点紧张。A有点兴奋错误；B精力充沛地走错误，是restlessly不安地；D和老师一起来错误，是班主任推荐他来的。

questions.text: As a psychologist, the author ______.
options: A. was ready to listen to David
B. was skeptical about psychology
C. was able to describe David's problem
D. was sure of handling David's problem
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'Sometimes the best thing one can do is to listen openly and sympathetically.'以及作者实际行动（默默陪David下棋）可知，作为心理学家，作者准备好倾听David。B怀疑心理学错误；C能够描述David的问题错误，作者说有些问题心理学没有答案、无法用语言描述；D确信能处理David的问题错误，作者一开始问'How could I help him?'。

questions.text: David enjoyed being with the author because he ________.
options: A. wanted to ask the author for advice
B. needed to share sorrow with the author
C. liked the children's drawings in the office
D. beat the author many times in the chess game
questions.explanation: 根据第五段作者的想法'Perhaps he simply needs someone to share his pain with'可知，David喜欢和作者在一起是因为他需要有人分担他的悲伤/痛苦。A想向作者征求建议错误，他一直不说话；C喜欢办公室里的儿童画错误，那只是他看的东西；D下棋赢了作者很多次错误，作者故意让他赢一两次。

questions.text: What can be inferred about David?
options: A. He recovered after months of treatment.
B. He liked biking before he lost his family.
C. He went into university soon after starting to talk.
D. He got friends in school before he met the author.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段'After that day, David started talking. He got friends in school and joined a bicycle club... Now he had really started to live his own life.'可推知，经过几个月的治疗后David恢复了。B失去家人前喜欢骑自行车无依据；C开始说话后不久上大学错误，只是计划上大学；D遇见作者前在学校有朋友错误，他之前拒绝和别人说话。

questions.text: What made David change?
options: A. His teacher's help.
B. The author's friendship.
C. His exchange of letters with the author.
D. The author's silent communication with him.
questions.explanation: 根据全文，作者通过默默陪伴David下棋、不说话、倾听，几个月后David终于开口。最后一段作者总结'one — without any words — can reach out to another person'，说明是作者与David的无声交流改变了他。A老师的帮助只是推荐；B作者的友谊过于笼统，核心是无声的陪伴；C与作者通信错误，是David恢复后才写信。

items.title: 2013 广东 阅读D
items.passage: While Jennifer was at home taking an online exam for her business law class, a monitor a few hundred miles away was watching her every move. Using a web camera equipped in Jennifer's Los Angeles apartment, the monitor in Phoenix tracked how frequently her eyes moved from the computer screen and listened for the secret sounds of a possible helper in the room. Her Internet access was locked — remotely — to prevent Internet searches, and her typing style was analyzed to make sure she was who she said she was: Did she enter her student number at the same speed as she had in the past? Or was she slowing down? In the battle against cheating, this is the cutting edge and a key to encourage honesty in the booming field of online education. The technology gives trust to the entire system, to the institution and to online education in general. Only with solid measures against cheating, experts say, can Internet universities show that their exams and diplomas are valid — that students haven't just searched the Internet to get the right answers. Although online classes have existed for more than a decade, the concern over cheating has become sharper in the last year with the growth of "open online courses." Private colleges, public universities and corporations are jumping into the online education field, spending millions of dollars to attract potential students, while also taking steps to help guarantee honesty at a distance. Aside from the web cameras, a number of other high-tech methods are becoming increasingly popular. Among them are programs that check students' identities using personal information, such as the telephone number they once used. Other programs can produce unique exams by drawing on a large list of questions and can recognize possible cheaters by analyzing whether difficult test questions are answered at the same speed as easy ones. As in many university classes, term papers are scanned against some large Internet data banks for cheating.

questions.text: Why was Jennifer watched in an online exam?
options: A. To correct her typing mistakes.
B. To find her secrets in the room.
C. To prevent her from slowing down.
D. To keep her from dishonest behaviors.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'In the battle against cheating, this is the cutting edge and a key to encourage honesty'可知，监控Jennifer是为了防止作弊，即防止她的不诚实行为。A纠正打字错误错误；B找她房间里的秘密错误，是监听是否有帮手；C防止她放慢速度错误，分析打字速度是为了验证身份。

questions.text: The underlined expression "cutting edge" in Paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: A. advanced technique
B. sharpening tool
C. effective rule
D. dividing line
questions.explanation: 根据第三段上下文，这种通过网络摄像头、远程锁定、打字分析等高科技手段防止作弊的方法是'in the battle against cheating'中的cutting edge，结合后文'a key to encourage honesty'可推知，cutting edge意为'先进技术、前沿手段'。B磨刀工具是字面意思；C有效规则不准确，这是技术手段不是规则；D分界线不符合语境。

questions.text: For Internet universities, exams and diplomas will be valid if _____.
options: A. they can attract potential students
B. they can defeat academic cheating
C. they offer students online help
D. they offer many online courses
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'Only with solid measures against cheating, experts say, can Internet universities show that their exams and diplomas are valid'可知，只有采取有力措施防止作弊（即战胜学术作弊），网络大学的考试和文凭才有效。A吸引潜在学生、C提供在线帮助、D提供许多在线课程均不是文凭有效的条件。

questions.text: Some programs can find out possible cheaters by _____.
options: A. checking the question answering speed
B. producing a large number of questions
C. scanning the Internet test questions
D. giving difficult test questions
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'can recognize possible cheaters by analyzing whether difficult test questions are answered at the same speed as easy ones'可知，一些程序通过分析难题和容易题的答题速度是否相同来识别可能的作弊者，即检查答题速度。B生成大量题目是生成独特试卷的方式；C扫描互联网测试题目错误，是扫描论文；D给出难题不是识别作弊的方式。

questions.text: Which of the following is the best title of this passage?
options: A. The Advantages of Online Exams
B. The High-tech Methods in Online Courses
C. The Fight against Cheating in Online Education
D. The War against the Booming of Online Education
questions.explanation: 全文围绕在线教育中的反作弊展开：以Jennifer考试被监控为例，介绍了网络摄像头、身份验证、答题速度分析、论文扫描等多种防止作弊的高科技手段，核心是在线教育中的反作弊斗争。A在线考试的优点偏离主题；B在线课程中的高科技方法过于宽泛，核心是反作弊；D反对在线教育蓬勃发展错误，在线教育是在发展的。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读A
items.passage: Some people will do just about anything to save money. And I am one of them. Take my family's last vacation. It was my six-year-old son's winter break from school, and we were heading home from Fort Lauderdale after a weeklong trip. The flight was overbooked, and Delta, the airline, offered us $400 per person in credits to give up our seats and leave the next day. I had meetings in New York, so I had to get back. But that didn't mean my husband and my son couldn't stay. I took my nine-month-old and took off for home. The next day my husband and son were offered more credits to take an even later flight. Yes, I encouraged — okay, ordered — them to wait it out at the airport, to "earn" more Delta Dollars. Our total take: $1,600. Not bad, huh? Now some people may think I'm a bad mother and not such a great wife either. But as a big-time bargain hunter, I know the value of a dollar. And these days, a good deal is something few of us can afford to pass up. I've made a living looking for the best deals and exposing the worst tricks. I have been the consumer reporter of NBC's Today show for over a decade. I have written a couple of books including one titled Tricks of the Trade: A Consumer Survival Guide. And I really do what I believe in. I tell you this because there is no shame in getting your money's worth. I'm also tightfisted when it comes to shoes, clothes for my children, and expensive restaurants. But I wouldn't hesitate to spend on a good haircut. It keeps its shape longer, and it's the first thing people notice. And I will also spend on a classic piece of furniture. Quality lasts.

questions.text: Why did Delta give the author's family credits?
options: A. They took a later flight.
B. They had early bookings.
C. Their flight had been delayed.
D. Their flight had been cancelled.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段The flight was overbooked, and Delta, the airline, offered us $400 per person in credits to give up our seats and leave the next day可知，达美航空公司给作者一家积分是因为他们放弃了座位，乘坐了更晚的航班。B他们提前预订错误；C他们的航班延误了错误；D他们的航班取消了错误。

questions.text: What can we learn about the author?
options: A. She rarely misses a good deal.
B. She seldom makes a compromise.
C. She is very strict with her children.
D. She is interested in cheap products.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段But as a big-time bargain hunter, I know the value of a dollar. And these days, a good deal is something few of us can afford to pass up可知，作者是一个一流的杀价者，知道一美元的价值，很少有人能拒绝一笔好交易，所以作者很少错过好交易。B她很少妥协错误；C她对孩子很严格错误；D她对便宜产品感兴趣不准确，她是明智地花钱，不是只对便宜产品感兴趣。

questions.text: What does the author do?
options: A. She's a teacher.
B. She's a housewife.
C. She's a media person.
D. She's a businesswoman.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段I have been the consumer reporter of NBC's Today show for over a decade可知，作者是NBC《今日秀》的消费者记者，即媒体人。A教师错误；B家庭主妇错误；D女商人错误。

questions.text: What does the author want to tell us?
options: A. How to expose bad tricks.
B. How to reserve airline seats.
C. How to spend money wisely.
D. How to make a business deal.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段I tell you this because there is no shame in getting your money's worth和But I wouldn't hesitate to spend on a good haircut... And I will also spend on a classic piece of furniture. Quality lasts可知，作者想告诉我们如何明智地花钱——该省的省，该花的花，让钱花得值。A如何揭露坏伎俩只是部分内容；B如何预订机票座位错误；D如何做商业交易错误。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读B
items.passage: The baby is just one day old and has not yet left hospital. She is quiet but alert. Twenty centimeters from her face researchers have placed a white card with two black spots on it. She stares at it carefully. A researcher removes the card and replaces it by another, this time with the spots differently spaced. As the cards change from one to the other, her gaze starts to lose its focus — until a third, with three black spots, is presented. Her gaze returns; she looks at it for twice as long as she did at the previous card. Can she tell that the number two is different from three, just 24 hours after coming into the world? Or do newborns simply prefer more to fewer? The same experiment, but with three spots shown before two, shows the same return of interest when the number of spots changes. Perhaps it is just the newness? When slightly older babies were shown cards with pictures of objects (a comb, a key, an orange and so on), changing the number of objects had an effect separate from changing the objects themselves. Could it be the pattern that two things make, as opposed to three? No again. Babies paid more attention to squares moving randomly on a screen when their number changed from two to three, or three to two. The effect even crosses between senses. Babies who were repeatedly shown two spots became more excited when they then heard three drumbeats than when they heard just two; likewise when the researchers started with drumbeats and moved to spots.

questions.text: The experiment described in Paragraph 1 is related to the baby's _________.
options: A. sense of hearing
B. sense of sight
C. sense of touch
D. sense of smell
questions.explanation: 根据第一段She stares at it carefully和her gaze starts to lose its focus可知，实验中婴儿盯着卡片看，凝视随着卡片变化而变化，所以这个实验与婴儿的视觉有关。A听觉是第二段的实验；C触觉错误；D嗅觉错误。

questions.text: Babies are sensitive to the change in _________.
options: A. the size of cards
B. the colour of pictures
C. the shape of patterns
D. the number of objects
questions.explanation: 根据第一段As the cards change from one to the other, her gaze starts to lose its focus — until a third, with three black spots, is presented. Her gaze returns和第二段changing the number of objects had an effect separate from changing the objects themselves可知，婴儿对物体数量的变化敏感。A卡片大小错误；B图片颜色错误；C图案形状错误。

questions.text: Why did the researchers test the babies with drumbeats?
options: A. To reduce the difficulty of the experiment.
B. To see how babies recognize sounds.
C. To carry their experiment further.
D. To keep the babies' interest.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段The effect even crosses between senses. Babies who were repeatedly shown two spots became more excited when they then heard three drumbeats than when they heard just two可知，研究人员用鼓声测试婴儿是为了进一步研究婴儿对数量变化的敏感性，验证这种效果是否跨感官。A减少实验难度错误；B看婴儿如何识别声音不是主要目的；D保持婴儿兴趣错误。

questions.text: Where does this text probably come from?
options: A. Science fiction.
B. Children's literature.
C. An advertisement.
D. A science report.
questions.explanation: 本文提到了experiment和researchers，是研究人员做了一个实验来检验婴儿对数量变化的敏感性，属于科学研究报告。A科幻小说错误；B儿童文学错误；C广告错误。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读C
items.passage: It happened to me recently. I was telling someone how much I had enjoyed reading Barack Obama's Dreams From My Father and how it had changed my views of our President. A friend I was talking to agreed with me that it was, in his words, "a brilliantly written book". However, he then went on to talk about Mr. Obama in a way which suggested he had no idea of his background at all. I sensed that I was talking to a book liar. And it seems that my friend is not the only one. Approximately two thirds of people have lied about reading a book which they haven't. In the World Book Day's "Report on Guilty Secrets", Dreams From My Father is at number 9. The report lists ten books, and various authors, which people have lied about reading, and as I'm not one to lie too often (I'd hate to be caught out), I'll admit here and now that I haven't read the entire top ten. But I am pleased to say that, unlike 42 percent of people, I have read the book at number one, George Orwell's 1984. I think it's really brilliant. The World Book Day report also has some other interesting information in it. It says that many people lie about having read Jane Austen, Charles Dickens, Fyodor Dostoevsky (I haven't read him, but haven't lied about it either) and Herman Melville. Asked why they lied, the most common reason was to "impress" someone they were speaking to. This could be tricky if the conversation became more in-depth! But when asked which authors they actually enjoy, people named J.K. Rowling, John Grisham, Sophie Kinsella (ah, the big sellers, in other words). Forty-two percent of people asked admitted they turned to the back of the book to read the end before finishing the story (I'll come clean: I do this and am astonished that 58 percent said they had never done so).

questions.text: How did the author find his friend a book liar?
options: A. By judging his manner of speaking.
B. By looking into his background.
C. By mentioning a famous name.
D. By discussing the book itself.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段However, he then went on to talk about Mr. Obama in a way which suggested he had no idea of his background at all可知，作者发现朋友撒谎是因为朋友在谈论这本书时暴露了他对奥巴马背景的无知，即通过讨论这本书本身发现的。A通过判断他的说话方式错误；B通过调查他的背景错误；C通过提到一个著名的名字错误。

questions.text: Which of the following is a "guilty secret" according to the World Book Day report?
options: A. Charles Dickens is very low on the top-ten list.
B. 42% of people pretended to have read 1984.
C. The author admitted having read 9 books.
D. Dreams From My Father is hardly read.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段But I am pleased to say that, unlike 42 percent of people, I have read the book at number one, George Orwell's 1984可知，作者不像42%的人，她读过排名第一的《1984》，由此可推断出42%的人假装读过《1984》。A狄更斯在前十名中排名很低错误；C作者承认读过9本书错误；D《我父亲的梦想》几乎没人读错误。

questions.text: By lying about reading, a person hopes to _________.
options: A. control the conversation
B. appear knowledgeable
C. learn about the book
D. make more friends
questions.explanation: 根据第四段Asked why they lied, the most common reason was to "impress" someone they were speaking to可知，人们撒谎说读过书的最常见原因是想给说话的对象留下深刻印象，即显得有知识。A控制对话错误；C了解这本书错误；D交更多朋友不是直接原因。

questions.text: What is the author's attitude to 58% of readers?
options: A. Favorable
B. Uncaring
C. Doubtful
D. Friendly
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段I'll come clean: I do this and am astonished that 58 percent said they had never done so可知，作者坦白自己也会在读完故事之前翻到后面看结局，并且很惊讶58%的人说他们从未这样做过，由此可推断出作者对这58%的人表示怀疑。A赞成的错误；B不关心的错误；D友好的错误。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D
items.passage: The National Gallery Description: The National Gallery is the British national art museum built on the north side of Trafalgar Square in London. It houses a diverse collection of more than 2,300 examples of European art ranging from 13th-century religious paintings to more modern ones by Renoir and Van Gogh. The older collections of the gallery are reached through the main entrance while the more modern works in the East Wing are most easily reached from Trafalgar Square by a ground floor entrance. Layout: The modern Sainsbury Wing on the western side of the building houses 13th-to 15th-century paintings, and artists include Duccio, Uccello, Van Eyck, Lippi, Mantegna, Botticelli and Memling. The main West Wing houses 16th-century paintings, and artists include Leonardo da Vinci, Cranach, Michelangelo, Raphael, Bruegel, Bronzino, Titian and Veronese. The North Wing houses 17th-century paintings, and artists include Caravaggio, Rubens, Poussin, Van Dyck, Velazquez, Claude and Vermeer. The East Wing houses 18th-to early 20th-century paintings, and artists include Canaletto, Goya, Turner, Constable, Renoir and Van Gogh. Opening Hours: The Gallery is open every day from 10am to 6pm (Fridays 10am to 9pm) and is free, but charges apply to some special exhibitions. Getting There: Nearest underground stations: Charing Cross (2-minute walk), Leicester Square (3-minute walk), Embankment (7-minute walk), and Piccadilly Circus (8-minute walk).

questions.text: In which century's collection can you see religious paintings?
options: A. The 13th.
B. The 17th.
C. The 18th.
