D. The 20th.
questions.explanation: 根据Description部分It houses a diverse collection of more than 2,300 examples of European art ranging from 13th-century religious paintings to more modern ones by Renoir and Van Gogh可知，13世纪的藏品中有宗教绘画。B17世纪错误；C18世纪错误；D20世纪错误。

questions.text: Where are Leonardo da Vinci's works shown?
options: A. In the East Wing.
B. In the main West Wing.
C. In the Sainsbury Wing.
D. In the North Wing.
questions.explanation: 根据Layout部分The main West Wing houses 16th-century paintings, and artists include Leonardo da Vinci可知，达·芬奇的作品在主西翼展出。A东翼错误；C塞恩斯伯里翼楼错误；D北翼错误。

questions.text: Which underground station is closest to the National Gallery?
options: A. Piccadilly Circus.
B. Leicester Square.
C. Embankment.
D. Charing Cross.
questions.explanation: 根据Getting There部分Nearest underground stations: Charing Cross (2-minute walk), Leicester Square (3-minute walk), Embankment (7-minute walk), and Piccadilly Circus (8-minute walk)可知，查令十字站步行只需2分钟，是最近的地铁站。A皮卡迪利 Circus步行8分钟错误；B莱斯特广场步行3分钟错误；C堤岸步行7分钟错误。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读A
items.passage: Doctors are known to be terrible pilots. They don't listen because they already know it all. I was lucky: I became a pilot in 1970, almost ten years before I graduated from medical school. I didn't realize then, but becoming a pilot makes me a better surgeon. I loved flying. As I flew bigger, faster planes, and in worse weather, I learned about crew resource management (机组资源管理), or CRM, a new idea to make flying safer. It means that crew members should listen and speak up for a good result, regardless of positions. I first read about CRM in 1980. Not long after that, an attending doctor and I were flying in bad weather. The controller had us turn too late to get our landing ready. The attending doctor was flying; I was safety pilot. He was so busy because of the bad turn, he had forgotten to put the landing gear (起落架) down. He was a better pilot — and my boss — so it felt unusual to speak up. But I had to: Our lives were in danger. I put aside my uneasiness and said, "We need to put the landing gear down now!" That was my first real lesson in the power of CRM, and I've used it in the operating room ever since. CRM requires that the pilot/surgeon encourage others to speak up. It further requires that when opinions are from the opposite, the doctor doesn't overreact, which might prevent fellow doctors from voicing opinions again. So when I'm in the operating room, I ask for ideas and help from others. Sometimes they're not willing to speak up. But I hope that if I continue to encourage them, someday someone will keep me from "landing gear up".

questions.text: What does the author say about doctors in general?
options: A. They like flying by themselves.
B. They are unwilling to take advice.
C. They pretend to be good pilots.
D. They are quick learners of CRM.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段第一句'Doctors are known to be terrible pilots. They don't listen because they already know it all.'可知，作者认为医生普遍不喜欢接受意见，因为他们自以为什么都懂。A选项喜欢独自飞行、C选项假装是好飞行员、D选项学习CRM很快均与原文不符。

questions.text: The author deepened his understanding of the power of CRM when_______.
options: A. he saved the plane by speaking up
B. he was in charge of a flying task
C. his boss landed the plane too late
D. his boss operated on a patient
questions.explanation: 根据第二段最后一句'That was my first real lesson in the power of CRM'可知，作者在那次飞行中勇于向上级提出放下起落架的建议，从而挽救了飞机，这是他第一次真正体会到CRM的力量。B选项负责飞行任务、C选项老板着陆太晚、D选项老板给病人做手术均不符合原文。

questions.text: In the last paragraph "landing gear up" probably means ______.
options: A. following flying requirements
B. overreacting to different opinions
C. listening to what fellow doctors say
D. making a mistake that may cost lives
questions.explanation: 根据第二段中作者喊出'We need to put the landing gear down now!'避免了空难，而最后一段用相反的'landing gear up'（未放下起落架）比喻可能付出生命代价的错误。作者希望有人能及时指出他的错误，避免'起落架未放下'式的悲剧。A遵循飞行要求、B对不同意见反应过度、C倾听同事意见均不符合比喻含义。

questions.text: Which of the following can be the best title for the text?
options: A. CRM: A New Way to Make Flying Safe
B. Flying Makes Me a Better Doctor
C. The Making of a Good Pilot
D. A Pilot-Turned Doctor
questions.explanation: 文章首段点明'becoming a pilot makes me a better surgeon'，全文围绕作者从飞行中学到CRM理念并运用于医疗工作展开，核心是飞行经历如何让他成为更好的医生。A选项仅强调飞行安全，偏离医疗主题；C选项讲如何成为好飞行员，不是文章重点；D选项仅描述身份转变，未体现核心主旨。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读B
items.passage: In 1947 a group of famous people from the art world headed by an Austrian conductor decided to hold an international festival of music, dance and theatre in Edinburgh. The idea was to reunite Europe after the Second World War. At the same time, the "Fringe" appeared as a challenge to the official festival. Eight theatre groups turned up uninvited in 1947, in the belief that everyone should have the right to perform, and they did so in a public house disused for years. Soon, groups of students firstly from Edinburgh University, and later from the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Durham and Birmingham were making the journey to the Scottish capital each summer to perform theatre by little-known writers of plays in small church halls to the people of Edinburgh. Today the "Fringe", once less recognized, has far outgrown the festival with around 1,500 performances of theatre, music and dance on every one of the 21 days it lasts. And yet as early as 1959, with only 19 theatre groups performing, some said it was getting too big. A paid administrator was first employed only in 1971, and today there are eight administrators working all year round and the number rises to 150 during August itself. In 2004 there were 200 places housing 1,695 shows by over 600 different groups from 50 different countries. More than 1.25 million tickets were sold.

questions.text: What was the purpose of Edinburgh Festival at the beginning?
options: A. To bring Europe together again.
B. To honor heroes of World War II.
C. To introduce young theatre groups.
D. To attract great artists from Europe.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段最后一句'The idea was to reunite Europe after the Second World War.'可知，创办爱丁堡艺术节的初衷是在二战后重新团结欧洲。B纪念二战英雄、C介绍年轻剧团、D吸引欧洲伟大艺术家均不是创办初衷。

questions.text: Why did some uninvited theatre groups come to Edinburgh in 1947?
options: A. They owned a public house there.
B. They came to take up a challenge.
C. They thought they were also famous.
D. They wanted to take part in the festival.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'Eight theatre groups turned up uninvited in 1947, in the belief that everyone should have the right to perform'可知，这些不请自来的剧团认为每个人都应有表演的权利，即他们想参加这个节日。A选项拥有酒馆、B选项来接受挑战、C选项认为自己也很有名均不符合原文。

questions.text: Who joined the "Fringe" after it appeared?
options: A. Popular writers.
B. University students.
C. Artists from around the world.
D. Performers of music and dance.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'Soon, groups of students firstly from Edinburgh University, and later from the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Durham and Birmingham were making the journey...'可知，边缘艺术节出现后，首先是爱丁堡大学的学生，后来牛津、剑桥等大学的学生也加入了。A受欢迎作家、C世界各地艺术家、D音乐舞蹈表演者均不是最早加入的群体。

questions.text: We may learn from the text that Edinburgh Festival________.
options: A. has become a non-official event
B. has gone beyond an art festival
C. gives shows all year round
D. keeps growing rapidly
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段数据：从1971年才有第一位带薪管理员到如今8名全年管理员、8月增至150人；2004年有200个场地、1695场演出、600多个团体来自50个国家、售出125万多张票，这些数据表明爱丁堡艺术节一直在快速发展。A成为非官方活动错误，官方和边缘并存；B超越艺术节范畴无依据；C全年演出错误，主要在8月。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C
items.passage: Given that many people's moods (情绪) are regulated by the chemical action of chocolate, it was probably only a matter of time before somebody made the chocolate shop similar to a drugstore of Chinese medicine. Looking like a setting from the film Charlie & the Chocolate Factory, Singapore's Chocolate Research Facility (CRF) has over 100 varieties of chocolates. Its founder is Chris Lee who grew up at his parents' corner store with one hand almost always in the jar of sweets. If the CRF seems to be a smart idea, that's because Lee is not merely a seasoned salesperson but also head of a marketing department that has business relations with big names such as Levi's and Sony. That idea surely results in the imagination at work when it comes to making different flavored (味道) chocolates. The CRF's produce is "green", made within the country and divided into 10 lines, with the Alcohol Series being the most popular. The Exotic Series — with Sichuan pepper, red bean (豆), cheese and other flavors — also does well and is fun to taste. And for chocolate snobs, who think that they have a better knowledge of chocolate than others, the Connoisseur Series uses cocoa beans from Togo, Cuba, Venezuela, and Ghana, among others.

questions.text: What is good about chocolate?
options: A. It serves as a suitable gift.
B. It works as an effective medicine.
C. It helps improve the state of mind.
D. It strengthens business relations.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段第一句'many people's moods are regulated by the chemical action of chocolate'可知，巧克力的化学作用能调节人的情绪，即有助于改善心理状态。A适合做礼物无原文依据；B是有效药物错误，原文只是说类似中药铺，并非真的是药；D加强商业关系不是巧克力本身的好处。

questions.text: Why is Chris Lee able to develop his idea of the CRF?
options: A. He knows the importance of research.
B. He learns from shops of similar types.
C. He has the support of many big names.
D. He has a lot of marketing experience.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'Lee is not merely a seasoned salesperson but also head of a marketing department that has business relations with big names such as Levi's and Sony'可知，Lee不仅是经验丰富的销售员，还是市场部门主管，与大品牌有业务往来，由此可推知他有丰富的营销经验，这使他能够发展CRF的创意。A知道研究重要性、B从同类店铺学习均无依据；C有大品牌支持错误，是有业务往来而非支持。

questions.text: Which line of the CRF produce sells best?
options: A. The Connoisseur Series.
B. The Exotic Series.
C. The Alcohol Series.
D. The Sichuan Series.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'with the Alcohol Series being the most popular'可知，酒心系列是最受欢迎的，即销量最好。A鉴赏家系列是面向行家的高端产品；B异国风味系列也卖得好但不是最受欢迎；D四川系列不存在，四川花椒只是异国系列中的一种口味。

questions.text: The words "chocolate snobs" in Paragraph 3 probably refer to people who ______.
options: A. are particular about chocolate
B. know little about cocoa beans
C. look down upon others
D. like to try new flavors
questions.explanation: 根据划线词后定语从句'who think that they have a better knowledge of chocolate than others'可知，chocolate snobs指那些自认为比别人更懂巧克力的人，即对巧克力很挑剔、有讲究的人。B对可可豆知之甚少与原文相反；C看不起别人过于贬义，原文只是说自认为更懂；D喜欢尝试新口味不是snob的含义。

items.title: 2013 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读D
items.passage: Low-Cost Gifts for Mother's Day Gift No. 1 Offer to be your mother's health friend. Promise to be there for any and all doctor's visits whether a disease or a regular medical check-up. Most mothers always say "no need," but another set of eyes and ears is always a good idea at a doctor's visit. The best part? This one is free. Gift No. 2 Help your mother organize all of her medical records, which include the test results and medical information. Put them all in one place. Be sure to make a list of all of her medicines and what times she takes them. "Having all this information in one place could end up saving your mother's life," Dr. Marie Savard said. Gift No. 3 Enough sleep is connected to general health conditions. "Buy your mother cotton sheets and comfortable pillows to encourage better sleep," Savard said. "We know that good sleep is very important to our health." Gift No. 4 Some gift companies such as Presents for Purpose allow you to pay it forward this Mother's Day by picking gifts in which 10 percent of the price you pay goes to a charity (慈善机构). Gift givers can choose from a wide variety of useful but inexpensive things — many of which are "green" — and then choose a meaningful charity from a list. When your mother gets the gift, she will be told that she has helped the chosen charity.

questions.text: What are you advised to do for your mother at doctor's visits?
options: A. Take notes.
B. Be with her.
C. Buy medicine.
D. Give her gifts.
questions.explanation: 根据Gift No.1中'Promise to be there for any and all doctor's visits whether a disease or a regular medical check-up'可知，建议在母亲看医生时陪伴她。'be there'与'be with her'同义。A记笔记、C买药、D送礼物均不是该建议的内容。

questions.text: Where can you find a gift idea to improve your mother's sleep?
options: A. In Gift No. 1.
B. In Gift No. 2.
C. In Gift No. 3.
D. In Gift No. 4.
questions.explanation: 根据Gift No.3中'Buy your mother cotton sheets and comfortable pillows to encourage better sleep'可知，第三款礼物建议购买棉质床单和舒适枕头来改善母亲睡眠。A是陪伴看医生、B是整理医疗记录、D是公益礼品，均与改善睡眠无关。

questions.text: Buying gifts from Presents for Purpose allows mothers to_______.
options: A. enjoy good sleep
B. be well-organized
C. get extra support
D. give others help
questions.explanation: 根据Gift No.4最后一句'When your mother gets the gift, she will be told that she has helped the chosen charity.'可知，从Presents for Purpose购买礼物时，售价的10%会捐给慈善机构，母亲收到礼物时会被告知她帮助了所选慈善机构，即给予了他人帮助。A享受好睡眠、B有条理、C获得额外支持均不符合。

items.title: 2013 江苏 阅读A
items.passage: Canada's Wonderland Guest Services Front Gate Guest Services can help you with anything from finding out what time your favourite show starts to purchasing tickets. The Guest Services location inside Front Gate also serves as a lost and found, children's check-in area and a place to rent wheelchairs and strollers. Food & Drink Options Shops can be found throughout the park. Picnics and coolers are welcome at the park, but alcohol and glass bottles are not permitted. Outside food and drink are not permitted in the Water Park. ATMs ATMs are located just inside the Park beside Stroller, Locker and Wheelchair Rentals at the Front Gate, as well as just outside KidZville, and beside Guest Services in the Water Park. Pet Care A pet care facility is available outside the Front Gate for dogs and cats. Pets must be kept on a leash at all times. Pets are not permitted in the park, with the exception of service animals. First Aid If you need first aid, tell any park employee who will call First Aid and have them come to your location. First Aid is located beside Thunder Run. Stroller, Locker and Wheelchair Rentals Strollers, wheelchairs and lockers may be rented at the Front Gate. A valid photo ID is required. Smoking Policy Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the park, except in designated areas. Designated smoking areas are located near the Front Gate, behind the International Showplace and in the Water Park.

questions.text: The leaflet is to inform visitors of the Park's _________.
options: A. advanced management
B. thrill performances
C. entertainment facilities
D. thoughtful services
questions.explanation: 根据文章中的关键信息Guest Services、Food & Drink Options、ATMs、Pet Care、First Aid、Stroller, Locker and Wheelchair Rentals、Smoking Policy可知，这个宣传单的目的是告知游客们有关加拿大奇幻乐园提供的体贴周到的服务信息。A先进管理错误；B惊险表演错误；C娱乐设施错误。

questions.text: A visitor to the Park can _________.
options: A. rent a stroller outside Front Gate
B. ask for first aid by Thunder Run
C. smoke in the Water Park
D. leave his pet at KidZville
questions.explanation: 根据First Aid部分First Aid is located beside Thunder Run可知，急救站位于Thunder Run旁边，游客可以在Thunder Run旁边寻求急救。A在前门外租婴儿车错误，是在前门内租；C在水上乐园吸烟错误，只有指定区域可以吸烟；D把宠物留在KidZville错误，宠物照护设施在前门外。

items.title: 2013 江苏 阅读B
items.passage: We've considered several ways of paying to cut in line: hiring line standers, buying tickets from scalpers, or purchasing line-cutting privileges directly from, say, an airline or an amusement park. Each of these deals replaces the morals of the queue (waiting your turn) with the morals of the market (paying a price for faster service). Markets and queues — paying and waiting — are two different ways of allocating things, and each is appropriate to different activities. The morals of the queue, "First come, first served," have an egalitarian appeal. They tell us to ignore privilege, power, and deep pockets. The principle seems right on playgrounds and at bus stops. But the morals of the queue do not govern all occasions. If I put my house up for sale, I have no duty to accept the first offer that comes along, simply because it's the first. Selling my house and waiting for a bus are different activities, properly governed by different standards. Sometimes standards change, and it is unclear which principle should apply. Think of the recorded message you hear, played over and over, as you wait on hold when calling your bank: "Your call will be answered in the order in which it was received." This is essential for the morals of the queue. It's as if the company is trying to ease our impatience with fairness. But don't take the recorded message too seriously. Today, some people's calls are answered faster than others. Call center technology enables companies to "score" incoming calls and to give faster service to those that come from rich places. You might call this telephonic queue jumping. Of course, markets and queues are not the only ways of allocating things. Some goods we distribute by merit, others by need, still others by chance. However, the tendency of markets to replace queues, and other non-market ways of allocating goods is so common in modern life that we scarcely notice it anymore. It is striking that most of the paid queue-jumping schemes we've considered — at airports and amusement parks, in call centers, doctors' offices, and national parks — are recent developments, scarcely imaginable three decades ago. The disappearance of the queues in these places may seem an unusual concern, but these are not the only places that markets have entered.

questions.text: According to the author, which of the following seems governed by the principle "First come, first served"?
options: A. Taking buses.
B. Buying houses.
C. Flying with an airline.
D. Visiting amusement parks.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段The principle seems right on playgrounds and at bus stops. Selling my house and waiting for a bus are different activities, properly governed by different standards可知，等公交车受"先到先得"原则支配，而卖房子则不同。B买房错误；C乘飞机错误；D参观游乐园错误。

questions.text: The example of the recorded message in Paragraphs 4 and 5 illustrates _________.
options: A. the necessity of patience in queuing
B. the advantage of modern technology
C. the uncertainty of allocation principle
D. the fairness of telephonic services
questions.explanation: 根据第四段Sometimes standards change, and it is unclear which principle should apply和第五段But don't take the recorded message too seriously. Today, some people's calls are answered faster than others可知，录音信息的例子说明了分配原则的不确定性——表面上说按顺序接听，但实际上来自富裕地区的电话接听得更快。A排队时耐心的必要性错误；B现代技术的优势错误；D电话服务的公平性错误，文章说实际上并不公平。

questions.text: The passage is meant to _________.
options: A. justify paying for faster services
B. discuss the morals of allocating things
C. analyze the reason for standing in line
D. criticize the behavior of queue jumping
questions.explanation: 根据第六段Of course, markets and queues are not the only ways of allocating things和全文内容可知，本文主要探讨了分配事物的道德问题——市场道德和队列道德各自适用于不同场合，以及市场取代队列的趋势。A为更快的服务付费辩护错误；C分析排队的原因错误；D批评插队行为错误，文章是客观探讨，不是单纯批评。

items.title: 2013 江苏 阅读C
items.passage: If a diver surfaces too quickly, he may suffer the bends. Nitrogen dissolved in his blood is suddenly liberated by the reduction of pressure. The consequence, if the bubbles accumulate in a joint, is sharp pain and a bent body — thus the name. If the bubbles form in his lungs or his brain, the consequence can be death. Other air-breathing animals also suffer this decompression sickness if they surface too fast: whales, for example. And so, long ago, did ichthyosaurs. That these ancient sea animals got the bends can be seen from their bones. If bubbles of nitrogen form inside the bone they can cut off its blood supply. This kills the cells in the bone, and consequently weakens it, sometimes to the point of collapse. Fossil bones that have caved in on themselves are thus a sign that the animal once had the bends. Bruce Rothschild of the University of Kansas knew all this when he began a study of ichthyosaur bones to find out how widespread the problem was in the past. What he particularly wanted to investigate was how ichthyosaurs adapted to the problem of decompression over the 150 million years. To this end, he and his colleagues traveled the world's natural-history museums, looking at hundreds of ichthyosaurs from the Triassic period and from the later Jurassic and Cretaceous periods. When he started, he assumed that signs of the bends would be rarer in younger fossils, reflecting their gradual evolution of measures to deal with decompression. Instead, he was astonished to discover the opposite. More than 15% of Jurassic and Cretaceous ichthyosaurs had suffered the bends before they died, but not a single Triassic specimen showed evidence of that sort of injury. If ichthyosaurs did evolve an anti-decompression means, they clearly did so quickly — and, most strangely, they lost it afterwards. But that is not what Dr Rothschild thinks happened. He suspects it was evolution in other animals that caused the change. Whales that suffer the bends often do so because they have surfaced to escape a predator such as a large shark. One of the features of Jurassic oceans was an abundance of large sharks and crocodiles, both of which were fond of ichthyosaur lunches. Triassic oceans, by contrast, were mercifully shark- and crocodile-free. In the Triassic, then, ichthyosaurs were top of the food chain. In the Jurassic and Cretaceous, they were prey as well as predator — and often had to make a speedy exit as a result.

questions.text: Which of the following is a typical symptom of the bends?
options: A. A twisted body.
B. A gradual decrease in blood supply.
C. A sudden release of nitrogen in blood.
D. A drop in blood pressure.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段The consequence, if the bubbles accumulate in a joint, is sharp pain and a bent body — thus the name可知，减压病的典型症状是身体弯曲（bent body），即扭曲的身体。B血液供应逐渐减少错误；C血液中氮的突然释放是原因不是症状；D血压下降错误。

questions.text: The purpose of Rothschild's study is to see _________.
options: A. how often ichthyosaurs caught the bends
B. how ichthyosaurs adapted to decompression
C. why ichthyosaurs bent their bodies
D. when ichthyosaurs broke their bones
questions.explanation: 根据第三段What he particularly wanted to investigate was how ichthyosaurs adapted to the problem of decompression over the 150 million years可知，Rothschild研究的目的是了解鱼龙如何适应减压问题。A鱼龙多久患一次减压病不是主要目的；C鱼龙为什么弯曲身体错误；D鱼龙什么时候骨折错误。

questions.text: Rothschild's finding stated in Paragraph 4 _________.
options: A. confirmed his assumption
B. speeded up his research process
C. disagreed with his assumption
D. changed his research objectives
questions.explanation: 根据第四段he assumed that signs of the bends would be rarer in younger fossils和Instead, he was astonished to discover the opposite可知，他的假设是较年轻的化石中减压病迹象更罕见，但实际发现相反，即他的发现与假设不一致。A证实了他的假设错误；B加快了他的研究进程错误；D改变了他的研究目标错误。

questions.text: Rothschild might have concluded that ichthyosaurs _________.
options: A. failed to evolve an anti-decompression means
B. gradually developed measures against the bends
C. died out because of large sharks and crocodiles
D. evolved an anti-decompression means but soon lost it
questions.explanation: 根据第五段If ichthyosaurs did evolve an anti-decompression means... But that is not what Dr Rothschild thinks happened和第六段内容可知，Rothschild认为鱼龙没有进化出抗减压的方法，而是因为其他动物（鲨鱼和鳄鱼）的进化导致它们不得不快速浮出水面逃生，从而患减压病。B逐渐发展出对抗减压病的措施错误；C因大型鲨鱼和鳄鱼而灭绝错误，文章没说灭绝原因；D进化出抗减压方法但很快失去错误，这不是Rothschild的观点。

items.title: 2013 江苏 阅读D
items.passage: Mark Twain has been called the inventor of the American novel. And he surely deserves additional praise: the man who popularized the clever literary attack on racism. I say clever because anti-slavery fiction had been the important part of the literature in the years before the Civil War. H.B. Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin is only the most famous example. These early stories dealt directly with slavery. With minor exceptions, Twain planted his attacks on slavery and prejudice into tales that were on the surface about something else entirely. He drew his readers into the argument by drawing them into the story. Again and again, in the postwar years, Twain seemed forced to deal with the challenge of race. Consider the most controversial, at least today, of Twain's novels, Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. Only a few books have been kicked off the shelves as often as Huckleberry Finn, Twain's most widely read tale. Once upon a time, people hated the book because it struck them as rude. Twain himself wrote that those who banned the book considered the novel "trash and suitable only for the slums." More recently the book has been attacked because of the character Jim, the escaped slave, and many occurrences of the word nigger. (The term Nigger Jim, for which the novel is often severely criticized, never appears in it.) But the attacks were and are silly — and miss the point. The novel is strongly anti-slavery. Jim's search through the slave states for the family from whom he has been forcibly parted is heroic. As J. Chadwick has pointed out, the character of Jim was a first in American fiction — a recognition that the slave had two personalities, "the voice of survival within a white slave culture and the voice of the individual: Jim, the father and the man." There is much more. Twain's mystery novel Pudd'nhead Wilson stood as a challenge to the racial beliefs of even many of the liberals of his day. Written at a time when the accepted wisdom held Negroes to be inferior to whites, especially in intelligence, Twain's tale centered in part around two babies switched at birth. A slave gave birth to her master's baby and, for fear that the child should be sold South, switched him for the master's baby by his wife. The slave's light-skinned child was taken to be white and grew up with both the attitudes and the education of the slave-holding class. The master's wife's baby was taken for black and grew up with the attitudes and intonations of the slave. The point was difficult to miss: nurture, not nature, was the key to social status. The features of the black man that provided the stuff of prejudice — manner of speech, for example — were, to Twain, indicative of nothing other than the conditioning that slavery forced on its victims. Twain's racial tone was not perfect. One is left uneasy, for example, by the lengthy passage in his autobiography about how much he loved what were called "nigger shows" in his youth — mostly with white men performing in black-face — and his delight in getting his mother to laugh at them. Yet there is no reason to think Twain saw the shows as representing reality. His frequent attacks on slavery and prejudice suggest his keen awareness that they did not. Was Twain a racist? Asking the question in the 21st century is as wise as asking the same of Lincoln. If we read the words and attitudes of the past through the "wisdom" of the considered moral judgments of the present, we will find nothing but error. Lincoln, who believed the black man the inferior of the white, fought and won a war to free him. And Twain, raised in a slave state, briefly a soldier, and inventor of Jim, may have done more to anger the nation over racial injustice and awaken its collective conscience than any other novelist in the past century.

questions.text: How do Twain's novels on slavery differ from Stowe's?
options: A. Twain was more willing to deal with racism.
B. Twain's attack on racism was much less open.
C. Twain's themes seemed to agree with plots.
D. Twain was openly concerned with racism.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段These early stories dealt directly with slavery. With minor exceptions, Twain planted his attacks on slavery and prejudice into tales that were on the surface about something else entirely可知，斯托夫人等早期作家直接处理奴隶制，而吐温把对奴隶制和偏见的抨击植入表面上完全是关于其他事情的故事中，即吐温对种族主义的抨击不那么公开。A吐温更愿意处理种族主义错误；C吐温的主题似乎与情节一致错误；D吐温公开关注种族主义错误。

questions.text: Recent criticism of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn arose partly from its _________.
options: A. target readers at the bottom
B. anti-slavery attitude
C. rather impolite language
D. frequent use of "nigger"
questions.explanation: 根据第三段More recently the book has been attacked because of the character Jim, the escaped slave, and many occurrences of the word nigger可知，最近对《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的批评部分是因为多次使用"nigger"一词。A针对底层读者错误；B反奴隶制态度错误，这是优点不是批评原因；C相当不礼貌的语言是以前人们讨厌它的原因，不是最近的批评原因。

questions.text: What best proves Twain's anti-slavery stand according to the author?
options: A. Jim's search for his family was described in detail.
B. The slave's voice was first heard in American novels.
C. Jim grew up into a man and a father in the white culture.
D. Twain suspected that the slaves were less intelligent.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段the character of Jim was a first in American fiction — a recognition that the slave had two personalities, "the voice of survival within a white slave culture and the voice of the individual: Jim, the father and the man"可知，吉姆这个角色是美国小说中的第一个，承认奴隶有两种人格——在白人奴隶文化中生存的声音和个人的声音：吉姆，父亲和男人，这最能证明吐温的反奴隶制立场。A吉姆寻找家人被详细描述不是最有力的证据；B奴隶的声音在美国小说中首次被听到不准确；D吐温怀疑奴隶智力较低错误，这与反奴隶制立场相反。

questions.text: The story of two babies switched mainly indicates that _________.
options: A. slaves were forced to give up their babies to their masters
B. slaves' babies could pick up slave holders' way of speaking
C. blacks' social position was shaped by how they were brought up
D. blacks were born with certain features of prejudice
questions.explanation: 根据第六段The point was difficult to miss: nurture, not nature, was the key to social status可知，两个婴儿被调换的故事主要表明黑人的社会地位是由他们的成长方式决定的，而不是天生的。A奴隶被迫把孩子交给主人错误；B奴隶的孩子能学会奴隶主的说话方式是表面现象不是要点；D黑人生来就有某些偏见特征错误，文章说偏见特征是奴隶制强加的条件作用。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "they" in Paragraph 7 refer to?
options: A. The attacks.
B. Slavery and prejudice.
C. White men.
D. The shows.
questions.explanation: 根据第七段Yet there is no reason to think Twain saw the shows as representing reality. His frequent attacks on slavery and prejudice suggest his keen awareness that they did not可知，前一句说没有理由认为吐温把这些表演视为代表现实，后一句说他对奴隶制和偏见的频繁抨击表明他敏锐地意识到它们不是现实，所以they指代the shows（这些表演）。A攻击错误；B奴隶制和偏见错误；C白人错误。

questions.text: What does the author mainly argue for?
options: A. Twain had done more than his contemporary writers to attack racism.
B. Twain was an admirable figure comparable to Abraham Lincoln.
C. Twain's works had been banned on unreasonable grounds.
D. Twain's works should be read from a historical point of view.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段And Twain, raised in a slave state, briefly a soldier, and inventor of Jim, may have done more to anger the nation over racial injustice and awaken its collective conscience than any other novelist in the past century可知，作者主要论证的是吐温在抨击种族主义方面比他同时代的作家做得更多。B吐温是一个可与林肯相比的令人钦佩的人物只是类比不是主要论点；C吐温的作品因不合理的理由被禁是部分内容；D吐温的作品应该从历史角度阅读是建议不是主要论点。

items.title: 2013 江西 阅读A
items.passage: The light from the campfire brightened the darkness, but it could not prevent the damp cold of Dennis's Swamp creeping into their bones. It was a strange place. Martin and Tom wished that they had not accepted Jack's dare. They liked camping, but not near this swamp. "So," Martin asked as they sat watching the hot coals. "How did this place get its name?" "Are you sure you want to hear it? It's a scary story," warned Jack. "Of course!" cried out Tom. "If there were anything to be scared of, you wouldn't have chosen this place!" "Ok, but don't say I didn't warn you," said Jack, and he began this tale. "Way back in time, a man called Dennis tried to start a farm here. He built that cottage over there to live in. In those days, the area looked quite different — it was covered with tall trees and the swamp was a crystal-clear river. After three hard years, Dennis had cleared several fields and planted crops. He was so proud of his success that he refused to listen to advice. "'You are clearing too much land,' warned one old man. 'The land is a living thing. It will hit back at you if you abuse it.' "'Silly fool,' said Dennis to himself. 'If I clear more land, I can grow more crops. I'll become wealthier. He's just jealous!'" "Dennis continued to chop down trees. Small animals that relied on them for food and shelter were destroyed. He was so eager to expand his farm that he did not notice the river flowing slowly towards his door. He did not notice salt seeping to the surface of the land. He did not notice swamp plants choking all the native plants." "What happened?" Martin asked. It was growing colder. He trembled, twisting his body closer to the fire. "The land hit back — just as the old man warned," Jack shrugged. "Dennis disappeared. Old folks around here believe that swamp plants moved up from the river and dragged him underwater. His body was never found." "What a stupid story," laughed Tom. "Plants can't ..." Before he had finished speaking, he screamed and fainted. The other two boys jumped up with fright, staring at Tom. Suddenly, they burst out laughing. Some green swamp ivy had covered Tom's face. It was a while before Tom could appreciate the joke.

questions.text: The underlined word "dare" in Paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ________.
options: A. courage
B. assistance
C. instruction
D. challenge
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Martin and Tom wished that they had not accepted Jack's dare'以及他们在这个可怕的沼泽地露营可推知，dare意为'挑战、激将'，与challenge同义。courage勇气；assistance帮助；instruction指示，均不符合语境。

questions.text: Why did Jack tell Tom and Martin the story?
options: A. To frighten them.
B. To satisfy their curiosity.
C. To warn them of the danger of the place.
D. To persuade them to camp in the swamp.
questions.explanation: 根据Martin问'How did this place get its name?'以及Tom说'Of course!'可知，是他们的好奇心促使Jack讲故事，即Jack是为了满足他们的好奇心。A吓唬他们只是故事的效果而非目的；C警告他们危险不是目的；D说服他们在沼泽露营与原文相反。

questions.text: Why did Dennis ignore the warning of the old man?
options: A. The old man envied him.
B. The old man was foolish.
C. He was too busy to listen to others.
D. He was greedy for more crops.
questions.explanation: 根据Dennis的话'If I clear more land, I can grow more crops. I'll become wealthier. He's just jealous!'可知，Dennis认为开垦更多土地就能种更多庄稼、变得更富有，即他贪婪地想要更多庄稼。A老人嫉妒他是Dennis的想法而非事实；B老人愚蠢是Dennis的想法；C太忙没时间听别人说无依据。

questions.text: Why did Tom scream and faint?
options: A. He saw Dennis's shadow
B. He was scared by a plant
C. His friends played a joke on him.
D. The weather became extremely cold.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Some green swamp ivy had covered Tom's face.'可知，Tom被绿色沼泽常春藤盖住脸，在刚听完恐怖故事的情境下被吓到晕倒，即被植物吓到。A看到Dennis的影子错误；C朋友开玩笑错误，是常春藤意外盖住脸；D天气变得极冷不是晕倒原因。

questions.text: What lesson can we learn from the story of Dennis?
options: A. Grasp all, lose all.
B. No sweat, no sweet.
C. It is no use crying over spilt milk.
D. He who makes no mistakes makes nothing.
questions.explanation: Dennis过度开垦，贪得无厌，想要更多庄稼和财富，最终土地报复，他失踪了，体现了'贪多必失'（Grasp all, lose all）的道理。B不劳无获强调努力；C覆水难收强调后悔无用；D不犯错的人一事无成强调犯错的价值，均不符合故事主旨。

items.title: 2013 江西 阅读B
items.passage: When international aid is given, steps must be taken to ensure that the aid reaches the people for whom it is intended. The way to achieve this may not be simple. It is very difficult for a nation to give help directly to people in another nation. The United Nations Organization (UNO) could undertake to direct the distribution of aid. Here however rises the problem of costs. Also tied with this is time. Perhaps the UNO could set up a body of devoted men and women in every country who can speedily distribute aid to victims of floods and earthquakes. More than the help that one nation can give to another during a disaster, it would be more effective to give other forms of help during normal times. A common proverb says, "Give me a fish and I eat for a day, teach me to fish and I eat for a lifetime." If we follow this wise saying, it would be right to teach people from less developed nations to take care of themselves. For example, a country could share its technology with another. This could be in simple areas like agriculture or in more complex areas like medical and health care or even in building satellites. Even a small country is able to help less developed nations. Sometimes what is taken for granted, like the setting up of a water purification plant or the administration of a school, could be useful for countries which are looking about to solve common problems. It does not cost much to share such simple things. Exchange students could be attached for a number of months or years and learn the required craft while on the site. They can then take their knowledge back to their homelands and if necessary come back from time to time to clear doubts or to update themselves. Such aid will be truly helpful and there is no chance of it being temporary or of it falling into the wrong hands. Many countries run extensive courses in all sorts of skills. It will not cost much to include deserving foreigners in these courses. Besides giving effective help to the countries concerned, there is also the build-up of friendships to consider. Giving direct help by giving materials may be effective in the short run and must continue to be given in the event of emergencies. However, in the long run what is really effective would be the sharing of knowledge.

questions.text: According to the author, how could international aid reach the victims in time?
options: A. By solving the cost problems
B. By solving the transportation problems
C. By setting up a body of devoted people in every country.
D. By relying on the direct distribution of the UNO.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段最后一句'Perhaps the UNO could set up a body of devoted men and women in every country who can speedily distribute aid to victims of floods and earthquakes.'可知，作者建议在每个国家建立一支由热心人士组成的队伍，以快速向灾民分发援助。A解决成本问题只是提到的问题之一；B解决交通问题文中未提及；D依靠联合国直接分发错误，直接分发有成本和时间问题。

questions.text: What does the author try to express in the underlined sentence?
options: A. Providing food is vital
B. Learning to fish is helpful
C. Teaching skills is essential
D. Looking after others is important.
questions.explanation: 划线句'Give me a fish and I eat for a day, teach me to fish and I eat for a lifetime'意为'授人以鱼不如授人以渔'，结合后文'it would be right to teach people from less developed nations to take care of themselves'可知，作者想表达的是传授技能（教人们自力更生）是至关重要的。A提供食物至关重要与句意相反；B学钓鱼有帮助是字面意思；D照顾别人重要不是核心。

questions.text: The second paragraph is developed mainly _________.
options: A. by example
B. by process
C. by comparison
D. by contrast
questions.explanation: 第二段提出'授人以渔'的观点后，用'For example'引出多个例子：分享技术（农业、医疗、卫星制造）、建立净水厂、学校管理、交换学生等，说明如何帮助欠发达国家。因此第二段主要是通过举例（by example）展开的。B按过程、C按比较、D按对比均不符合。

questions.text: Which aid is likely to fall into the wrong hands?
options: A. A medical team.
B. An exchange program.
C. A water plant.
D. Financial support.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段最后一句'Such aid will be truly helpful and there is no chance of it being temporary or of it falling into the wrong hands.'可知，技术分享、知识传授这类援助不会落入坏人之手。反过来，直接的资金支持（Financial support）最容易被挪用、落入坏人手中。A医疗队、B交换项目、C净水厂都属于技术/知识类援助，不易被挪用。

questions.text: What can we infer about international aid from the passage?
options: A. It is facing difficulties.
B. It is unnecessary during normal times
C. It should be given in the form of materials
D. It has gained support from developed countries
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'it could not be simple'、'rises the problem of costs'、'Also tied with this is time'以及直接援助难以到达灾民手中可推知，国际援助正面临困难。B平时不需要错误，作者认为平时更应提供技术援助；C应该以物资形式提供错误，作者认为长远来看知识共享更有效；D已获得发达国家支持文中未提及。

items.title: 2013 江西 阅读C
items.passage: Many people think that listening is a passive business. It is just the opposite. Listening well is an active exercise of our attention and hard work. It is because they do not realize this, or because they are not willing to do the work, that most people do not listen well. Listening well also requires total concentration upon someone else. An essential part of listening well is the rule known as 'bracketing'. Bracketing includes the temporary giving up or setting aside of your own prejudices and desires, to experience as far as possible someone else's world from the inside, stepping into his or her shoes. Moreover, since listening well involves bracketing, it also involves a temporary acceptance of the other person. Sensing this acceptance, the speaker will seem quite willing to open up the inner part of his or her mind to the listener. True communication is under way and the energy required for listening well is so great that it can be accomplished only by the will to extend oneself for mutual growth. Most of the time we lack this energy. Even though we may feel in our business dealings or social relationships that we are listening well, what we are usually doing is listening selectively. Often we have a prepared list in mind and wonder, as we listen, how we can achieve certain desired results to get the conversation over as quickly as possible or redirected in ways more satisfactory to us. Many of us are far more interested in talking than in listening, or we simply refuse to listen to what we don't want to hear. It wasn't until toward the end of my doctor career that I have found the knowledge that one is being truly listened to is frequently therapeutic. In about a quarter of the patients I saw, surprising improvement was shown during the first few months of psychotherapy, before any of the roots of problems had been uncovered or explained. There are several reasons for this phenomenon, but chief among them, I believe, was the patient's sense that he or she was being truly listened to, often for the first time in years, and for some, perhaps for the first time ever.

questions.text: The phrase "stepping into his or her shoes" in paragraph 2 probably means _______.
options: A. preparing a topic list first
B. focusing on one's own mind
C. directing the talk to the desired results
D. experiencing the speaker's inside world
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'to experience as far as possible someone else's world from the inside, stepping into his or her shoes'可知，'stepping into his or her shoes'是对前面'experience someone else's world from the inside'的解释，即体验说话者的内心世界。A先准备话题列表、B专注于自己的思想、C引导谈话达到预期结果均与原文意思相反。

questions.text: What is mainly discussed in Paragraph 2?
options: A. How to listen well.
B. What to listen to.
C. Benefits of listening.
D. Problems in listening
questions.explanation: 第二段开头说'Listening well also requires total concentration upon someone else'，然后介绍了'bracketing'（括号法）的具体做法：暂时放下偏见、站在对方角度、暂时接纳对方，全段都在讲如何良好地倾听（How to listen well）。B听什么、C倾听的好处、D倾听中的问题均不是第二段主旨。

questions.text: According to the author, in communication people tend to ________.
options: A. listen actively
B. listen purposefully
C. set aside their prejudices
D. open up their inner mind
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'what we are usually doing is listening selectively. Often we have a prepared list in mind and wonder, as we listen, how we can achieve certain desired results'可知，人们在交流中往往是有目的地倾听（listen purposefully），带着预设的目标，想尽快结束谈话或引导到自己满意的方向。A主动倾听错误，作者说大多数人做不到；C放下偏见是良好倾听的做法而非人们倾向于做的；D敞开心扉是说话者在被接纳时的反应。

questions.text: According to the author, the patients improved mainly because _______.
options: A. they were taken good care of.
B. they knew they were truly listened to.
C. they had partners to talk to.
D. they knew the roots of problems.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'chief among them, I believe, was the patient's sense that he or she was being truly listened to'可知，作者认为病人改善的主要原因是他们感觉到自己被真正倾听了。A被好好照顾不是主要原因；C有谈话伙伴不是核心；D知道问题根源错误，原文说在问题根源被揭示前就有了改善。

questions.text: What type of writing the article likely to be?
options: A. Science fiction
B. A news report.
C. A medical report.
D. Popular science
questions.explanation: 本文探讨了倾听的心理学原理和疗效，语言通俗易懂，面向普通读者，属于科普文章（Popular science）。A科幻小说错误；B新闻报道错误，不是报道事件；C医学报告错误，虽然提到心理治疗，但不是专业医学研究报告，而是面向大众的科普文章。

items.title: 2013 江西 阅读D
items.passage: One might expect that the ever-growing demands of the tourist trade would bring nothing but good for the countries that receive the holiday-makers. Indeed, a rosy picture is painted for the long-term future of the holiday industry. Every month sees the building of a new hotel somewhere, and every month another rock-bound Pacific island is advertised as the 'last paradise on earth'. However, the scale and speed of this growth seem set to destroy the very things tourists want to enjoy. In those countries where there was a rush to make quick money out of sea-side holidays, over-crowded beaches and the concrete jungles of endless hotels have begun to lose their appeal. Those countries with little experience of tourism can suffer most. In recent years, Nepal set out to attract foreign visitors to fund developments in health and education. Its forests, full of wildlife and rare flowers, were offered to tourists as one more untouched paradise. In fact, the nature all too soon felt the effects of thousands of holiday-makers traveling through the forest land. Ancient tracks became major routes for the walkers, with the consequent exploitation of precious trees and plants. Not only can the environment of a country suffer from the sudden growth of tourism. The people as well rapidly feel its effects. Farmland makes way for hotels, roads and airports; the old way of life goes. The one-time farmer is now the servant of some multi-national organization; he is no longer his own master. Once it was his back that bore the pain; now it is his smile that is exploited. No doubt he wonders whether he wasn't happier in his village working his own land. Thankfully, the tourist industry is waking up to the responsibilities it has towards those countries that receive its customers. The protection of wildlife and the creation of national parks go hand in hand with tourist development and in fact obtain financial support from tourist companies. At the same time, tourists are being encouraged to respect not only the countryside they visit but also its people. The way tourism is handled in the next ten years will decide its fate and that of the countries we all want to visit. Their needs and problems are more important than those of the tourist companies. Increased understanding in planning world-wide tourism can preserve the market for these companies. If not, in a few years' time the very things that attract tourists now may well have been destroyed.

questions.text: What does the author indicate in the last sentence of Paragraph 1?
options: A. The Pacific Island is a paradise.
B. The Pacific Island is worth visiting.
C. The advertisement is not convincing.
D. The advertisement is not impressive
questions.explanation: 第一段最后一句说每个月都有另一个太平洋岩石岛被宣传为'地球上最后的天堂'，结合第二段'However'转折指出旅游业正在破坏游客想要享受的东西，可推知作者暗示这些广告不可信（not convincing），因为'最后的天堂'太多了，名不副实。A太平洋岛是天堂、B值得参观是广告内容不是作者暗示；D广告不令人印象深刻不准确，核心是不可信。

questions.text: The example of Nepal is used to suggest _________.
options: A. its natural resources are untouched.
B. its forests are exploited for farmland
C. it develops well in health and education.
D. it suffers from the heavy flow of tourists.
questions.explanation: 第三段开头说'Those countries with little experience of tourism can suffer most'，然后举尼泊尔为例：尼泊尔吸引游客资助医疗教育，但很快自然就受到了成千上万游客的影响，古道变成步行路线，珍贵树木被砍伐。这个例子说明尼泊尔遭受了大量游客涌入的痛苦。A自然资源未受破坏与原文相反；B森林被开垦为农田错误，是被游客破坏；C医疗教育发展好不是例子要说明的重点。

questions.text: What can we learn about the farmers from Paragraph 4?
options: A. They are happy to work their own lands.
B. They have to please the tourists for a living.
C. They have to struggle for their independence.
D. They are proud of working in multi-national organizations.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'The one-time farmer is now the servant of some multi-national organization; he is no longer his own master. Once it was his back that bore the pain; now it is his smile that is exploited.'可知，曾经的农民现在成了跨国组织的仆人，不再是自己的主人，过去是脊背受苦，现在是微笑被利用，即他们不得不靠取悦游客谋生。A高兴耕种自己的土地错误，他们失去了土地；C不得不为独立而斗争无依据；D以为在跨国组织工作自豪错误，他们怀疑过去在村里种地是否更快乐。

questions.text: Which of the following determines the future of tourism?
options: A. The number of tourists
B. The improvement of services.
C. The promotion of new products.
D. The management of tourism
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'The way tourism is handled in the next ten years will decide its fate'可知，未来十年旅游业的管理方式（The way tourism is handled = The management of tourism）将决定其命运。A游客数量、B服务改善、C新产品推广均不是决定因素。

questions.text: The author's attitude towards the development of the tourist industry is __________.
options: A. optimistic
B. doubtful
C. objective
D. negative
questions.explanation: 作者既指出了旅游业快速发展带来的环境和社会问题，又提到'Thankfully, the tourist industry is waking up to the responsibilities'，最后说未来十年的管理将决定命运，增加理解可以保护市场。作者既不盲目乐观也不完全否定，而是客观地（objective）分析问题和前景。A乐观、B怀疑、D否定均不符合作者的平衡态度。

items.title: 2013 浙江 阅读A
items.passage: No one knows for sure when advertising first started. It is possible that it grew out of the discovery that some people did certain kinds of work better than others did them. That led to the conception of specialization, which means that people would specialize, or focus on doing one special job. Let's take a man we'll call Mr. Fielder, for example. He did everything connected with farming. He planted seeds, tended the fields and harvested and sold his crops. At the same time, he did many other jobs on the farm. However, he didn't make the bricks for his house, cut his trees into boards, make the plows, or any of the other hundreds of things a farm needs. Instead, he got them from people who specialized in doing each of those things. Suppose there was another man we shall call Mr. Plowright. Using what he knew about farming and working with iron, Mr. Plowright invented a plow that made farming easier. Mr. Plowright did not really like farming himself and wanted to specialize in making really good plows. Perhaps, he thought, other farmers will trade what they grow for one of my plows. How did Mr. Plowright let people know what he was doing? Why, he advertised, of course. First, he opened a shop and then he put up a sign outside the shop to attract customers. That sign may have been no more than a plow carved into a piece of wood and a simple arrow pointed to the shop door. It was probably all the information people needed to find Mr. Plowright and his really good plows. Many historians believe that the first outdoor signs were used about five thousand years ago. Even before most people could read, they understood such signs. Shopkeepers would carve into stone, clay or wood symbols for the products they had for sale. A medium, in advertising talk, is the way you communicate your message. You might say the first medium used in advertising was signs with symbols. The second medium was audio, or sound, although that term isn't used exactly the way we use it today. Originally just human voice and maybe some simple instruments, such as a bell, were used to get people's attention. A crier, in a historical sense, isn't someone who wept easily. It is someone, probably a man, with a voice loud enough to be heard over the other noises of a city. In ancient Egypt, shopkeepers might hire such a person to spread the news about their products. Often these earliest forms of advertising involved a newly arrived ship loaded with goods. Perhaps the crier described the goods, explained where they came from and praised their quality. His job was, in other words, not too different from a TV or radio commercial in today's world.

questions.text: What probably led to the start of advertising?
options: A. The discovery of iron
B. The specialization of labor
C. The appearance of new jobs
D. The development of farm techniques
questions.explanation: 根据第一段It is possible that it grew out of the discovery that some people did certain kinds of work better than others did them. That led to the conception of specialization可知，广告可能源于人们发现有些人做某些工作比别人做得好，这导致了专业化的概念，即劳动专业化。A铁的发现错误；C新工作的出现不是根本原因；D农业技术的发展错误。

questions.text: To advertise his plow, Mr. Plowright _________.
options: A. praised his plows in public
B. placed a sign outside the shop
C. hung an arrow pointing to the shop
D. showed his products to the customers
questions.explanation: 根据第四段First, he opened a shop and then he put up a sign outside the shop to attract customers可知，Plowright先生为了给他的犁做广告，先开了一家店，然后在店外挂了一个招牌吸引顾客。A公开赞扬他的犁错误；C挂一个指向商店的箭头只是招牌的一部分，不全面；D向顾客展示产品错误。

questions.text: The writer makes up the two stories of Mr. Fielder and Mr. Plowright in order to _________.
options: A. explain the origin of advertising
B. predict the future of advertising
C. expose the problems in advertising
D. provide suggestions for advertising
questions.explanation: 文章以Fielder先生（农民，什么都做但不做砖、犁等）和Plowright先生（犁匠，专门做犁并开店做广告）为例，说明专业化如何促使广告产生，所以作者编造这两个故事是为了解释广告的起源。B预测广告的未来错误；C揭露广告中的问题错误；D提供广告建议错误。

questions.text: In ancient Egypt, a crier was probably someone who _________.
options: A. owned a ship
B. had the loudest voice
C. ran a shop selling goods to farmers
D. functioned like today's TV or radio commercial
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段In ancient Egypt, shopkeepers might hire such a person to spread the news about their products和His job was, in other words, not too different from a TV or radio commercial in today's world可知，古代埃及的叫卖者的工作与今天的电视或广播广告没有太大不同，即功能类似今天的电视或广播广告。A拥有一艘船错误；B有最大的声音只是特征之一，不是功能；C开商店向农民卖货错误。

questions.text: The last two paragraphs are mainly about _________.
options: A. the history of advertising
B. the benefits of advertising
C. the early forms of advertising
D. the basic design of advertising
questions.explanation: 倒数第二段介绍广告的媒介从符号招牌发展到声音（人声和铃铛等简单乐器），最后一段介绍古代埃及的叫卖者（crier），这两段主要介绍广告的早期形式。A广告的历史范围太广；B广告的好处不是这两段的重点；D广告的基本设计错误。

items.title: 2013 浙江 阅读B
items.passage: Below is a selection from a popular science book. If blood is red, why are veins blue? Actually, veins are not blue at all. They are more of a clear, yellowish color. Although blood looks red when it's outside the body, when it's sitting in a vein near the surface of the skin, it's more of a dark reddish purple color. At the right depth, these blood-filled veins reflect less red light than the surrounding skin, making them look blue by comparison. Which works harder, your heart or your brain? That kind of depends on whether you're busy thinking or busy exercising. Your heart works up to three times harder during exercise, and shifts enough blood over a lifetime to fill a supertanker. But, in the long run, your brain probably tips it, because even when you're sitting still your brain is using twice as much energy as your heart, and it takes four to five times as much blood to feed it. Why do teeth fall out, and why don't they grow back in grown-ups? Baby (or "milk") teeth do not last long; they fall out to make room for bigger, stronger adult teeth later on. Adult teeth fall out when they become damaged, decayed and infected by bacteria. Once this second set of teeth has grown in, you're done. When they're gone, they're gone. This is because nature figures you're set for life, and what controls regrowth of your teeth switches off. Do old people shrink as they age? Yes and no. Many people do get shorter as they age. But, when they do, it isn't because they're shrinking all over. They simply lose height as their spine becomes shorter and more curved due to disuse and the effects of gravity. Many (but not all) men and women do lose height as they get older. Men lose an average of 3-4 cm in height as they age, while women may lose 5 cm or more. If you live to be 200 years old, would you keep shrinking till you were, like 60 cm tall, like a little boy again? No, because old people don't really shrink! It is not that they are growing backwards — their legs, arms and backbones getting shorter. When they do get shorter, it's because the spine has shortened a little. Or, more often, become more bent and curved. Why does spinning make you dizzy? Because your brain gets confused between what you're seeing and what you're feeling. The brain senses that you're spinning using special gravity-and motion-sensing organs in your inner ear, which work together with your eyes to keep your vision and balance stable. But, when you suddenly stop spinning the system goes out of control, and your brain thinks you're moving while you're not! Where do feelings and emotions come from? Mostly from an ancient part of the brain called the limbic system. All mammals have this brain area — from mice to dogs, cats, and humans. So all mammals feel basic emotions like fear, pain and pleasure. But since human feelings also involve other, newer bits of the brain, we feel more complex emotions than any other animal on the planet. If exercise wears you out, how can it be good for you? Because our bodies adapt to everything we do to them. And as far as your body is concerned, it's "use it, or lose it"! It's not that exercise makes you healthy; it's more that a lack of exercise leaves your body weak and easily affected by disease.

questions.text: What is the colour of blood in a vein near the surface of the skin?
options: A. Blue.
B. Light yellow.
C. Red.
D. Dark reddish purple.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段when it's sitting in a vein near the surface of the skin, it's more of a dark reddish purple color可知，皮肤表面附近静脉中的血液呈暗红紫色。A蓝色是静脉看起来的颜色，不是血液的颜色；B淡黄色是静脉本身的颜色；C红色是血液在体外的颜色。

questions.text: Why do some old people look a little shrunken as they age?
options: A. Because their spine is in active use.
B. Because they are more easily affected by gravity.
C. Because they keep growing backwards.
D. Because their spine becomes more bent.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段They simply lose height as their spine becomes shorter and more curved due to disuse and the effects of gravity和When they do get shorter, it's because the spine has shortened a little. Or, more often, become more bent and curved可知，老年人看起来有点萎缩是因为脊柱变得更弯了。A脊柱在积极使用错误；B更容易受重力影响不是直接原因；C他们一直在反向生长错误。

questions.text: Which of the following statements about our brain is true?
options: A. In the long run, our brain probably works harder than our heart.
B. When our brain senses the spinning, we will feel dizzy.
C. The brains of the other mammals are as complex as those of humans.
D. Our feelings and emotions come from the most developed area in our brain.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段But, in the long run, your brain probably tips it, because even when you're sitting still your brain is using twice as much energy as your heart可知，从长远来看，大脑可能比心脏工作更辛苦。B当大脑感觉到旋转时我们会头晕错误，是突然停止旋转时系统失控才头晕；C其他哺乳动物的大脑和人类一样复杂错误，人类的感觉涉及更新的大脑部分，更复杂；D我们的感觉和情绪来自大脑中最发达的区域错误，来自古老的边缘系统。

questions.text: What is the main purpose of this selection?
options: A. To give advice on how to stay healthy.
B. To provide information about our body.
C. To challenge new findings in medical research.
D. To report the latest discoveries in medical science.
questions.explanation: 本文以问答形式解答了关于人体的七个常见问题（静脉颜色、心脏与大脑、牙齿脱落、老年人萎缩、旋转头晕、情绪来源、运动好处），所以主要目的是提供关于我们身体的信息。A给出保持健康的建议只是部分内容；C挑战医学研究的新发现错误；D报道医学科学的最新发现错误，这些是常识性科普，不是最新发现。

questions.text: Which of the following can be the best title for this passage?
options: A. Amazing Human Body
B. Questions About Health
C. Myths and Facts About Body
D. What We Don't Know About Our Body
questions.explanation: 本文介绍了关于人体的七个有趣的科普知识，展示了人体的奇妙之处，所以最佳标题是Amazing Human Body（令人惊叹的人体）。B关于健康的问题范围太窄；C关于身体的迷思和事实不准确，这些不是迷思；D我们对身体不了解的东西不准确。

items.title: 2013 浙江 阅读C
items.passage: The baby monkey is much more developed at birth than the human baby. Almost from the moment it is born, the baby monkey can move around and hold tightly to its mother. During the first few days of its life the baby will approach and hold onto almost any large, warm, and soft object in its environment, particularly if that object also gives it milk. After a week or so, however, the baby monkey begins to avoid newcomers and focuses its attentions on "mother" — the real mother or the mother-substitute. During the first two weeks of its life warmth is perhaps the most important psychological thing that a monkey mother has to give to its baby. The Harlows, a couple who are both psychologists, discovered this fact by offering baby monkeys a choice of two types of mother-substitutes — one covered with cloth and one made of bare wire. If the two artificial mothers were both the same temperature, the little monkeys always preferred the cloth mother. However, if the wire model was heated, while the cloth model was cool, for the first two weeks after birth the baby monkeys picked the warm wire mother-substitutes as their favorites. Thereafter they switched and spent most of their time on the more comfortable cloth mother. Why is cloth preferable to bare wire? Something that the Harlows called contact comfort seems to be the answer, and a most powerful influence it is. Baby monkeys spend much of their time rubbing against their mothers' skins, putting themselves in as close contact with the parent as they can. Whenever the young animal is frightened, disturbed, or annoyed, it typically rushes to its mother and rubs itself against her body. Wire doesn't "rub" as well as does soft cloth. Prolonged "contact comfort" with a cloth mother appears to give the babies confidence and is much more rewarding to them than is either warmth or milk. According to the Harlows, the basic quality of a baby's love for its mother is trust. If the baby is put into an unfamiliar playroom without its mother, the baby ignores the toys no matter how interesting they might be. It screams in terror and curls up into a furry little ball. If its cloth mother is now introduced into the playroom, the baby rushes to it and holds onto it for dear life. After a few minutes of contact comfort, it obviously begins to feel more secure. It then climbs down from the mother-substitute and begins to explore the toys, but often rushes back for a deep embrace as if to make sure that its mother is still there and that all is well. Bit by bit its fears of the new environment are gone and it spends more and more time playing with the toys and less and less time holding onto its "mother".

questions.text: Psychologically, what does the baby monkey desire most during the first two weeks of its life?
options: A. Warmth
B. Milk
C. Contact
D. Trust
questions.explanation: 根据第二段During the first two weeks of its life warmth is perhaps the most important psychological thing that a monkey mother has to give to its baby可知，在出生后的头两周，温暖是幼猴在心理上最渴望的东西。B奶是生理需求，不是心理需求；C接触安慰是两周后更重要的；D信任是更高级的情感。

questions.text: After the first two weeks of their life, baby monkeys prefer the cloth mother to the wire mother because the former is _________.
options: A. larger in size
B. closer to them
C. less frightening and less disturbing
D. more comfortable to rub against
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Why is cloth preferable to bare wire? Something that the Harlows called contact comfort seems to be the answer和Baby monkeys spend much of their time rubbing against their mothers' skins... Wire doesn't "rub" as well as does soft cloth可知，两周后幼猴更喜欢布妈妈是因为布妈妈摩擦起来更舒适，能提供接触安慰。A尺寸更大错误；B离它们更近错误；C不那么令人害怕和打扰不是主要原因。

questions.text: What does the baby monkey probably gain from prolonged "contact comfort"?
options: A. Attention.
B. Softness.
C. Confidence.
D. Interest.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Prolonged "contact comfort" with a cloth mother appears to give the babies confidence and is much more rewarding to them than is either warmth or milk可知，长时间的接触安慰给了幼猴信心。A注意力错误；B柔软只是布的特性，不是幼猴获得的心理收益；D兴趣错误。

questions.text: It can be inferred that when the baby monkey feels secure, _________.
options: A. it frequently rushes back for a deep embrace when exploring the toys
B. it spends more time screaming to get rewards
C. it is less attracted to the toys though they are interesting
D. it cares less about whether its mother is still around
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Bit by bit its fears of the new environment are gone and it spends more and more time playing with the toys and less and less time holding onto its "mother"可知，当幼猴感到安全时，它花越来越多的时间玩玩具，越来越少的时间抓住妈妈，即不太在意妈妈是否还在身边。A探索玩具时经常冲回来深抱是还没完全安全时的行为；B花更多时间尖叫以获得奖励错误；C虽然玩具有趣但对玩具的吸引力较小错误，感到安全时会更被玩具吸引。

questions.text: The main purpose of the passage is to _________.
options: A. give the reasons for the experiment
B. present the findings of the experiment
C. introduce the method of the experiment
D. describe the process of the experiment
questions.explanation: 本文主要介绍了Harlow夫妇关于幼猴依恋实验的发现：头两周温暖最重要，两周后接触安慰更重要，接触安慰给幼猴信心，婴儿对母亲的爱的基本品质是信任。所以文章的主要目的是呈现实验的发现。A给出实验的原因只是部分内容；C介绍实验的方法只是部分内容；D描述实验的过程只是部分内容。

items.title: 2013 浙江 阅读D
items.passage: In 1974, after filling out fifty applications, going through four interviews, and winning one offer, I took what I could get — a teaching job at what I considered a distant wild area: western New Jersey. My characteristic optimism was alive only when I reminded myself that I would be doing what I had wanted to do since I was fourteen — teaching English. School started, but I felt more and more as if I were in a foreign country. Was this rural area really New Jersey? My students took a week off when hunting season began. I was told they were also frequently absent in late October to help their fathers make hay on the farms. I was a young woman from New York City, who thought that "Make hay while the sun shines" just meant to have a good time. But, still, I was teaching English. I worked hard, taking time off only to eat and sleep. And then there was my sixth-grade class — seventeen boys and five girls who were only six years younger than me. I had a problem long before I knew it. I was struggling in my work as a young idealistic teacher. I wanted to make literature come alive and to promote a love of the written word. The students wanted to throw spitballs and whisper dirty words in the back of the room. In college I had been taught that a successful educator should ignore bad behavior. So I did, confident that, as the textbook had said, the bad behavior would disappear as I gave my students positive attention. It sounds reasonable, but the text evidently ignored the fact that humans, particularly teenagers, rarely seem reasonable. By the time my boss, who was also my taskmaster, known to be the strictest, most demanding, most quick to fire inexperienced teachers, came into the classroom to observe me, the students exhibited very little good behavior to praise. My boss sat in the back of the room. The boys in the class were making animal noises, hitting each other while the girls filed their nails or read magazines. I just pretended it all wasn't happening, and went on lecturing and tried to ask some inspiring questions. My boss, sitting in the back of the room, seemed to be growing bigger and bigger. After twenty minutes he left, silently. Visions of unemployment marched before my eyes. I felt mildly victorious that I got through the rest of class without crying, but at my next free period I had to face him. I wondered if he would let me finish out the day. I walked to his office, took a deep breath, and opened the door. He was sitting in his chair, and he looked at me long and hard. I said nothing. All I could think of was that I was not an English teacher; I had been lying to myself, pretending that everything was fine. When he spoke, he said simply, without accusation, "You had nothing to say to them." "You had nothing to say to them," he repeated. "No wonder they're bored. Why not get to the meat of the literature and stop talking about symbolism. Talk with them, not at them. And more important, why do you ignore their bad behavior?" We talked. He named my problems and offered solutions. We role played. He was the bad student, and I was the forceful, yet warm, teacher. As the year progressed, we spent many hours discussing literature and ideas about human beings. And their attentions, he helped me identify my weakness and my strengths. In short, he made a teacher of me by teaching me the reality of Emerson's words: "The secret to education lies in respecting the pupil." Fifteen years later I still drive that same winding road to the same school. Thanks to the help I received that difficult first year, the school is my home now.

questions.text: It can be inferred from the story that in 1974 _________.
options: A. The writer became an optimistic person
B. The writer was very happy about her new job
C. It was rather difficult to get a job in the USA
D. It was easy to get a teaching job in New Jersey
questions.explanation: 根据第一段In 1974, after filling out fifty applications, going through four interviews, and winning one offer可知，作者填了50份申请、经历了4次面试才获得1份录用，说明1974年在美国找工作相当困难。A作者变成了一个乐观的人错误，她本来就有特有的乐观；B作者对她的新工作非常高兴错误，她认为这是遥远荒凉的地方；D在新泽西找教学工作很容易错误，恰恰相反。

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following is most probably the writer's problem as a new teacher?
options: A. She had blind trust in what she learnt at college.
B. She didn't ask experienced teachers for advice.
C. She took too much time off to eat and sleep.
D. She didn't like teaching English literature
questions.explanation: 根据第四段In college I had been taught that a successful educator should ignore bad behavior. So I did, confident that, as the textbook had said, the bad behavior would disappear as I gave my students positive attention可知，作者作为新教师的问题是她盲目相信大学所学的东西——成功的教育者应该忽视不良行为，结果导致课堂纪律混乱。B她没有向有经验的老师请教不是主要问题；C她花太多时间吃饭睡觉错误，她只在吃饭睡觉时休息；D她不喜欢教英国文学错误，她从14岁起就想教英语。

questions.text: What is the writer's biggest worry after her taskmaster's observation of her class?
options: A. She might lose her teaching job.
B. She might lose her students' respect.
C. She couldn't teach the same class any more.
D. She couldn't ignore her students' bad behavior any more
questions.explanation: 根据第五段Visions of unemployment marched before my eyes和第六段I wondered if he would let me finish out the day可知，老板听课后作者最大的担忧是她可能会失去教学工作。B她可能会失去学生的尊重不是最大的担忧；C她不能再教同一个班了错误；D她不能再忽视学生的不良行为了不是最大的担忧。

questions.text: Which of the following gives the writer a sense of mild victory?
options: A. Her talk about symbolism sounded convincing
B. Her students behaved a little better than usual.
C. She managed to finish the class without crying.
D. She was invited for a talk by her boss after class.
questions.explanation: 根据第六段I felt mildly victorious that I got through the rest of class without crying可知，作者感到有点胜利是因为她没有哭着上完剩下的课。A她关于象征主义的谈话听起来有说服力错误；B她的学生表现比平时好一点错误；D课后她被老板邀请谈话不是胜利感的来源。

questions.text: The taskmaster's attitude towards the writer after his observation of her class can be best described as _________.
options: A. cruel but encouraging
B. fierce but forgiving
C. sincere and supportive
D. angry and aggressive
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第三段When he spoke, he said simply, without accusation和He named my problems and offered solutions. We role played. He was the bad student, and I was the forceful, yet warm, teacher以及倒数第二段he helped me identify my weakness and my strengths可知，老板听课后对作者的态度是真诚和支持的——没有指责，指出问题并提供解决方案，进行角色扮演帮助她，帮助她认识自己的弱点和长处。A残酷但鼓励错误；B严厉但宽容不全面；D愤怒和攻击性错误。

items.title: 2013 湖北 阅读A
items.passage: Some years ago, writing in my diary used to be a usual activity. I would return from school and spend the expected half hour recording the day's events, feelings, and impressions in my little blue diary. I did not really need to express my emotions by way of words, but I gained a certain satisfaction from seeing my experiences forever recorded on paper. After all, isn't accumulating memories a way of preserving the past? When I was thirteen years old, I went on a long journey on foot in a great valley, well-equipped with pens, a diary, and a camera. During the trip, I was busy recording every incident, name and place I came across. I felt proud to be spending my time productively, dutifully preserving for future generations a detailed description of my travels. On my last night there, I wandered out of my tent, diary in hand. The sky was clear and lit by the glare of the moon, and the walls of the valley looked threatening behind their screen of shadows. I automatically took out my pen... At that point, I understood that nothing I wrote could ever match or replace the few seconds I allowed myself to experience the dramatic beauty of the valley. All I remembered of the previous few days were the dull characterizations I had set down in my diary. Now, I only write in my diary when I need to write down a special thought or feeling. I still love to record ideas and quotations that strike me in books, or observations that are particularly meaningful. I take pictures, but not very often — only of objects I find really beautiful. I'm no longer blindly satisfied with having something to remember when I grow old. I realize that life will simply pass me by if I stay behind the camera, busy preserving the present so as to live it in the future. I don't want to wake up one day and have nothing but a pile of pictures and notes. Maybe I won't have as many exact representations of people and places; maybe I'll forget certain facts, but at least the experiences will always remain inside me. I don't live to make memories — I just live, and the memories form themselves.

questions.text: Before the age of thirteen, the author regarded keeping a diary as a way of ______.
options: A. observing her school routine
B. expressing her satisfaction
C. impressing her classmates
D. preserving her history
questions.explanation: 根据第一段最后一句'After all, isn't accumulating memories a way of preserving the past?'可知，十三岁前作者认为记日记是积累记忆、保存过去的方式，即保存她的历史。A观察学校日常、B表达满足感、C给同学留下深刻印象均不是主要目的。

questions.text: What caused a change in the author's understanding of keeping a diary?
options: A. A dull night on the journey.
B. The beauty of the great valley.
C. A striking quotation from a book.
D. Her concerns for future generations.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'At that point, I understood that nothing I wrote could ever match or replace the few seconds I allowed myself to experience the dramatic beauty of the valley.'可知，是大峡谷的壮丽美景让作者改变了对记日记的理解，意识到任何文字都无法替代亲身经历。A旅途中一个无聊的夜晚错误；C书中引人注目的引语错误；D对后代的担忧错误。

questions.text: What does the author put in her diary now?
options: A. Notes and beautiful pictures.
B. Special thoughts and feelings.
C. Detailed accounts of daily activities.
D. Descriptions of unforgettable events.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段第一句'Now, I only write in my diary when I need to write down a special thought or feeling.'可知，作者现在只在需要记录特殊想法或感受时才写日记。A笔记和漂亮照片错误；C日常活动的详细记录是过去的做法；D难忘事件的描述错误。

questions.text: The author comes to realize that to live a meaningful life is ______.
options: A. to experience it
B. to live the present in the future
C. to make memories
D. to give accurate representations of it
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'maybe I'll forget certain facts, but at least the experiences will always remain inside me. I don't live to make memories — I just live, and the memories form themselves.'可知，作者意识到有意义的生活是去亲身经历，而不是为了制造回忆而生活。B在未来活在当下错误；C制造记忆与作者观点相反；D给出准确的描述错误。

items.title: 2013 湖北 阅读B
items.passage: Mothers and daughters go through so much — yet when was the last time a mother and daughter sat down to write a book together about it all? Perri Klass and her mother, Sheila Solomon Klass, both gifted professional writers, prove to be ideal co-writers as they examine their decades of motherhood, daughterhood, and the wonderful ways their lives have overlapped. Perri notes with amazement how closely her own life has mirrored her mother's: both have full-time careers; both have published books, articles, and stories; each has three children; they both love to read. They also love to travel — in fact, they often take trips together. But in truth, the harder they look at their lives, the more they acknowledge their big differences in circumstance and basic nature. A child of the Depression, Sheila was raised in Brooklyn by parents who considered education a luxury for girls. Starting with her college education, she has fought for everything she's ever accomplished. Perri, on the other hand, grew up privileged in the New Jersey suburbs of the 1960s and 1970s. For Sheila, wasting time or money is a crime, and luxury is unthinkable while Perri enjoys the occasional small luxury, but has not been successful at trying to persuade her mother into enjoying even the tiniest thing she likes. Each writing in her own unmistakable voice, Perri and Sheila take turns exploring the joys and pains, the love and bitterness, the minor troubles and lasting respect that have always bonded them together. Sheila describes the adventure of giving birth to Perri in a tiny town in Trinidad where her husband was doing research fieldwork. Perri admits that she can't sort out all the mess in the households, even though she knows it drives her mother crazy. Together they compare thoughts on bringing up children and working, admit long-hidden sorrows, and enjoy precious memories. Looking deep into the lives they have lived separately and together, Perri and Sheila tell their mother-daughter story with honesty, humor, enthusiasm, and admiration for each other. A written account in two voices, Every Mother Is a Daughter is a duet that produces a deep, strong sound with the experiences that all mothers and daughters will recognize.

questions.text: Why does Perri think that her own life has mirrored her mother's?
options: A. They both have gone through difficult times.
B. They have strong emotional ties with each other.
C. They have the same joys and pains, and love and bitterness.
D. They both have experiences as daughter, mother and writer.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'both have full-time careers; both have published books, articles, and stories; each has three children; they both love to read'可知，Perri认为自己的生活映照了母亲的生活，因为她们都有女儿、母亲和作家的经历。A都经历了困难时期不是主要原因；B彼此有强烈的情感纽带不是映照的含义；C有相同的喜怒哀乐错误，她们只是探讨这些，并非完全相同。

questions.text: The word "luxury" in Paragraph 3 means ______.
options: A. something rare but not pleasant
B. something that cannot be imagined
C. something expensive but not necessary
D. something that can only be enjoyed by boys
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'Sheila was raised in Brooklyn by parents who considered education a luxury for girls'以及'For Sheila, wasting time or money is a crime, and luxury is unthinkable'可知，在大萧条时期，Sheila的父母认为教育对女孩来说是奢侈品，即昂贵但非必需的东西。A稀有但不愉快错误；B无法想象的东西错误；D只能男孩享受的东西错误。

questions.text: What is Paragraph 4 mainly about?
options: A. The content of the book.
B. The purpose of the book.
C. The influence of the book.
D. The writing style of the book.
questions.explanation: 第四段描述了母女俩轮流探讨'the joys and pains, the love and bitterness, the minor troubles and lasting respect'，Sheila描述在特立尼达生Perri的经历，Perri承认家务混乱，两人比较育儿和工作的想法，这些都是书的内容（The content of the book）。B书的目的、C书的影响、D书的写作风格均不是第四段主要内容。

questions.text: How are women's lives explored in this book?
options: A. In a musical form.
B. Through field research.
C. With unique writing skills.
D. From different points of view.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'Each writing in her own unmistakable voice, Perri and Sheila take turns exploring...'和最后一段'A written account in two voices, Every Mother Is a Daughter is a duet'可知，这本书用两种声音（母亲和女儿）从不同的角度探讨女性生活。A音乐形式是比喻，不是实际形式；B通过实地研究错误；C独特的写作技巧不是核心，核心是两种视角。

items.title: 2013 湖北 阅读C
items.passage: We've reached a strange — some would say unusual — point. While fighting world hunger continues to be the matter of vital importance according to a recent report from the World Health Organization (WHO), more people now die from being overweight, or say, from being extremely fat, than from being underweight. It's the good life that's more likely to kill us these days. Worse, nearly 18 million children under the age of five around the world are estimated to be overweight. What's going on? We really don't have many excuses for our weight problems. The dangers of the problem have been drilled into us by public-health campaigns since 2001 and the message is getting through — up to a point. In the 1970s, Finland, for example, had the highest rate of heart disease in the world and being overweight was its main cause. Not any more. A public-health campaign has greatly reduced the number of heart disease deaths by 80 per cent over the past three decades. Maybe that explains why the percentage of people in Finland taking diet pills doubled between 2001 and 2005, and doctors even offer surgery of removing fat inside and change the shape of the body.
