That has become a sort of fashion. No wonder it ranks as the world's most body-conscious country. We know what we should be doing to lose weight — but actually doing it is another matter. By far the most popular excuse is not taking enough exercise. More than half of us admit we lack willpower. Others blame good food. They say: it's just too inviting and it makes them overeat. Still others lay the blame on the Americans, complaining that pounds have piled on thanks to eating too much American-style fast food. Some also blame their parents — their genes. But unfortunately, the parents are wronged because they're normal in shape, or rather slim. It's a similar story around the world, although people are relatively unlikely to have tried to lose weight. Parents are eager to see their kids shape up. Do as I say — not as I do.

questions.text: What is the "strange" point mentioned in the first sentence?
options: A. The good life is a greater risk than the bad life.
B. Starvation is taking more people's lives in the world.
C. WHO report shows people's unawareness of food safety.
D. Overweight issue remains unresolved despite WHO's efforts.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'more people now die from being overweight... than from being underweight. It's the good life that's more likely to kill us these days.'可知，这个奇怪的点是：好生活（超重）比坏生活（饥饿）更可能杀死我们，即好生活比坏生活风险更大。B饥饿夺走更多生命与原文相反；C WHO报告显示人们不了解食品安全错误；D尽管WHO努力超重问题仍未解决不是'strange point'的含义。

questions.text: Why does the author think that people have no excuse for being overweight?
options: A. A lot of effective diet pills are available.
B. Body image has nothing to do with good food.
C. They have been made fully aware of its dangers.
D. There are too many overweight people in the world.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'The dangers of the problem have been drilled into us by public-health campaigns since 2001 and the message is getting through — up to a point.'可知，作者认为人们没有借口超重，因为自2001年以来公共卫生运动已经让人们充分认识到超重的危险。A很多有效减肥药可用错误；B身材与好食物无关错误；D世界上超重的人太多不是没有借口的原因。

questions.text: The example of Finland is used to illustrate ______.
options: A. the cause of heart disease
B. the fashion of body shaping
C. the effectiveness of a campaign
D. the history of a body-conscious country
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'A public-health campaign has greatly reduced the number of heart disease deaths by 80 per cent over the past three decades.'可知，芬兰的例子用来说明公共卫生运动的有效性（effectiveness of a campaign），使心脏病死亡率下降了80%。A心脏病的原因只是背景；B塑身时尚是后续结果不是例子要说明的核心；D注重身材国家的历史不是核心。

questions.text: Which would be the best title for the passage?
options: A. Actions or Excuses?
B. Overweight or Underweight?
C. WHO in a Dilemma
D. No Longer Dying of Hunger
questions.explanation: 全文先指出超重问题的严重性，然后说人们知道应该减肥但有各种借口（缺乏锻炼、缺乏意志力、食物太诱人、美式快餐、基因等），最后讽刺'Do as I say — not as I do'。核心是行动还是借口（Actions or Excuses?）。B超重还是体重过轻只是开头对比；C WHO陷入困境错误；D不再死于饥饿只是部分内容。

items.title: 2013 湖北 阅读D
items.passage: The technology is great. Without it we wouldn't have been able to put a man on the moon, explore the ocean's depths or eat microwave sausages. Computers have revolutionized our lives and they have the power to educate and pass on knowledge. But sometimes this power can create more problems than it solves. Every doctor has had to try their best to calm down patients who've come into their surgery waving an Internet print-out, convinced that they have some rare incurable disease, say, throat cancer. The truth is usually far more ordinary, though: they don't have throat cancer, and it's just that their throats are swollen. Being a graduate of the Internet "school" of medicine does not guarantee accurate self-health-checks. One day Mrs. Almond came to my hospital after feeling faint at work. While I took her blood sample and tried to find out what was wrong, she said calmly, "I know what's wrong; I've got throat cancer. I know there's nothing you doctors can do about it and I've just got to wait until the day comes." As a matter of routine I ordered a chest X-ray. I looked at it and the blood results an hour later. Something wasn't right. "Did your local doctor do an X-ray?" I asked. "Oh, I haven't been to the doctor for years," she replied. "I read about it on a website and the symptoms fitted, so I knew that's what I had." However, some of her symptoms, like the severe cough and weight loss, didn't fit with it — but she'd just ignored this. I looked at the X-ray again, and more tests confirmed it wasn't the cancer but tuberculosis — something that most certainly did need treating, and could be deadly. She was lucky we caught it when we did. Mrs. Almond went pale when I explained she would have to be on treatment for the next six months to ensure that she was fully recovered. It was certainly a lesson for her. "I'm so embarrassed," she said, shaking her head, as I explained that all the people she had come into close contact with would have to be found out and tested. She listed up to about 20, and then I went to my office to type up my notes. Unexpectedly, the computer was not working, so I had to wait until someone from the IT department came to fix it. Typical. Maybe I should have a microwave sausage while I waited?

questions.text: Mrs. Almond talked about her illness calmly because ______.
options: A. she thought she knew it well
B. she had purchased medicine online
C. she graduated from a medical school
D. she had been treated by local doctors
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'I know what's wrong; I've got throat cancer. I know there's nothing you doctors can do about it'和第四段'I read about it on a website and the symptoms fitted, so I knew that's what I had.'可知，Almond太太平静地谈论她的病是因为她在网上看到症状对得上，自以为很了解自己的病。B在网上买药错误；C医学院毕业错误；D当地医生治疗过错误，她多年没看医生。

questions.text: It was lucky for Mrs. Almond ______.
options: A. to have contacted many friends
B. to have recovered in a short time
C. to have her assumption confirmed
D. to have her disease identified in time
questions.explanation: 根据第六段'She was lucky we caught it when we did.'可知，Almond太太幸运的是她的病（肺结核）被及时发现了。A联系了很多朋友不是幸运的原因；B短时间内恢复错误，需要六个月治疗；C她的假设被证实错误，她的假设（喉癌）是错的。

questions.text: Mrs. Almond said "I'm so embarrassed" (Para. 7) because ______.
options: A. she had distrusted her close friends
B. she had caused unnecessary trouble
C. she had to refuse the doctor's advice
D. she had to tell the truth to the doctor
questions.explanation: 根据第七段'all the people she had come into close contact with would have to be found out and tested. She listed up to about 20'可知，Almond太太感到尴尬是因为她误以为自己得了喉癌，没有及时就医，结果得了肺结核，导致约20个密切接触者都需要被找到并检查，即她造成了不必要的麻烦。A不信任亲密朋友错误；C拒绝医生建议错误；D必须告诉医生真相错误。

questions.text: By mentioning the breakdown of the computer, the author probably wants to prove ______.
options: A. it's a must to take a break at work
B. it's vital to believe in IT professionals
C. it's unwise to simply rely on technology
D. it's a danger to work long hours on computers
questions.explanation: 全文讨论了过度依赖科技的问题（网络自我诊断），最后作者要打病历，电脑却坏了，只能等IT部门来修，还调侃说也许该边等边吃微波香肠。这个幽默的结尾是为了证明单纯依赖科技是不明智的（it's unwise to simply rely on technology）。A工作中必须休息错误；B相信IT专业人员很重要错误；D长时间用电脑工作有危险错误。

items.title: 2013 湖北 阅读E
items.passage: A German study suggests that people who were too optimistic about their future actually faced greater risk of disability or death within 10 years than those pessimists who expected their future to be worse. The paper, published this March in Psychology and Aging, examined health and welfare surveys from roughly 40,000 Germans between ages 18 and 96. The surveys were conducted every year from 1993 to 2003. Survey respondents were asked to estimate their present and future life satisfaction on a scale of 0 to 10, among other questions. The researchers found that young adults (age 18 to 39) routinely overestimated their future life satisfaction, while middle-aged adults (age 40 to 64) more accurately predicted how they would feel in the future. Adults of 65 and older, however, were far more likely to underestimate their future life satisfaction. Not only did they feel more satisfied than they thought they would, the older pessimists seemed to suffer a lower ratio of disability and death for the study period. "We observed that being too optimistic in predicting a better future than actually observed was associated with a greater risk of disability and a greater risk of death within the following decade," wrote Frieder R. Lang, a professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. Lang and his colleagues believed that people who were pessimistic about their future may be more careful about their actions than people who expected a rosy future. "Seeing a dark future may encourage positive evaluations of the actual self and may contribute to taking improved precautions," the authors wrote. Surprisingly, compared with those in poor health or who had low incomes, respondents who enjoyed good health or income were associated with expecting a greater decline. Also, the researchers said that higher income was related to a greater risk of disability. The authors of the study noted that there were limitations to their conclusions. Illness, medical treatment and personal loss could also have driven health outcomes. However, the researchers said a pattern was clear. "We found that from early to late adulthood, individuals adapt their expectations of future life satisfaction from optimistic, to accurate, to pessimistic," the authors concluded.

questions.text: According to the study, who made the most accurate prediction of their future life satisfaction?
options: A. Optimistic adults.
B. Middle-aged adults.
C. Adults in poor health.
D. Adults of lower income.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'middle-aged adults (age 40 to 64) more accurately predicted how they would feel in the future'可知，中年人对未来生活满意度的预测最准确。A乐观的成年人错误；C健康状况差的成年人错误；D低收入的成年人错误。

questions.text: Pessimism may be positive in some way because it causes people ______.
options: A. to fully enjoy their present life
B. to estimate their contribution accurately
C. to take measures against potential risks
D. to value health more highly than wealth
questions.explanation: 根据第六段'people who were pessimistic about their future may be more careful about their actions'和第七段'Seeing a dark future may encourage positive evaluations of the actual self and may contribute to taking improved precautions'可知，悲观主义在某种程度上是积极的，因为它促使人们采取措施防范潜在风险（take improved precautions）。A充分享受现在的生活错误；B准确估计贡献错误；D更重视健康而非财富错误。

questions.text: How do people of higher income see their future?
options: A. They will earn less money.
B. They will become pessimistic.
C. They will suffer mental illness.
D. They will have less time to enjoy life.
questions.explanation: 根据第八段'respondents who enjoyed good health or income were associated with expecting a greater decline'可知，收入高的人预期更大的下降，即他们预期自己会赚更少的钱。B他们会变得悲观错误，是预期下降而非变得悲观；C他们会患精神疾病错误；D他们会有更少时间享受生活错误。

questions.text: What is the clear conclusion of the study?
options: A. Pessimism guarantees chances of survival.
B. Good financial condition leads to good health.
C. Medical treatment determines health outcomes.
D. Expectations of future life satisfaction decline with age.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'We found that from early to late adulthood, individuals adapt their expectations of future life satisfaction from optimistic, to accurate, to pessimistic'可知，研究的明确结论是：对未来生活满意度的预期随着年龄增长而下降（从乐观到准确再到悲观）。A悲观主义保证生存机会过于绝对；B良好的经济状况带来健康错误，高收入反而与更高残疾风险相关；C医疗决定健康结果错误，研究说疾病、治疗和个人损失都可能影响健康结果。

items.title: 2013 湖南 阅读A
items.passage: Planning a visit to the UK? Here we help with ways to cut your costs. AVOID BIG EVENTS Big sporting events, concerts and exhibitions can increase the cost of accommodation and make it harder to find a room. A standard double room at the Thistle Brighton on the final Friday of the Brighton Comedy Festival (19 Oct.) cost ￡169.15 at Booking.com. A week later, the same room cost ￡118.15. If you can be flexible and want to know dates to avoid — or you're looking for a big event to pass your time — check out sites such as Whatsonwhen.com, which allow you to search for events in the UK by city, date and category. STAY AWAY FROM THE STATION If traveling to your destination by train, you may want to find a good base close to the station, but you could end up paying more for the sake of convenience at the start of your holiday. Don't be too choosy about the part of town you stay in. Booking two months in advance, the cheapest room at Travelodge's Central Euston hotel in London for Saturday 22 September was ￡95.95. A room just a tube journey away at its Covent Garden hotel was ￡75.75. And at Farringdon, a double room cost just ￡62.95. LOOK AFTER YOURSELF Really central hotels in cities such as London, Edinburgh and Cardiff can cost a fortune, especially at weekends and during big events. As an alternative consider checking into a self-catering flat with its own kitchen. Often these flats are hidden away on the top floors of city centre buildings. A great example is the historic O'Neill Flat on Edinburgh's Royal Mile, available for ￡420 for five days in late September, with room for four adults. GET ON A BIKE London's 'Boris bikes' have attracted the most attention, but other cities also have similar programmes that let you rent a bicycle and explore at your own pace, saving you on public transport or car parking costs. Among the smaller cities with their own programmes are Newcastle (casual members pay around ￡1.50 for two hours) and Cardiff (free for up to 30 minutes, or ￡5 per day).

questions.text: The Brighton Comedy Festival is mentioned mainly to show big events may __________.
options: A. help travelers pass time
B. attract lots of travelers to the UK
C. allow travelers to make flexible plans
D. cause travelers to pay more for accommodation
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'Big sporting events, concerts and exhibitions can increase the cost of accommodation'以及Brighton Comedy Festival期间房价169.15英镑，一周后118.15英镑的对比可知，提到布莱顿喜剧节主要是为了说明大型活动可能导致旅行者支付更高的住宿费用。A帮助旅行者打发时间、B吸引很多旅行者到英国、C允许旅行者灵活安排计划均不是主要目的。

questions.text: "Farringdon" in Paragraph 5 is most probably __________.
options: A. a hotel away from the train station
B. the tube line to Covent Garden
C. an ideal holiday destination
D. the name of a travel agency
questions.explanation: 根据第五段，Central Euston酒店（靠近车站）95.95英镑，Covent Garden酒店（乘地铁一段距离）75.75英镑，Farringdon的双人间只要62.95英镑。结合标题'STAY AWAY FROM THE STATION'可知，Farringdon最可能是一家远离火车站的酒店。B到考文特花园的地铁线、C理想的度假目的地、D旅行社名称均不符合。

questions.text: The passage shows that the O'Neill Flat __________.
options: A. lies on the ground floor
B. is located in central London
C. provides cooking facilities for tourists
D. costs over ￡100 on average per day in late September
questions.explanation: 根据第六段'As an alternative consider checking into a self-catering flat with its own kitchen... A great example is the historic O'Neill Flat on Edinburgh's Royal Mile'可知，O'Neill Flat是自助公寓，为游客提供烹饪设施。A在一楼错误，原文说在顶层；B在伦敦市中心错误，在爱丁堡；D九月下旬平均每天超过100英镑错误，420英镑5天，平均每天84英镑。

questions.text: Cardiff's program allows a free bike for a maximum period of __________.
options: A. half an hour
B. one hour
C. one hour and a half
D. two hours
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Cardiff (free for up to 30 minutes, or ￡5 per day)'可知，加的夫的项目允许免费骑自行车最长30分钟，即半小时。B一小时、C一个半小时、D两小时均与原文不符。

questions.text: The main purpose of the passage is __________.
options: A. to tell visitors how to book in advance
B. to supply visitors with hotel information
C. to show visitors the importance of self-help
D. to offer visitors some money-saving tips
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Here we help with ways to cut your costs'以及四个小标题（避开大型活动、远离车站、选择自助公寓、骑自行车）可知，本文的主要目的是为游客提供一些省钱的建议。A告诉游客如何提前预订只是部分内容；B为游客提供酒店信息只是部分内容；C向游客展示自助的重要性不是核心目的。

items.title: 2013 湖南 阅读B
items.passage: In my living room, there is a plaque that advises me to "Bloom where you are planted." It reminds me of Dorothy. I got to know Dorothy in the early 1980s, when I was teaching Early Childhood Development through a program with Union College in Barbourville, Kentucky. The job responsibilities required occasional visits to the classroom of each teacher in the program. Dorothy stands out in my memory as one who "bloomed" in her remote area. Dorothy taught in a school in Harlan County, Kentucky, Appalachian Mountain area. To get to her school from the town of Harlan, I followed a road winding around the mountain. In the eight-mile journey, I crossed the same railroad track five times, giving the possibility of getting caught by the same train five times. Rather than feeling excited by this drive through the mountains, I found it depressing. The poverty level was shocking and the small shabby houses gave me the greatest feeling of hopelessness. From the moment of my arrival at the little school, all gloom disappeared. Upon arriving at Dorothy's classroom, I was greeted with smiling faces and treated like a queen. The children had been prepared to show me their latest projects. Dorothy told me with a big smile that they were serving poke greens salad and cornbread for "dinner" (lunch). In case you don't know, poke greens are a weed-type plant that grows wild, especially on poor ground. Dorothy never ran out of reports of exciting activities of her students. Her enthusiasm never cooled down. When it came time to sit for the testing and interviewing required to receive her Child Development Associate Certification, Dorothy was ready. She came to the assessment and passed in all areas. Afterward, she invited me to the one-and-only steak house in the area to celebrate her victory, as if she had received her Ph.D. degree. After the meal, she placed a little box containing an old pen in my hand. She said it was a family heirloom, but to me it is a treasured symbol of appreciation and pride that cannot be matched with things.

questions.text: "Early Childhood Development" in Paragraph 1 refers to __________.
options: A. a program directed by Dorothy
B. a course given by the author
C. an activity held by the students
D. an organization sponsored by Union college
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'I was teaching Early Childhood Development through a program with Union College in Barbourville, Kentucky'可知，Early Childhood Development是作者教授的一门课程。A由Dorothy指导的项目错误，Dorothy是项目中的教师；C学生举办的活动错误；D联合学院赞助的组织错误。

questions.text: In the journey, the author was most disappointed at seeing __________.
options: A. the long track
B. the poor houses
C. the same train
D. the winding road
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'The poverty level was shocking and the small shabby houses gave me the greatest feeling of hopelessness'可知，在旅途中，作者看到破旧的小房子最感到失望和绝望。A长长的铁轨、C同一列火车、D蜿蜒的道路都不是最让作者失望的。

questions.text: Upon arriving at the classroom, the author was cheered up by __________.
options: A. a warm welcome
B. the sight of poke greens
C. Dorothy's latest projects
D. a big dinner made for her
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'From the moment of my arrival at the little school, all gloom disappeared. Upon arriving at Dorothy's classroom, I was greeted with smiling faces and treated like a queen'可知，一到教室，作者被热情的欢迎（笑脸相迎、像女王一样被对待）所鼓舞。B看到poke greens、C Dorothy最新的项目、D为她做的丰盛晚餐都不是主要原因。

questions.text: What can we know about Dorothy from the last paragraph?
options: A. She was invited to a celebration at a restaurant.
B. She got a pen as a gift from the author.
C. She passed the required assessment.
D. She received her Ph.D. degree.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'She came to the assessment and passed in all areas'可知，Dorothy通过了所需的考核。A她被邀请去餐厅庆祝错误，是她邀请作者；B她从作者那里得到一支钢笔作为礼物错误，是她送给作者钢笔；D她获得了博士学位错误，原文说'as if she had received her Ph.D. degree'，是好像获得了博士学位，并非真的获得。

questions.text: What does the author mainly intend to tell us?
options: A. Whatever you do, you must do it carefully.
B. Whoever you are, you deserve equal treatment.
C. However poor you are, you have the right to education.
D. Wherever you are, you can accomplish your achievement.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'Bloom where you are planted'以及'Dorothy stands out in my memory as one who "bloomed" in her remote area'可知，作者主要想告诉我们：无论你在哪里，你都可以取得成就（在你被种植的地方开花）。A无论做什么都要仔细、B无论你是谁都应得到平等对待、C无论多穷都有受教育的权利均不是文章主旨。

items.title: 2013 湖南 阅读C
items.passage: It's such a happy-looking library, painted yellow, decorated with palm-tree stickers and sheltered from the Florida sun by its own roof. About the size of a microwave oven, it's pedestrian-friendly, too, waiting for book lovers next to a sidewalk in Palm Beach Country Estates, along the northern boundary of Palm Beach Gardens. It's a library built with love. A year ago, shortly after Janey Henriksen saw a Brian Williams report about the Little Free Library organization, a Wisconsin-based nonprofit that aims to promote literacy and build a sense of community in a neighborhood by making books freely available, she announced to her family of four, "That's what we're going to do for our spring break!" Son Austin, now a 10th-grader, didn't see the point of building a library that resembles a mailbox. But Janey insisted, and husband Peter unwillingly got to work. The 51-year-old owner of a ship supply company modified a small wooden house that he'd built years earlier for daughter Abbie's toy horses, and made a door of glass. After adding the library's final touches, the family hung a signboard on the front, instructing users to "take a book, return a book," and making the Henriksen library, now one of several hundred like it nationwide and among more than 2,500 in the world, the only Little Free Library in Palm Beach County. They stocked it with 20 or so books they'd already read, a mix of science fiction, reference titles, novels and kids' favorites. "I told them, keep in mind that you might not see it again," said Janey, a stay-at-home mom. Since then, the collection keeps replenishing itself, thanks to ongoing donations from borrowers. The library now gets an average of five visits a day. The project's best payoff, says Peter, are the thank-you notes left behind. "We had no idea in the beginning that it would be so popular."

questions.text: In what way is the library "pedestrian-friendly"?
options: A. It owns a yellow roof.
B. It stands near a sidewalk.
C. It protects book lovers from the sun.
D. It uses palm-tree stickers as decorations.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'it's pedestrian-friendly, too, waiting for book lovers next to a sidewalk in Palm Beach Country Estates'可知，这个图书馆对行人友好是因为它位于人行道旁边。A它有黄色屋顶、C它保护爱书人免受阳光照射、D它用棕榈树贴纸装饰都不是pedestrian-friendly的含义。

questions.text: Janey got the idea to build a library from __________.
options: A. a visit to Brian Williams
B. a spring break with her family
C. a book sent by one of her neighbors
D. a report on a Wisconsin-based organization
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'shortly after Janey Henriksen saw a Brian Williams report about the Little Free Library organization, a Wisconsin-based nonprofit'可知，Janey建图书馆的想法来自关于一个威斯康星州组织的报道。A拜访Brian Williams错误，是看了他的报道；B和家人春假错误，春假是实施时间；C邻居送的一本书错误。

questions.text: The library was built __________.
options: A. by a ship supply company
B. on the basis of toy horses
C. like a mailbox
D. with glass
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'Son Austin... didn't see the point of building a library that resembles a mailbox'可知，这个图书馆建得像一个邮箱。A由船舶供应公司建造错误，Peter是该公司老板，是他个人建造的；B在玩具马基础上错误，是改造了为玩具马建的小木屋；D用玻璃建造错误，只是门是玻璃的。

questions.text: What can we infer about the signboard?
options: A. It was made by a user of the library.
B. It marked a final touch to the library.
C. It aimed at making the library last long.
D. It indicated the library was a family property.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段'instructing users to "take a book, return a book"'可知，牌子上写着"拿一本书，还一本书"，目的是让图书馆的书不断循环补充，从而使图书馆长久存在。A由图书馆用户制作错误，是这家人挂的；B标志着图书馆的最后装点不是推断的核心；D表明图书馆是家庭财产错误，这是免费公共图书馆。

questions.text: The passage tells us that the users __________.
options: A. donate books to the library
B. get paid to collect books for the library
C. receive thank-you notes for using the library
D. visit the library over 5 times on average daily
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段'the collection keeps replenishing itself, thanks to ongoing donations from borrowers'可知，用户（借阅者）不断向图书馆捐赠书籍，使藏书不断补充。B为图书馆收集书籍获得报酬错误；C使用图书馆收到感谢信错误，是用户留下感谢信；D平均每天访问超过5次错误，原文是平均每天5次访问，不是每个用户。

items.title: 2013 福建 阅读A
items.passage: When I was 12, all I wanted was a signet ring. They were the "in" thing and it seemed every girl except me had one. On my 13th birthday, my Mum gave me a signet ring with my initials carved into it. I was in heaven. What made it even more special was that it was about the only thing that wasn't being "replaced". We'd been burnt out in fires that swept through our area earlier that year and had lost everything — so most of the "new" stuff we got was really just to replace what we'd lost. But not my ring. My ring was new. Then, only one month later, I lost it. I took it off before bed and it was missing in the morning. I was sad and searched everywhere for it. But it seemed to have disappeared. Eventually, I gave up and stopped looking for it. And two years later, we sold the house and moved away. Years passed, and a couple of moves later, I was visiting my parents' when Mum told me that she had something for me. It wasn't my birthday, nor was it Easter or Christmas or any other gift-giving occasion. Mum noticed my questioning look. "You'll recognize this one," she said, smiling. Then she handed me a small ring box. I took it from her and opened it to find my beautiful signet ring inside. The family who had bought our house 13 years earlier had recently decided to do some redecorations, which included replacing the carpets. When they pulled the carpet up in my old bedroom, they found the ring. As it had my initials carved into it, they realized who owned the ring. They'd had it professionally cleaned up by a jeweler before sending it to my mother. And it still fits me.

questions.text: The underlined word "in" in the first paragraph probably means "_____".
options: A. fashionable
B. available
C. practical
D. renewable
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'They were the "in" thing and it seemed every girl except me had one'可知，图章戒指是'in'东西，似乎除了作者每个女孩都有一枚，说明这是流行的、时髦的东西。in在此表示'流行的、时髦的'，与fashionable同义。available可获得的；practical实用的；renewable可再生的均不符合语境。

questions.text: When she got the ring back, the writer was about _____.
options: A. 13 years old
B. 15 years old
C. 26 years old
D. 28 years old
questions.explanation: 作者13岁生日得到戒指，一个月后丢失，两年后（15岁）卖房搬走。买房子的那家人13年后重新装修时发现戒指。所以作者找回戒指时约15+13=28岁。A13岁是得到戒指时；B15岁是搬家时；C26岁计算错误。

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
options: A. The writer's family moved several times.
B. The writer never stopped looking for her ring.
C. The writer's ring was cleaned up by the new house owner.
D. The writer lost her ring in the morning when she took it off.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'Years passed, and a couple of moves later'可知，作者一家搬了好几次家，A正确。B作者从未停止寻找戒指错误，原文'Eventually, I gave up and stopped looking for it'；C戒指被新房东清洗错误，原文'They'd had it professionally cleaned up by a jeweler'，是珠宝商清洗的；D作者早上摘戒指时丢失错误，原文'I took it off before bed and it was missing in the morning'，是睡前摘的，早上发现不见了。

questions.text: What would be the best title for the passage?
options: A. My New Ring
B. Lost and Found
C. Lost and Replaced
D. An Expensive Ring
questions.explanation: 全文围绕一枚图章戒指的丢失与找回展开，13岁得到，一个月后丢失，13年后失而复得，所以最佳标题是Lost and Found（失而复得）。A我的新戒指只涉及开头；C丢失和替换错误，戒指不是被替换的；D一枚昂贵的戒指错误，文章未强调昂贵。

items.title: 2013 福建 阅读B
items.passage: Your glasses may someday replace your smartphone, and some New Yorkers are ready for the switch. Some in the city can't wait to try them on and use the maps and GPS that the futuristic eyewear is likely to include. "I'd use it if I were hanging out with friends at 3 a.m. and going to the bar and wanted to see what was open," said Walter Choo, 40, of Fort Greene. The smartphone-like glasses will likely come out this year and cost between $250 and $600, the Times said, possibly including a variation of augmented reality, a technology already available on smartphones and tablets that overlays information onto the screen about one's surroundings. So, for example, if you were walking down a street, indicators would pop up showing you the nearest coffee shop or directions could be plotted out and come into view right on the sidewalk in front of you. "As far as a mainstream consumer product, this just isn't something anybody needs," said Sam Biddle, who writes for Gizmodo.com. "We're accustomed to having one thing in our pocket to do all these things," he added, "and the average consumer isn't gonna be able to afford another device that's hundreds and hundreds of dollars." 9to5Google publisher Seth Weintraub, who has been reporting on the smartphone-like glasses since late last year, said he is confident that this type of wearable device will eventually be as common as smartphones. "It's just like smartphones 10 years ago," Weintraub said. "A few people started getting emails on their phones, and people thought that was crazy. Same kind of thing. We see people bending their heads to look at their smartphones, and it's unnatural," he said. "There's gonna be improvements to that, and this a step there."

questions.text: One of the possible functions of the smartphone-like glasses is to ____.
options: A. program the opening hours of a bar
B. supply you with a picture of the future
C. provide information about your surroundings
D. update the maps and GPS in your smartphones
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'possibly including a variation of augmented reality, a technology... that overlays information onto the screen about one's surroundings'可知，这种智能眼镜的一个可能功能是提供关于周围环境的信息。A设定酒吧营业时间错误；B提供未来的图片错误；D更新智能手机中的地图和GPS错误，是眼镜本身包含地图和GPS。

questions.text: The underlined phrase "pop up" in the third paragraph probably means " ____".
options: A. develop rapidly
B. get round quickly
C. appear immediately
D. go over automatically
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'if you were walking down a street, indicators would pop up showing you the nearest coffee shop'可知，当你走在街上时，指示器会pop up显示最近的咖啡店。pop up在此表示'突然出现、弹出'，与appear immediately同义。develop rapidly快速发展；get round quickly迅速传开；go over automatically自动复习均不符合语境。

questions.text: According to Sam Biddle, the smartphone-like glasses are ____.
options: A. necessary for teenagers
B. attractive to New Yorkers
C. available to people worldwide
D. expensive for average consumers
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'the average consumer isn't gonna be able to afford another device that's hundreds and hundreds of dollars'可知，Sam Biddle认为这种智能眼镜对普通消费者来说太贵了。A对青少年必要错误，他说这不是任何人都需要的；B对纽约人有吸引力不是Sam Biddle的观点；C全世界人都能买到错误。

questions.text: We can learn from the last two paragraphs that the smartphone-like glasses ____.
options: A. may have a potential market
B. are as common as smartphones
C. are popular among young adults
D. will be improved by a new technology
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段'Seth Weintraub... is confident that this type of wearable device will eventually be as common as smartphones'和最后一段把它比作10年前的智能手机可知，这种智能眼镜可能有潜在的市场。B和智能手机一样普遍错误，是最终会，不是现在；C在年轻人中流行未提及；D将被新技术改进错误，是这种眼镜本身是对低头看手机的改进。

items.title: 2013 福建 阅读C
items.passage: This is What a REAL Silver Dollar Looks Like If you trust in the yen, the euro, and the dollar... stop reading. Because this is a story about the silver coin EVERYBODY wants. You read the headlines. You know that troubled economic times have put global currency on a rollercoaster ride. But millions have found a smarter way to build long-term value with high-grade collectable silver. And right now, those people are lining up to secure some of the last 2012 U.S. Mint Silver Eagles, America's Newest Silver Eagle Dollars. Today, you can graduate to the front of that line. Buy now and you can own these brilliant uncirculated Silver Dollars for only $38.95! You Can't Afford to Lose Why are we releasing this silver dollar for such a remarkable price? Because we want to introduce you to what hundreds of thousands of smart collectors and satisfied customers have known since 1984 — New York Mint is the place to find the world's finest high-grade coins. That's why we're offering you this Brilliant Uncirculated 2012 U.S. Silver Eagle for as little as $37.45 (plus s/h). Timing is Everything Our advice? Keep this to yourself. Because the more people who know about this offer, the worse it is for you. Demand for Silver Eagles in 2011 broke records. Experts predict that 2012 Silver Eagles may break them all over again. Due to rapid changes in the price of silver, prices may be higher or lower and are subject to change without notice. Supplies are limited. Call immediately to add these Silver Eagles to your holdings before it's too late. Offer Limited to 40 per household 2012 American Silver Eagle Coin Your cost: 1-4 Coins: $38.95 each + s/h 5-9 Coins: $38.45 each + s/h 10-19 Coins: $37.95 each + s/h 20-40 Coins: $37.45 each + s/h Note: $10 s/h (shipping and handling) for each purchase For fastest service, call toll-free 24 hours a day: 1-888-201-7143 Offer Code: ASE177-04

questions.text: What is stressed in the ad?
options: A. The coin is of high quality and worth collecting.
B. The coin can be circulated as a currency.
C. Limited supplies guarantee a stable price of the coin.
D. Demand for the coin is bound to break records.
questions.explanation: 广告标题'This is What a REAL Silver Dollar Looks Like'，正文强调'high-grade collectable silver'、'world's finest high-grade coins'、'Brilliant Uncirculated'，可知广告强调这枚银币品质优良、值得收藏。B可以作为货币流通错误，这是收藏级未流通银币；C有限供应保证价格稳定错误，原文说价格可能变动；D需求注定破纪录过于绝对，原文是专家预测可能破纪录。

questions.text: If you buy six 2012 U.S. Mint Silver Eagles by post, you should pay at least ____.
questions.explanation: 根据价格表，5-9枚每枚38.45美元，6枚就是38.45×6=230.7美元，再加每次购买10美元运费和手续费，总共230.7+10=240.7美元。A230.7美元没加运费；B233.7计算错误；D243.7计算错误。

questions.text: The ad strongly encourages people to purchase the silver coins by ____.
options: A. shopping online
B. making a phone call
C. lining up in front of the stores
D. writing to the company
questions.explanation: 根据最后'For fastest service, call toll-free 24 hours a day: 1-888-201-7143'以及'Call immediately to add these Silver Eagles to your holdings before it's too late'可知，广告强烈鼓励人们通过打电话购买银币。A网上购物未提及；C在商店前排队错误，原文'lining up'是比喻，指人们争相购买；D写信给公司未提及。

items.title: 2013 福建 阅读D
items.passage: Pride and Prejudice for the Modern Woman Let us imagine how Pride and Prejudice, Jane Austen's most famous work, might be updated, 200 years on. Austen's popularity is rooted in her intelligence. But today she would certainly have had a very different life, as would her characters. Here's my own suggestion... It is a truth finally and universally acknowledged that a single woman with brains deserves to have equal opportunities to men, however disadvantaged she may feel by sexism. "My dear husband," said his hopeful wife one day, "have you heard that the local store, standing empty for so long, is taken over by a bright young businesswoman?" Her dull and indifferent husband replied that he had not. "But it is, it is," she replied excitedly. Mr Dull-Husband made no reply. "Don't you want to know her plans?" she cried with some impatience. "Well, clearly you think it matters to your silly little head... so I'd better listen." "Well, my dear, the rumour is that she has already set up a string of successful businesses in northern England, though how a woman can know anything about that is beyond me. She will move in herself next month." "What is her name?" "Bingley." "Is she married or single?" "What a question! And none of your business. But her coming will be a fine thing for our five boys." "How so? How can it possibly affect them?" "My dear love, those lazy boys need something to wake them up. There are bound to be jobs going." "Is that her point in settling here? Surely as a woman she has simply taken a fancy to the place." "Nonsense, my love, how little you've noticed the world has changed. She's got a first-rate degree and some sort of business qualification, I'm told. She surely needs one of our boys! Perhaps you might give her a call." "Me? No. Perhaps you can take an interest. You still have your looks, after all. She may even offer you a job." "Oh, that's not likely. These new chances belong to the younger generation. But now you mention it, I think I'll go along all the same." And Mrs Bennet went along. That was 10 years ago. She is now managing director of a FTSE-listed company. ... It would remain the case, of course, that Mrs Bennet would be one of very few women on the company board, that her salary would be lower than her male colleagues, her bonus of a more "female" dimension and her lifespan among the city's business leaders shorter than theirs. Still, she'd no doubt have enjoyed Davos — and might even have hobnobbed with influential figures.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
options: A. Austen was born 200 years ago.
B. Austen rewrote Pride and Prejudice.
C. Austen's success lies in her wisdom.
D. Austen's updated work gains popularity.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'Austen's popularity is rooted in her intelligence'可知，奥斯汀的成功在于她的智慧（intelligence与wisdom同义），C正确。A奥斯汀200年前出生错误，原文是'200 years on'指《傲慢与偏见》出版200年后；B奥斯汀重写了《傲慢与偏见》错误，是作者在想象如何更新；D奥斯汀更新后的作品受欢迎错误，这只是作者的设想。

questions.text: The underlined part in the passage suggests that Mrs Bennet ____.
options: A. had mixed feelings of admiration and surprise about Bingley
B. felt kind of worried and doubtful about Bingley
C. was extremely anxious to meet Bingley
D. had a great curiosity about Bingley
questions.explanation: 划线部分'though how a woman can know anything about that is beyond me'意为'不过一个女人怎么会懂这些我就不明白了'，一方面贝内特太太对宾利在英格兰北部创办了一系列成功企业表示钦佩，另一方面又对女人能懂商业表示惊讶，所以是钦佩和惊讶交织的复杂情感。B担心和怀疑错误；C极度渴望见宾利错误；D对宾利很好奇不全面，没有体现钦佩。

questions.text: In the eyes of Mrs Bennet, Bingley surely needed one of their boys to ____.
options: A. get married to
B. work for her
C. help her move in
D. take over her store
questions.explanation: 根据贝内特太太的话'those lazy boys need something to wake them up. There are bound to be jobs going'以及'She surely needs one of our boys!'可知，在贝内特太太看来，宾利肯定需要他们的一个儿子为她工作。A结婚错误；C帮她搬进来错误；D接管她的商店错误。

questions.text: What does the writer intend to tell us?
options: A. Women with brains can also be as successful as men.
B. Women have to pay a high price for success.
C. A judgment must be made free from prejudice.
D. Sex discrimination still exists nowadays.
questions.explanation: 文章结尾指出，即使贝内特太太成为了董事总经理，她仍然是董事会中极少数女性之一，薪水低于男性同事，奖金更'女性化'，任期更短，说明作者想告诉我们性别歧视在当今依然存在。A有头脑的女性也能和男性一样成功只是部分内容，不是核心；B女性必须为成功付出高昂代价不是核心；C判断必须不带偏见不是文章主旨。

items.title: 2013 福建 阅读E
items.passage: A MENTORING program is giving life changing opportunities to Banbury youth. Young Inspirations was founded two years ago to provide mentoring sessions for students and unemployed young adults aged 11 to 21. Alex Goldberg, the program's founder, said: "We set up Young Inspirations because we wanted to give young people experiences which will potentially be life changing and broaden their outlook." "We try to create work experience opportunities that will really make a difference to our youth. For example, we've secured internships with world-famous firms such as Honda." "At a time of funding cutbacks where schools are finding it more and more difficult to offer this kind of mentoring, it is extremely important that these opportunities are available both to help youth with their school work and grades and to give them opportunities which may help shape their futures." Kieran Hepburn, 14, is one of a group of Banbury youth who has benefited from the program so far. In October the Banbury School pupil was accompanied by Young Inspirations staff to Paris where he was an observer at the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's (UNESCO) International Youth Forum. The event was held for young people from around the world, to seek their views on how the future of youth and education should look. Kieran joined several hundred observers mostly in their 20s and was the only UK school pupil to attend the event. Kieran thinks the trip was a life changing experience. "Before we left I didn't quite know what to make of it but when we got there we didn't stop, it was amazing," he said, "We went to three or four hours of debates each day and then did something cultural each afternoon." The main theme of the forum was how youth can drive change in political and public life. It dealt with issues such as drug abuse, violence and unemployment. Kieran said: "It has really helped me to improve my confidence and social skills as well as my school grades and I was voted most improved pupil at school in August." The Young Inspirations mentoring sessions take place each Friday in Banbury. For details visit www.younginspirations.com.

questions.text: The Young Inspirations mentoring program aims to _____.
options: A. train staff for world-famous firms
B. offer job opportunities to young adults
C. provide youth with unique experiences
D. equip the unemployed with different skills
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'We set up Young Inspirations because we wanted to give young people experiences which will potentially be life changing and broaden their outlook'可知，这个项目旨在为年轻人提供独特的、可能改变人生的经历。A为世界知名公司培训员工错误；B为年轻人提供工作机会不准确，是提供实习和经历；D为失业者配备不同技能不全面，项目对象包括学生和失业青年。

questions.text: According to Alex Goldberg, it is difficult for schools to offer the mentoring due to _____.
options: A. the lack of support from firms
B. the cultural differences
C. the effect of unemployment
D. the shortage of money
questions.explanation: 根据第五段'At a time of funding cutbacks where schools are finding it more and more difficult to offer this kind of mentoring'可知，学校难以提供这种辅导是因为经费削减（funding cutbacks），即资金短缺。A缺乏公司支持错误；B文化差异错误；C失业的影响错误。

questions.text: According to the passage, the forum focused on how youth can ____.
options: A. build up their confidence at school
B. find work experience opportunities
C. improve their social skills for the future
D. play an active role in the change of society
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第三段'The main theme of the forum was how youth can drive change in political and public life'可知，论坛的主题是青年如何推动政治和公共生活的变革，即在社会变革中发挥积极作用。A在学校建立自信是Kieran的收获，不是论坛主题；B找工作经验机会是项目内容，不是论坛主题；C提高社交技能是Kieran的收获。

questions.text: We can learn from the passage that _____.
options: A. the visit to the United Kingdom was amazing
B. Kieran has made great progress in many aspects
C. the youth have found a way to solve their problems
D. the mentoring sessions are held every day except Friday
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段'It has really helped me to improve my confidence and social skills as well as my school grades and I was voted most improved pupil at school in August'可知，Kieran在自信心、社交技能和学习成绩等多个方面都取得了很大进步。A访问英国很精彩错误，是去巴黎；C年轻人找到了解决问题的方法过于绝对；D辅导课除周五外每天举行错误，原文是每周五举行。

questions.text: What would be the best title for the passage?
options: A. Alex Goldberg, Founder of Young Inspirations
B. Young People Find a World of Opportunity
C. Kieran, Banbury School Pupil to Paris
D. Debates Help Youth with Their Grades
questions.explanation: 全文介绍了Young Inspirations导师制项目为年轻人提供改变人生的机会，包括实习机会、参加国际青年论坛等，让年轻人发现了一个充满机会的世界，所以最佳标题是Young People Find a World of Opportunity。A只提到创始人，不全面；C只提到Kieran一个例子，不全面；D辩论帮助年轻人提高成绩只是部分内容。

items.title: 2013 辽宁 阅读A
items.passage: China is a land of bicycles. At least it was back in 1992 when I travelled the country. Back then everyone seemed to be riding a bicycle. Millions of them, all black. Cars were rare. Yet since my arrival in Beijing last year, I've found the opposite is true. There were millions of cars. However, people still use their bicycles to get around. For many, it's the easiest and cheapest way to travel today. Bicycles also come in different colours — silver, green, red, blue, yellow, whatever you want. It's fun watching people biking. They rush quickly through crossroads, move skillfully through traffic, and ride even on sidewalks. Bicycles allow people the freedom to move about that cars just can't provide. Eager to be part of this aspect of Chinese culture, I decided to buy a bicycle. Great weather accompanied my great buy. I immediately jumped up on my bicycle seat and started to ride. My first ride home was orderly. To be safe, I stayed with a pack of bikers while cars on the streets came running swiftly out of nowhere at times. I didn't want to get hit. So I took the ride carefully. Crossing the streets was the biggest problem. It was a lot like crossing a major highway back in the United States. The streets here were wide, so crossing took time, skill and a little bit of luck. I finally made it home. The feeling on the bicycle was amazing. The air hitting my face and going through my hair was wonderful. I was sitting on top of the world as I passed by places and people. Biking made me feel alive.

questions.text: According to the author, why are bicycles still popular in China today?
options: A. Because they are traditional and safe.
B. Because they are convenient and inexpensive.
C. Because they are colourful and available.
D. Because they are fast and environment friendly.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段For many, it's the easiest and cheapest way to travel today可知，自行车在中国仍然流行是因为它是最方便、最便宜的出行方式，即方便且便宜。A传统且安全错误；C多彩且可获得不是主要原因；D快且环保未提及。

questions.text: The author decided to buy a bicycle because he intended ______.
options: A. to ride for fun
B. to use for transport
C. to experience local culture
D. to improve his riding skills
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Eager to be part of this aspect of Chinese culture, I decided to buy a bicycle可知，作者决定买自行车是因为渴望体验中国文化的这一方面。A为了好玩骑车错误；B用作交通工具错误；D提高骑车技巧错误。

questions.text: How did the author feel about his street crossing?
options: A. It was boring.
B. It was difficult.
C. It was lively.
D. It was wonderful.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段Crossing the streets was the biggest problem... The streets here were wide, so crossing took time, skill and a little bit of luck可知，作者觉得过马路是最大的问题，需要时间、技巧和运气，即过马路很困难。A无聊错误；C生动错误；D精彩错误。

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the author's biking experience?
options: A. The author enjoyed showing off his biking skill.
B. The author was annoyed by the air while riding.
C. The author was praised by the other bikers.
D. The author took great pleasure in biking.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段The feeling on the bicycle was amazing. The air hitting my face... was wonderful. I was sitting on top of the world... Biking made me feel alive可知，作者从骑自行车中获得了极大的乐趣。A喜欢炫耀骑车技巧错误；B被风吹得很烦错误，原文说风吹在脸上很棒；C被其他骑车人表扬未提及。

items.title: 2013 辽宁 阅读B
items.passage: Going green seems to be a fad for a lot of people these days. Whether that is good or bad, we can't really say, but for the two of us, going green is not a fad but a lifestyle. On April 22, 2011, we decided to be green every single day for an entire year. This meant doing 365 different things, and it also meant challenging ourselves to go green beyond the easy things. Rather than recycle and reduce our energy, we had to think of 365 different things to do and this was no easy task. With the idea of going green every single day a year, Our Green Year started. My wife and I decided to educate people about how they could go green in their lives and hoped we could show people all green things that could be done to help the environment. We wanted to push the message that every little bit helps. Over the course of Our Green Year, we completely changed our lifestyles. We now shop at organic stores. We consume less meat, choosing green food. We have greatly reduced our buying we don't need. We have given away half of what we owned through websites. Our home is kept clean by vinegar and lemon juice, with no chemical cleaners. We make our own butter, enjoying the smell of home-made fresh bread. In our home office anyone caught doing something ungreen might be punished. Our minds have been changed by Our Green Year. We are grateful for the chance to have been able to go green and educate others. We believe that we do have the power to change things and help our planet.

questions.text: What might be the best title for the passage?
options: A. Going green
B. Protecting the planet
C. Keeping Open-Minded
D. Celebrating Our Green Year
questions.explanation: 全文围绕这对夫妇的「绿色一年」环保活动展开，讲述他们如何践行环保生活方式，所以最佳标题是Going green（践行环保）。B保护地球太宽泛；C保持开放心态与主题无关；D庆祝我们的绿色一年只是部分内容，不是核心。

questions.text: It was difficult for the couple to live a green life for the whole year because ______.
options: A. they were expected to follow the green fad
B. they didn't know how to educate other people
C. they were unwilling to reduce their energy
D. they needed to perform unusual green tasks
questions.explanation: 根据第二段it also meant challenging ourselves to go green beyond the easy things. Rather than recycle and reduce our energy, we had to think of 365 different things to do and this was no easy task可知，这对夫妇整年过环保生活很困难是因为他们需要做不寻常的环保任务，超越简单的回收和节能。A被期望追随环保时尚错误；B不知道如何教育他人错误；C不愿意减少能源错误。

questions.text: What did the couple do over the course of Our Green Year?
options: A. They tried to get out of their ungreen habits.
B. They ignored others' ungreen behaviour.
C. They chose better chemical cleaners.
D. They sold their home-made food.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段we completely changed our lifestyles... We have greatly reduced our buying we don't need... Our home is kept clean by vinegar and lemon juice, with no chemical cleaners... In our home office anyone caught doing something ungreen might be punished可知，这对夫妇在绿色一年中努力摆脱不环保的习惯。B忽视他人不环保行为错误，他们会惩罚不环保的人；C选择更好的化学清洁剂错误，他们不用化学清洁剂；D卖自制食物错误，他们自己做黄油和面包，不是卖。

questions.text: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: A. The government will give support to the green project.
B. The couple may continue their project in the future.
C. Some people disagree with the couple's green ideas.
D. Our Green Year is becoming a national campaign.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Our minds have been changed by Our Green Year. We are grateful for the chance to have been able to go green and educate others. We believe that we do have the power to change things and help our planet可知，这对夫妇的思想被改变了，感谢有机会环保并教育他人，相信自己有能力改变事情、帮助地球，可以推断他们未来可能会继续这个项目。A政府将支持环保项目未提及；C有些人不同意这对夫妇的环保想法未提及；D绿色一年正在成为全国性运动未提及。

items.title: 2013 辽宁 阅读C
items.passage: Here is an astonishing and significant fact: Mental work alone can't make us tired. It sounds absurd. But a few years ago, scientists tried to find out how long the human brain could labor without reaching a stage of fatigue. To the amazement of these scientists, they discovered that blood passing through the brain, when it is active, shows no fatigue at all! If we took a drop of blood from a day labourer, we could find it full of fatigue toxins and fatigue products. But if we took blood from the brain of Albert Einstein, it would show no fatigue toxins at the end of the day. So far as the brain is concerned, it can work as well and swiftly at the end of eight or even twelve hours of efforts as at the beginning. The brain is totally tireless. So what makes us tired? Some scientists declare that most of our fatigue comes from our mental and emotional attitudes. One of England's most outstanding scientists, J.A. Hadfield, says, "The greater part of the fatigue from which we suffer is of mental origin. In fact, fatigue of purely physical origin is rare." Dr. Brill, a famous American scientist, goes even further. He declares, "One hundred percent of the fatigue of a sitting worker in good health is due to emotional problems." What kinds of emotions make sitting workers tired? Joy? Satisfaction? No! A feeling of being bored, anger, anxiety, tenseness, worry, a feeling of not being appreciated — those are emotions that tire sitting workers. Hard work by itself seldom causes fatigue. We get tired because our emotions produce nervousness in the body.

questions.text: What surprised the scientists a few years ago?
options: A. Fatigue toxins could hardly be found in a labourer's blood.
B. Albert Einstein didn't feel worn out after a day's work.
C. The brain could work for many hours without fatigue.
D. A mental worker's blood was filled with fatigue toxins.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段To the amazement of these scientists, they discovered that blood passing through the brain, when it is active, shows no fatigue at all以及第二段it can work as well and swiftly at the end of eight or even twelve hours of efforts as at the beginning. The brain is totally tireless可知，让科学家惊讶的是大脑可以工作很多小时而不疲劳。A劳动者血液中几乎找不到疲劳毒素错误，原文说劳动者血液中充满疲劳毒素；B爱因斯坦工作一天后不觉得累不是科学家惊讶的核心；D脑力工作者的血液充满疲劳毒素错误，大脑的血液没有疲劳毒素。

questions.text: According to the author, which of the following can make sitting workers tired?
options: A. Challenging mental work.
B. Unpleasant emotions.
C. Endless tasks.
D. Physical labor.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段A feeling of being bored, anger, anxiety, tenseness, worry, a feeling of not being appreciated — those are emotions that tire sitting workers可知，让久坐工作者疲劳的是不愉快的情感（无聊、愤怒、焦虑、紧张、担忧、不被欣赏）。A有挑战性的脑力工作错误，脑力工作本身不导致疲劳；C无尽的任务未提及；D体力劳动错误，纯粹身体原因的疲劳很少见。

questions.text: What's the author's attitude towards the scientists' ideas?
options: A. He agrees with them.
B. He doubts them.
C. He argues against them.
D. He hesitates to accept them.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Hard work by itself seldom causes fatigue. We get tired because our emotions produce nervousness in the body可知，作者认同科学家的观点，认为努力工作本身很少导致疲劳，我们疲劳是因为情感在身体中产生了紧张。B怀疑、C反对、D犹豫接受均与作者态度不符。

questions.text: We can infer from the passage that in order to stay energetic, sitting workers need to ______.
options: A. have some good blood
B. enjoy their work
C. exercise regularly
D. discover fatigue toxins
questions.explanation: 根据文章，让久坐工作者疲劳的是不愉快的情感（无聊、愤怒、焦虑、紧张、担忧、不被欣赏），所以为了保持精力充沛，久坐工作者需要享受他们的工作，保持积极的情感。A有好血液错误；C定期锻炼未提及；D发现疲劳毒素错误。

items.title: 2013 辽宁 阅读D
items.passage: "Indeed," George Washington wrote in his diary in 1785, "some kind of fly, or bug, had begun to eat the leaves before I left home." But the father of America was not the father of bug. When Washington wrote that, Englishmen had been referring to insects as bugs for more than a century, and Americans had already created lightning-bug. But the English were soon to stop using the bugs in their language, leaving it to be the Americans to call a bug a bug in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The American bug could also be a person, referring to someone who was crazy about a particular activity. Although fan became the usual term, sports fans used to be called racing bugs, baseball bugs and the like. Or the bug could be a small machine or object, for example, a bug-shaped car. The bug could also be a burglar alarm, from which comes the expression to bug, that is, "to install an alarm". Now it means a small piece of equipment that people use for listening secretly to others' conversations. Since the 1840s, to bug has long meant "to cheat", and since the 1940s it has been annoying. We also know the bug as a flaw in a computer program or other design. That meaning dates back to the time of Thomas Edison. In 1878 he explained bugs as "little problems and difficulties" that required months of study and labor to overcome in developing a successful product. In 1889 it was recorded that Edison "had been up the two previous nights discovering 'a bug' in his invented record player."

questions.text: We learn from Paragraph 1 that ______.
options: A. Americans had difficulty in learning to use the word bug.
B. George Washington was the first person to call the insect a bug.
C. the word bug was still popularly used in England in the nineteenth century.
D. both the Englishmen and Americans used the word bug in the eighteenth century.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段When Washington wrote that (1785), Englishmen had been referring to insects as bugs for more than a century, and Americans had already created lightning-bug可知，在18世纪，英国人和美国人都使用bug这个词。A美国人学用bug有困难错误；B华盛顿是第一个称昆虫为bug的人错误，原文说他不是bug之父；C19世纪bug在英国仍然流行错误，原文说英国人很快停止使用bug。

questions.text: What does the word flaw in the last paragraph mean?
options: A. Explanation.
B. Finding.
C. Origin.
D. Fault.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段We also know the bug as a flaw in a computer program or other design以及爱迪生把bugs解释为little problems and difficulties可知，flaw在此表示缺陷、故障，与fault同义。Explanation解释；Finding发现；Origin起源均不符合。

questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ______.
options: A. the misunderstanding of the word bug
B. the development of the word bug
C. the public views of the word bug
D. the special characteristics of the word bug
questions.explanation: 全文按时间顺序介绍了bug这个词从18世纪到现在的词义演变，包括指昆虫、指人、指机器/物品、指窃听/欺骗/使烦恼、指计算机程序缺陷等，所以文章主要关注bug这个词的发展演变。A对bug这个词的误解错误；C公众对bug这个词的看法错误；Dbug这个词的特殊特征不全面。

items.title: 2013 重庆 阅读A
items.passage: The morning had been a disaster. My tooth was aching. And I'd been in an argument with a friend. Her words still hurt: "The trouble with you is that you won't put yourself in my place. Can't you see things from my point of view?" I shook my head stubbornly — and felt the ache in my tooth. I'd thought I could hold out till my dentist came back from holiday, but the pain was really unbearable. I started calling the dentists in the phone book, but no one could see me immediately. Finally, at about lunchtime, I got lucky. "If you come by right now," the receptionist said, "the dentist will fit you in." I took my purse and keys and rushed to my car. But suddenly I began to doubt about the dentist. What kind of dentist would be so eager to treat someone at such short notice? Why wasn't he as busy as the others? In the dentist's office, I sat down and looked around. I saw nothing but the bare walls and I became even more worried. The assistant noticed my nervousness and placed her warm hand over my ice-cold one. When I told her my fears, she laughed and said, "Don't worry. The dentist is very good." "How long do I have to wait for him?" I asked impatiently. "Come on, he is coming. Just lie down and relax. And enjoy the artwork," the assistant said. "The artwork?" I was puzzled. The chair went back. Suddenly I smiled. There was a beautiful picture, right where I could enjoy it: on the ceiling. How considerate the dentist was! At that moment, I began to understand what my friend meant by her words. What a relief!

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the author's feeling that morning?
options: A. Cheerful.
B. Nervous.
C. Satisfied.
D. Upset.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段The morning had been a disaster. My tooth was aching. And I'd been in an argument with a friend可知，那天早上很糟糕：牙疼，还和朋友吵架，所以作者的心情是沮丧的（upset）。Cheerful高兴的；Nervous紧张的；Satisfied满意的均不符合。

questions.text: What made the author begin to doubt about the dentist?
options: A. The dentist's agreeing to treat her at very short notice.
B. The dentist's being as busy as the other dentists.
C. The surroundings of the dentist's office.
D. The laughing assistant of the dentist.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段What kind of dentist would be so eager to treat someone at such short notice? Why wasn't he as busy as the others?可知，作者开始怀疑牙医是因为牙医同意在这么短的时间内给她看病。B牙医和其他牙医一样忙错误；C诊所的环境是到了之后才担心的，不是开始怀疑的原因；D笑的助手错误。

questions.text: Why did the author suddenly smile?
options: A. Because the dentist came at last.
B. Because she saw a picture on the ceiling.
C. Because she could relax in the chair.
D. Because the assistant kept comforting her.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段The chair went back. Suddenly I smiled. There was a beautiful picture, right where I could enjoy it: on the ceiling可知，作者突然笑了是因为她看到天花板上有一幅美丽的画。A牙医终于来了错误；C她能在椅子上放松错误；D助手一直安慰她错误。

questions.text: What did the author learn from her experience most probably?
options: A. Strike while the iron is hot.
B. Have a good word for one's friend.
C. Put oneself in other's shoes.
D. A friend in need is a friend indeed.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段朋友的话The trouble with you is that you won't put yourself in my place和倒数第二段At that moment, I began to understand what my friend meant by her words可知，作者从经历中学到的是要设身处地为别人着想（Put oneself in other's shoes）。A趁热打铁；B为朋友说好话；D患难见真情均不符合。

items.title: 2013 重庆 阅读B
items.passage: （注：B篇阅读原文在解析卷中缺失，以下为根据题目推断的内容概要。）本文介绍了Andrew Zuckerman的一个项目，他选择了50位长者进行采访，记录他们的智慧和人生经验。文中介绍了三位受访者：Federico Mayor Zaragoza（在政治和科学领域都有成就）、Nadine Gordimer（作家，教育来自图书馆和书籍）、Dave Brubeck（音乐家）。这个项目旨在传承长者的智慧。

questions.text: Why did Andrew Zuckerman choose the fifty elders for his project?
options: A. Because their wisdom deserves to be passed on.
B. Because they are physically impressive.
C. Because their accomplishments inspired him.
D. Because they have similar experiences.
questions.explanation: 根据文章主题，Andrew Zuckerman选择50位长者是因为他们的智慧值得传承。B他们身体令人印象深刻错误；C他们的成就激励了他不是主要原因；D他们有相似的经历错误。（注：原文缺失，根据题目推断。）

questions.text: According to the web page, Federico Mayor Zaragoza _____.
options: A. has won many awards for his work in politics
B. has served as the president of a university
C. has devoted all his life to the field of science
D. has made achievements in different areas
questions.explanation: 根据文章，Federico Mayor Zaragoza在不同领域都有成就（政治和科学等）。A因政治工作赢得许多奖项不全面；B担任大学校长未提及；C一生致力于科学领域错误，他在多个领域都有成就。（注：原文缺失，根据题目推断。）

questions.text: Who most probably said "My education has been the library and books" in the interview when reflecting on his/her experience?
options: A. Andrew Zuckerman.
B. Federico Mayor Zaragoza.
C. Nadine Gordimer.
D. Dave Brubeck.
questions.explanation: 说"我的教育来自图书馆和书籍"的最可能是作家Nadine Gordimer，因为作家的教育往往来自阅读。A Andrew Zuckerman是项目创始人；B Federico Mayor Zaragoza是政治和科学领域；D Dave Brubeck是音乐家。（注：原文缺失，根据题目推断。）

questions.text: What is the main purpose of this web page?
options: A. To show Zuckerman's awards.
B. To publicize Zuckerman's project.
C. To spread the wisdom of the three people.
D. To celebrate the achievements of the three people.
questions.explanation: 这个网页的主要目的是宣传Zuckerman的项目（采访50位长者，传承智慧）。A展示Zuckerman的奖项错误；C传播三个人的智慧只是部分内容；D庆祝三个人的成就不是主要目的。（注：原文缺失，根据题目推断。）

items.title: 2013 重庆 阅读C
items.passage: Almost every machine with moving parts has wheels, yet no one knows exactly when the first wheel was invented or what it was used for. We do know, however, that they existed over 5,500 years ago in ancient Asia. The oldest known transport wheel was discovered in 2002 in Slovenia. It is over 5,100 years old. Evidence suggests that wheels for transport didn't become popular for a while, though. This could be because animals did a perfectly good job of carrying farming tools and humans around. But it could also be because of a difficult situation. While wheels need to roll on smooth surfaces, roads with smooth surfaces weren't going to be constructed until there was plenty of demand for them. Eventually, road surfaces did become smoother, but this difficult situation appeared again a few centuries later. There had been no important changes in wheel and vehicle design before the arrival of modern road design. In the mid-1700s, a Frenchman came up with a new design of road — a base layer of large stones covered with a thin layer of smaller stones. A Scotsman improved on this design in the 1820s and a strong, lasting road surface became a reality. At around the same time, metal hubs (the central part of a wheel) came into being, followed by the pneumatic tyre in 1846. Alloy wheels were invented in 1967, sixty years after the appearance of tarmacked roads. As wheel design took off, vehicles got faster and faster.

questions.text: What might explain why transport wheels didn't become popular for some time?
options: A. Few knew how to use transport wheels.
B. Humans carried farming tools just as well.
C. Animals were a good means of transport.
D. The existence of transport wheels was not known.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段This could be because animals did a perfectly good job of carrying farming tools and humans around可知，运输轮子有一段时间没有流行可能是因为动物是很好的运输方式，在搬运农具和载人方面做得很好。A很少有人知道如何使用运输轮子错误；B人类也能很好地搬运农具错误；D运输轮子的存在不为人知错误。

questions.text: What do we know about road design from the passage?
options: A. It was easier than wheel design.
B. It improved after big changes in vehicle design.
C. It was promoted by fast-moving vehicles.
D. It provided conditions for wheel design to develop.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段There had been no important changes in wheel and vehicle design before the arrival of modern road design和第四段道路设计改进后轮子设计也随之发展可知，道路设计为轮子设计的发展提供了条件。A比轮子设计容易错误；B在车辆设计大变化后改进错误，是道路设计改进促进了车辆设计；C被快速车辆推动错误，因果关系反了。

questions.text: How is the last paragraph mainly developed?
options: A. By giving examples.
B. By making comparisons.
C. By following time order.
D. By making classifications.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段In the mid-1700s、in the 1820s、At around the same time、in 1846、in 1967等时间标志可知，最后一段主要是按时间顺序展开的。A举例说明；B作比较；D分类均不符合。

questions.text: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The beginning of road design.
B. The development of transport wheels.
C. The history of public transport.
D. The invention of fast-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕运输轮子的发展历史展开，从古代轮子的出现，到运输轮子未流行的原因，再到道路设计和轮子设计的共同发展，所以文章主要关于运输轮子的发展。A道路设计的开始只是部分内容；C公共交通的历史错误；D快速车辆的发明只是部分内容。

items.title: 2013 重庆 阅读D
items.passage: Not all bodies of water are so evidently alive as the Atlantic Ocean, an S-shaped body of water covering 33 million square miles. The Atlantic has, in a sense, replaced the Mediterranean as the inland sea of Western civilization. Unlike real inland seas, which seem strangely still, the Atlantic is rich in oceanic liveliness. It is perhaps not surprising that its vitality has been much written about by ancient poets. "Storm at Sea", a short poem written around 700, is generally regarded as one of mankind's earliest artistic representations of the Atlantic. When the wind is from the west All the waves that cannot rest To the east must thunder on Where the bright tree of the sun Is rooted in the ocean's breast. As the poem suggests, the Atlantic is never dead and dull. It is an ocean that moves, impressively and endlessly. It makes all kinds of noise — it is forever thundering, boiling, crashing, and whistling. It is easy to imagine the Atlantic trying to draw breath — perhaps not so noticeably out in mid-ocean, but where it meets land, its waters bathing up and down a sandy beach. It mimics nearly perfectly the steady breathing of a living creature. It is filled with symbiotic existences, too: unimaginable quantities of creatures, little and large alike, mix within its depths in a kind of oceanic harmony, giving to the waters a feeling of heartbeat, a kind of sub-ocean vitality. And it has a psychology. It has personalities: sometimes peaceful and pleasant, on rare occasions rough and wild; always it is strong and striking.

questions.text: Unlike real inland seas, the Atlantic Ocean is ______.
options: A. always energetic
B. lacking in liveliness
C. shaped like a square
D. favored by ancient poets
questions.explanation: 根据第一段Unlike real inland seas, which seem strangely still, the Atlantic is rich in oceanic liveliness可知，与真正平静的内海不同，大西洋充满海洋活力，即总是充满活力。B缺乏活力错误；C形状像正方形错误，是S形；D受古代诗人青睐不是与内海的不同点。

questions.text: What is the purpose of using the poem "Storm at Sea" in the passage?
options: A. To describe the movement of the waves.
B. To show the strength of the storm.
C. To represent the power of the ocean.
D. To prove the vastness of the sea.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段As the poem suggests, the Atlantic is never dead and dull. It is an ocean that moves, impressively and endlessly可知，引用《海上风暴》这首诗是为了表现大西洋的力量和生命力。A描述波浪的运动只是表面；B展示风暴的力量不是核心，核心是海洋的力量；D证明海洋的广阔错误。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "symbiotic" mean?
options: A. Living together.
B. Growing fast.
C. Moving harmoniously.
D. Breathing peacefully.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段unimaginable quantities of creatures, little and large alike, mix within its depths in a kind of oceanic harmony可知，symbiotic指的是大大小小的生物在海洋深处混合在一起，和谐共存，即Living together（共同生活）。Growing fast快速生长；Moving harmoniously和谐移动；Breathing peacefully平静呼吸均不符合。

questions.text: In the last paragraph, the Atlantic is compared to ______.
options: A. a beautiful and poetic place
B. a flesh and blood person
C. a wonderful world
D. a lovely animal
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段trying to draw breath（呼吸）、the steady breathing of a living creature（生物的呼吸）、a feeling of heartbeat（心跳的感觉）、It has a psychology. It has personalities（有心理，有个性）可知，大西洋被比作一个有血有肉的人（flesh and blood person）。A美丽而诗意的地方不全面；C精彩的世界不全面；D可爱的动物错误，是拟人化为人。

items.title: 2013 重庆 阅读E
items.passage: It is widely known that any English conversation begins with The Weather. Such a fixation with the weather finds expression in Dr. Johnson's famous comment that "When two English meet, their first talk is of weather." Though Johnson's observation is as accurate now as it was over two hundred years ago, most commentators fail to come up with a convincing explanation for this English weather-speak. Bill Bryson, for example, concludes that, as the English weather is not at all exciting, the obsession with it can hardly be understood. He argues that "To an outsider, the most striking thing about the English weather is that there is not very much of it." Simply, the reason is that the unusual and unpredictable weather is almost unknown in the British Isles. Jeremy Paxman, however, disagrees with Bryson, arguing that the English weather is by nature attractive. Bryson is wrong, he says, because the English preference for the weather has nothing to do with the natural phenomena. "The interest is less in the phenomena themselves, but in uncertainty." According to him, the weather in England is very changeable and uncertain and it attracts the English as well as the outsider. Bryson and Paxman stand for common misconceptions about the weather-speak among the English. Both commentators, somehow, are missing the point. The English weather conversation is not really about the weather at all. English weather-speak is a system of signs, which is developed to help the speakers overcome the natural reserve and actually talk to each other. Everyone knows conversations starting with weather-speak are not requests for weather data. Rather, they are routine greetings, conversation starters or the blank "fillers". In other words, English weather-speak is a means of social bonding.

questions.text: The author mentions Dr. Johnson's comment to show that ______.
options: A. most commentators agree with Dr. Johnson
B. Dr. Johnson is famous for his weather observation
C. the comment was accurate two hundred years ago
D. English conversations usually start with the weather
questions.explanation: 根据第一段It is widely known that any English conversation begins with The Weather. Such a fixation with the weather finds expression in Dr. Johnson's famous comment可知，作者提到约翰逊博士的评论是为了说明英语对话通常以天气开始。A大多数评论者同意约翰逊博士错误；B约翰逊博士因天气观察而出名错误；C评论两百年前准确不是目的。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "obsession" most probably refer to?
options: A. A social trend.
B. An emotional state.
C. A historical concept.
D. An unknown phenomenon.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段as the English weather is not at all exciting, the obsession with it can hardly be understood可知，obsession指的是对天气的痴迷、迷恋，是一种情感状态（emotional state）。A社会趋势；C历史概念；D未知现象均不符合。

questions.text: According to the passage, Jeremy Paxman believes that ______.
options: A. Bill Bryson has little knowledge of the weather
B. there is nothing special about the English weather
C. the English weather attracts people to the British Isles
D. English people talk about the weather for its uncertainty
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"The interest is less in the phenomena themselves, but in uncertainty." According to him, the weather in England is very changeable and uncertain可知，杰里米·帕克斯曼认为英国人谈论天气是因为天气的不确定性。A比尔·布莱森对天气知之甚少错误；B英国天气没什么特别的错误，他认为有吸引力；C英国天气吸引人们到不列颠群岛错误。

questions.text: What is the author's purpose of writing the passage?
options: A. To explain what English weather-speak is about.
B. To analyse misconceptions about the English weather.
C. To find fault with both Bill Bryson and Jeremy Paxman.
D. To convince people that the English weather is changeable.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段The English weather conversation is not really about the weather at all. English weather-speak is a system of signs... In other words, English weather-speak is a means of social bonding可知，作者写这篇文章的目的是解释英国的天气谈话到底是关于什么的——它不是关于天气本身，而是一种社会联系的手段。B分析对英国天气的误解只是部分内容；C挑布莱森和帕克斯曼的毛病错误；D说服人们英国天气多变错误。

items.title: 2013 陕西 阅读A
items.passage: Book 1: Joshua, Helmut, and Bethlehem by Gloria Coy-Kendall ISBN: 9781462031795 In this book, the author tells the story of a little boy named Joshua and a little mouse named Helmut. The two become friends and share many adventures together. The story is written in a simple and engaging style that is perfect for young readers. Book 2: More Things in Heaven by Bill Bosworth ISBN: 9781412027854 This book explores the mysteries of life and death, and the meaning of existence. The author draws on his own experiences and observations to offer insights into the spiritual dimension of life. It is a thought-provoking book that will appeal to readers who are searching for deeper meaning in their lives. Book 3: Creation or Evolution by Dr. Joseph I. Rose ISBN: 9780595433582 This book examines the debate between creationism and evolutionism. The author presents both sides of the argument in a fair and balanced way, and offers his own perspective on the origin of humans and the universe. It is a well-researched book that will be of interest to anyone who wants to understand this controversial topic. Book 4: Seeking in the Edge by Michael O. Donovan ISBN: 9781462058679 This book is a collection of poems that explore themes of love, loss, hope, and redemption. The poems are written in a variety of styles and forms, and offer a unique and personal perspective on the human experience. It is a beautiful and moving collection that will touch the hearts of readers.

questions.text: Who wrote the story about a little boy and a little mouse?
options: A. Bill Bosworth
B. Michael O. Donovan
C. Dr. Joseph I. Rose
D. Gloria Coy-Kendall
questions.explanation: 根据Book 1部分Joshua, Helmut, and Bethlehem by Gloria Coy-Kendall和the author tells the story of a little boy named Joshua and a little mouse named Helmut可知，写小男孩和小老鼠故事的作者是Gloria Coy-Kendall。A Bill Bosworth是More Things in Heaven的作者；B Michael O. Donovan是Seeking in the Edge的作者；C Dr. Joseph I. Rose是Creation or Evolution的作者。

questions.text: The ISBN for the book of poems is _________.
questions.explanation: 根据Book 4部分Seeking in the Edge by Michael O. Donovan, ISBN: 9781462058679和This book is a collection of poems可知，诗集的ISBN是9781462058679。A是第一本书的ISBN；B是第二本书的ISBN；C是第三本书的ISBN。

questions.text: What kind of readers will probably like reading More Things in Heaven?
options: A. Those who are searching for the meaning of life.
B. Those who are trying to be spiritual leaders.
C. Those who study the art of writing.
D. Those who like traveling abroad.
questions.explanation: 根据Book 2部分It is a thought-provoking book that will appeal to readers who are searching for deeper meaning in their lives可知，More Things in Heaven会吸引那些在生活中寻找更深层意义的读者。B那些想成为精神领袖的人错误；C那些研究写作艺术的人错误；D那些喜欢出国旅行的人错误。

questions.text: Which of the following books explores the origin of humans?
options: A. Seeking in the Edge
B. Creation or Evolution
C. Joshua, Helmut, and Bethlehem
D. More Things in Heaven
questions.explanation: 根据Book 3部分offers his own perspective on the origin of humans and the universe可知，Creation or Evolution探讨了人类和宇宙的起源。A Seeking in the Edge是诗集；C Joshua, Helmut, and Bethlehem是儿童故事；D More Things in Heaven探讨生命和死亡的奥秘。

items.title: 2013 陕西 阅读B
items.passage: In 1978, I was 18 and was working as a nurse in a small town about 270 km away from Sydney, Australia. I was looking forward to having five days off from duty. Unfortunately, the only one train a day back to my home in Sydney had already left. So I thought I'd hitch a ride. I waited by the side of highway for three hours but no one stopped for me. Finally, a man walked over and introduced himself as Gordon. He said that although he couldn't give me a lift, I should come back to his house for lunch. He noticed me standing for hours in the November heat and thought I must be hungry. I was doubtful as a young girl but he assured me I was safe, and he also offered to help me find a lift home afterwards. When we arrived at his house, he made us sandwiches. After lunch, he helped me find a lift home. Twenty-five years later, in 2003, while I was driving to a nearby town one day, I saw an elderly man standing in the glaring heat, trying to hitch a ride. I thought it was another chance to repay someone for favor I'd been given decades earlier. I pulled over and picked him up. I made him comfortable on the back seat and offered him some water. After a few moments of small talk, the man said to me, "You haven't changed a bit, even your red hair is still the same." I couldn't remember where I'd met him. He told me he was the man who had given me lunch and helped me find a lift all those years ago. It was Gordon.

questions.text: The author had to hitch a ride one day in 1978 because _________.
options: A. her work delayed her trip to Sydney
B. she was going home for her holidays
C. the town was far away from Sydney
D. she missed the only train back home

questions.text: Which of the following did Gordon do according to paragraph 2?

questions.text: The reason why the author offered a lift to the elderly man was that _________.

items.title: 2013 陕西 阅读C
items.passage: According to sociologists, every modern industrial society has some form of social stratification. Class, power and status are important in deciding people's rank in society. Class means a person's economic position in society. A commonly used classification is lower class, middle class and upper class. While sociologists disagree on how these terms should be exactly defined, they do describe societies like the United States quite well. One study shows that 53% of Americans belong to the lower class, 46% the middle class, and 1% the upper class. Interestingly, a surgeon earning $500,000 a year and a bus driver earning $50,000 a year both regard themselves as the middle class. Power refers to the amount of control a person has over other people. Obviously, people in positions of great power (such as governors) exercise big power, but people who take orders from others have less power. Power and class do not always go hand in hand, however. For example, the governor of a state has great power, but he or she may not belong to a corresponding economic class. Generally, however, there is a relationship between power and class. To our knowledge, there aren't too many people who aren't millionaires in the U.S. Senate! Status is the honor or respect attached to a person's position in society. It can also be affected by power and class, but not necessarily so. For example, a university professor may have a high status but not belong to a high social class or have a lot of power over others.

questions.text: What can we learn about "the middle class" from Paragraph 2?
options: A. People earning $500,000 a year belong to the middle class.
B. Nearly half Americans belong to the middle class.
C. People generally consider bus drivers as the middle class.
D. Sociologists have a clear definition of the middle class.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段One study shows that 53% of Americans belong to the lower class, 46% the middle class, and 1% the upper class可知，46%的美国人属于中产阶级，即近一半美国人属于中产阶级。A年收入50万美元的人属于中产阶级错误，他们只是自认为是中产阶级；C人们通常认为公交车司机是中产阶级错误，是公交车司机自认为是中产阶级；D社会学家对中产阶级有明确的定义错误，文章说社会学家对这些术语应该如何精确定义存在分歧。

questions.text: According to the text, we know that _________.

B. status refers to a person's economic position in society
C. people with high status have a lot of control over others

questions.explanation: 根据第三段Power and class do not always go hand in hand, however可知，权力和阶级并不总是一致的。B地位是指一个人在社会中的经济地位错误，阶级才是经济地位；C地位高的人对别人有很大的控制权错误，文章说大学教授可能有很高的地位，但不对其他人有很大的权力；D阶级在决定一个人的社会等级方面不那么重要错误，文章说阶级、权力和地位都很重要。
