questions.text: What can we learn from this passage?
options: A. An invitation is a reputation.
B. An innovation is a resolution.
C. A rejection can be a redirection.

D. A reflection can be a restriction.
In recent years, researchers from diverse fields have agreed that short-termism is now a significant problem in industrialised societies. The inability to engage with longer-term causes and consequences leads to some of the world’s most serious problems: climate change, biodiversity collapse, and more. The historian Francis Cole argues that the West has entered a period where “only the present exists, a present characterised at once by the cruelty of the instant and by the boredom of an unending now”.
It has been proved that people have a bias (偏向) towards the present, focusing on loud attractions in the moment at the expense of the health, well-being and financial stability of their future selves or community. In business, this bias surfaces as short-sighted decisions. And on slow-burning problems like climate change, it translates into the unwillingness to make small sacrifices (牺牲) today that could make a major difference tomorrow. Instead, all that matters is next quarter’s profit, or satisfying some other near-term desires.
These biased perspectives cannot be blamed on one single cause. It is fair to say, though, that our psychological biases play a major role. People’s hesitancy to delay satisfaction is the most obvious example, but there are others.One of them is about how the most accessible information in the present affects decisions about the future. For instance, you might hear someone say: “It’s cold this winter, so I needn’t worry about global warming.”Another is that loud and urgent matters are given too much importance, making people ignore longer-term trends that arguably matter more. This is when a pop star draws far more attention than, say, gradual biodiversity decline.
As a psychologist once joked, if aliens (外星人) wanted to weaken humanity, they wouldn’t send ships; they would invent climate change. Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary. Older people today, for example, can remember a time with insect-covered car windscreens after long drives. Children, on the other hand, have no idea that insect population has dropped dramatically.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段“Rather than setting plans in stone, I’ve learned that sometimes I need to take the opportunities that are offered, even if they don’t sound perfect at the time, and make the most of them. (我明白了有时候我需要抓住提供机会，即使这些机会在当时听起来并不完美，也要充分利用，而不是一成不变地制定计划)”结合文章中作者结合自己被拒绝后得到了更好的职业发展机会，告诉我们最初的拒绝给予了更好的方向。故C选项“拒绝可以是重定向”最符合文章的主旨。故选C。 In recent years, researchers from diverse fields have agreed that short-termism is now a significant problem in industrialised societies. The inability to engage with longer-term causes and consequences leads to some of the world’s most serious problems: climate change, biodiversity collapse, and more. The historian Francis Cole argues that the West has entered a period where “only the present exists, a present characterised at once by the cruelty of the instant and by t

questions.text: The author quotes Francis Cole mainly to ________.
options: A. draw a comparison
B. introduce a topic
C. evaluate a statement
D. highlight a problem
questions.explanation: 第一段首句“In recent years, researchers from diverse fields have agreed that short-termism is now a significant problem in industrialised societies.(近年来，来自不同领域的研究人员一致认为，短期主义现在是工业化社会的一个重大问题。)”提出一个问题——短期主义，接着下文“The historian Francis Cole argues that the West has entered a period where “only the present exists, a present characterised at once by the cruelty of the instant and by the boredom of an unending now”.(历史学家弗朗西斯•科尔（Francis Cole）认为，西方已经进入了一个“只有现在存在的时代，现在的特点是瞬间的残酷和无休止的现在的无聊”。)”引用历史学家Francis Cole的话来强调只注重现在的这种短期主义的危害，由此可推知，文章引用Francis Col的话是为了强调一个问题，故选D。

questions.text: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
options: A. Climate change has been forgotten.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段中“As a psychologist once joked, if aliens (外星人) wanted to weaken humanity, they wouldn’t send ships; they would invent climate change. Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary.(一位心理学家曾经开玩笑说，如果外星人想削弱人类，他们不会派出飞船；他们会发明气候变化。的确，在环境变化的问题上，我们可以形成一种集体的“记忆不良”，每一代人都会认为他们所遇到的情况并没有什么不同寻常的)”可知，一位心理学家曾经开玩笑说，如果外星人想要削弱人类，他们会发明气候变化，通过这种方式来削弱人类，因为人们对于气候变化形成一种集体的“记忆不良”，认为他们所遇到的情况没什么异常的，由此可推知人们不擅长察觉出缓慢的变化，故选C。

items.title: 2023 天津第一次 阅读A

questions.text: What documents are necessary for an international student to seek employment?

questions.text: Before searching for a job on Handshake, you need to ______.

questions.text: Which working arrangement is allowed for a domestic student?

B. 20 hours per week during the semester.

items.title: 2023 天津第一次 阅读B
items.passage: One freezing morning last February, I walked through Ontario Place. Trees were frosted sculptures. Large chunks of ice floated in the lake. Then I saw a group of people in bathing suits bouncing up and down on the shore before running into the lake. I've always found cold water thrilling. The shock of it is like pressing a switch. It seems to reset my body and soul. And last winter, I definitely needed a reset. I woke up most mornings with a dull, grey feeling as I forced myself out of bed to start the day. I needed something to cheer myself up, but I didn't know what. The ice warriors (勇士) emerged from the lake, their skin steaming. Trembling, they were yet laughing and hugging each other. I called out: "You guys are awesome!" One woman waved back, "Come and join us!" The night before my first dip (游泳), I was excited and nervous. Cold water was one thing, but this icy lake was a whole other level. Should I back out? Eventually, I got up in the dark and drove to the lake. After some wild warmup, I charged into the lake along with others. We yelled into the sky. Teeth chattering, heart rates slowing, fingers and toes going numb (麻木), we stayed there for somewhere between 30 seconds and a minute. Then we ran out, laughing and shaking, and put on our clothes. Now I go dipping almost every day, and I've come to long for that moment when the cold becomes a second skin and my internal voice goes silent. Apart from the thrill of those first heart-stopping dives, the community has become a huge part of it. We laughed together, often, but from the stories we've shared about ourselves, I know I'm not the only one who faces life's challenges. Holding hands in the freezing lake, we looked out for each other. It won't fix everything in our lives—but for some reason, it helps. At the end of each session I return home feeling stronger, lighter, more able to carry on. As another winter sets in, I'm more than ready.

questions.text: When the author saw the people in the lake, her feeling can be best described as ______.
options: A. nervous
B. amazed
C. frightened
D. calm
questions.explanation: 根据第一段，作者在一个寒冷的早晨看到一群人穿着泳衣在岸边蹦跳然后跑进湖里。结合作者一直觉得冷水令人兴奋，以及后来决定加入他们，可推断作者看到这些人时的感觉是惊讶的。amazed惊讶的，符合语境。A选项紧张的、C选项害怕的、D选项平静的均不符合。

questions.text: Why did the author think of joining the swimmers?
options: A. To expand her social circle.
B. To lift her spirits again.
C. To adapt to the cold weather.
D. To prepare for a new career.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"And last winter, I definitely needed a reset. I woke up most mornings with a dull, grey feeling as I forced myself out of bed to start the day. I needed something to cheer myself up, but I didn't know what"可知，去年冬天作者需要重新调整，大多数早晨醒来都有一种沉闷、灰暗的感觉，她需要一些东西让自己振作起来。由此可知作者想加入游泳者是为了重新振作精神。A选项扩大社交圈、C选项适应寒冷天气、D选项为新职业做准备均与原文不符。

questions.text: What can be learnt about the author's first dipping?
options: A. She hesitated a bit before going.
B. She suffered from a heart problem.
C. She stayed in cold water too long.
D. She regretted not doing enough warmup.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段"The night before my first dip, I was excited and nervous. Cold water was one thing, but this icy lake was a whole other level. Should I back out?"可知，第一次游泳前的晚上，作者既兴奋又紧张，冷水是一回事，但这个结冰的湖完全是另一个级别，她甚至想过要不要退出。由此可知作者在去之前犹豫了一下。B选项她患有心脏病、C选项她在冷水中待太久、D选项她后悔没有做足够的热身均与原文不符。

questions.text: What change has cold water swimming brought about in the author?
options: A. She is more intelligent.
B. She gets more competitive.
C. She becomes a better storyteller.
D. She regains her inner peace.
questions.explanation: 根据第七段"Now I go dipping almost every day, and I've come to long for that moment when the cold becomes a second skin and my internal voice goes silent"和最后一段"At the end of each session I return home feeling stronger, lighter, more able to carry on"可知，现在作者几乎每天都去游泳，她渴望寒冷成为第二层皮肤、内心声音沉默的那一刻；每次结束后回家时感觉更强壮、更轻松、更能继续前进。由此可推断冷水游泳让作者重新获得了内心的平静。A选项她更聪明了、B选项她变得更有竞争力、C选项她成为更好的讲故事的人均与原文不符。

questions.text: What message does the author most likely want to convey?
options: A. Severe cold builds up character.
B. Group wisdom brightens our life.
C. Tackling the odds together cures.
D. Doing sports promotes friendship.
questions.explanation: 全文讲述了作者在冬天开始冷水游泳的经历，通过和一群人一起在冰冷的湖水中游泳，作者重新振作了精神，获得了内心的平静。文章强调了社区的重要性——他们一起笑，分享故事，在冰冷的湖水中手牵手互相照顾。由此可知作者最想传达的信息是一起应对困难可以治愈心灵。A选项严寒塑造性格、B选项集体智慧照亮生活、D选项做运动促进友谊均不能准确概括文章主旨。

items.passage: Welcome to UCLA Exchange Program! Let's get started by checking out Student Guide for your academic journey! Signing up for ESL (English as a Second Language) ESL courses are designed to help international students improve academic English language skills. Enrollment (课程注册) priority is given to degree students. If space is available, you may enroll. You will be required to take an ESL Placement Test before enrolling in any ESL course. Changing Your Course Enrollment List You may change your class schedule during the first two weeks of the term by adding or dropping courses from your enrollment list. After the second week of classes, there will be a charge for each schedule change. Withdrawing from Courses If you choose to drop a course, you must follow the UCLA procedures for removing it from your schedule. If you forget to officially drop that course, a "F" (Fail) grade will be registered on your record. Taking Exams Some instructors choose to put previous test papers on library reserve, making them available to all students. These exams, which students commonly use for practice, can give you an idea of how instructors structure their tests and what topics they tend to focus on.

items.title: 2023 天津第二次 阅读B
items.passage: I looked through the window of the charming little violin shop, and my heart began to race. I'd been out to dinner that evening. Since it wasn't dark yet after the meal, I decided to walk home from the restaurant. I had traveled that way before, yet I had never noticed that old little shop. But there it was, with a violin displayed in the window. I wiped the dirt from the window to get a better look inside. Several violins hung from the dark walls, quietly waiting to be chosen. As my eyes rested on them, I felt as though I were looking through a window into my own past. My childhood was all about the pursuits I had attempted, most of which had been chosen by Mom. She was like, "Join the swim team, Tara. Your sister is a good swimmer; surely you will be, too." What she didn't understand was that I didn't want to be like my sister. I wanted to find my own passion. Every Saturday I begged Mom not to make me go to the swim meet, but had little chance of success. That said, with a bang of the starting gun, I would dive into the cold water with all my strength and swim as fast as I could. Dad would stand at the edge of the pool, cheering me on. He never pushed me to win; he just wanted me to do my best. Then came a turning point in my life the day our school orchestra (管弦乐队) visited my class, and gave a demonstration. The drums annoyed me. The flutes (笛子) bored me. But the violin…ah, the violin. It made my heart sing. Tightly holding the permission slip from the orchestra director, I ran all the way home after school, and shakily handed it to my parents with a fear that they might dismiss my desire. They didn't. Mom signed it immediately, and Dad promised to buy me a violin. I began practicing the violin with great passion, and rose quickly in ability. Before long I had won the first seat in the community orchestra…

questions.text: What did the sight of the violins in that little shop bring to Tara's mind?
options: A. Her miserable past.
B. An unforgettable sport event.
C. The stories behind the violins.
D. Her childhood memory.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"As my eyes rested on them, I felt as though I were looking through a window into my own past"以及第四段开始回忆童年可知，看到小店里的小提琴让Tara想起了自己的童年记忆。A选项她悲惨的过去、B选项一场难忘的体育赛事、C选项小提琴背后的故事均与原文不符。

questions.text: What Dad did for Tara during the swimming competition implies that he is ______.

B. caring and supportive
C. strict and demanding

questions.explanation: 根据第五段"Dad would stand at the edge of the pool, cheering me on. He never pushed me to win; he just wanted me to do my best"可知，爸爸总是站在泳池边为她加油，他从不强迫她赢，只是希望她尽力。由此可推断爸爸是关心和支持的。A选项没头脑且脾气坏、C选项严格且要求高、D选项宽容且有同情心均不符合。

questions.text: What fascinated Tara during her school orchestra's demonstration?
options: A. The tune of the flutes.
B. The beat of the drums.
C. The sound of the violin.
D. The manner of the musicians.
questions.explanation: 根据第六段"The drums annoyed me. The flutes bored me. But the violin…ah, the violin. It made my heart sing"可知，鼓让她烦恼，长笛让她无聊，但小提琴让她的心歌唱。由此可知在学校管弦乐队的演示中，小提琴的声音让Tara着迷。A选项长笛的曲调、B选项鼓的节拍、D选项音乐家的举止均与原文不符。

questions.text: What enabled Tara to win the first seat in the community orchestra?
options: A. The steady improvement in her taste.
B. Her strong desire for success.
C. Her natural gift for music.
D. The rapid progress in her ability.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段"I began practicing the violin with great passion, and rose quickly in ability. Before long I had won the first seat in the community orchestra"可知，她开始以极大的热情练习小提琴，能力迅速提升，不久就在社区管弦乐队中赢得了第一席位。由此可知能力的快速进步使Tara赢得了社区管弦乐队的第一席位。A选项品味的稳步提高、B选项她对成功的强烈渴望、C选项她的音乐天赋均与原文不符。

questions.text: What message does Tara's story convey?
options: A. It's never too young to learn.
B. A passionate interest works wonders.
C. Hard work will pay off in the long run.
D. Like mother, like daughter.
questions.explanation: 全文讲述了Tara从被妈妈安排学游泳，到找到自己真正热爱的小提琴，并以极大的热情练习，最终取得成功的故事。文章强调了找到自己真正热爱的事物的重要性，热情的兴趣能创造奇迹。A选项学习永远不嫌早、C选项努力工作最终会有回报、D选项有其母必有其女均不能准确概括文章主旨。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读A

C. It organizes free cycle tours.
D. It has over 2,500 rental shops.
questions.explanation: 根据Why MacBike部分"We offer the newest bicycles in a wide variety, including basic bikes with foot brake, bikes with hand brake and gears, bikes with child seats, and children's bikes"可知，MacBike提供多种类型的自行车。A选项给儿童折扣原文未提及；C选项组织免费骑行 tour 与原文不符，游览团需要购票；D选项有2500多家租赁店错误，原文是2500多辆自行车、5家租赁店。

questions.text: How much do you pay for renting a bike with hand brake and three gears for two days?
questions.explanation: 根据价格表，带手刹和三档的自行车第一天价格为€14.75，额外每天€8.00。因此租赁两天的费用为14.75 + 8.00 = €22.75。A、B、D选项计算均有误。

questions.text: Where does the guided city tour start?
options: A. The Gooyer Windmill.
B. The Skinny Bridge.
C. Heineken Brewery.
D. Dam Square.
questions.explanation: 根据Guided City Tours部分"The tour departs from Dam Square every hour on the hour, starting at 1:00 pm every day"可知，带导游的城市游览团从大坝广场（Dam Square）出发。A、B、C选项都是游览路线中经过的景点，不是出发地点。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读B
items.passage: When John Todd was a child, he loved to explore the woods around his house, observing how nature solved problems. A dirty stream, for example, often became clear after flowing through the marshy (沼泽的) area. This observation set him thinking. After studying agriculture, medicine, and fisheries in college, John went back to observing nature and asking questions. Why can certain plants trap harmful bacteria (细菌)? Which kinds of insects can help break down organic matter? He began to see nature as a vast library of solutions to human problems. The task John set for himself was to remove harmful substances from some sludge (污泥). First, he constructed a series of clear fiberglass tanks connected to each other. Then he went to the nearby marsh and collected some of the plants and animals that lived there. He put them into the tanks, and after a few weeks, John added the sludge. He was amazed at the results. The plants and animals in the eco-machine took the sludge as food and began to eat it! Within weeks, it had all been digested, and all that was left was clean water. Over the years, John has taken on many big jobs. He developed a greenhouse — like facility that treated sewage (污水) from 1,600 homes in South Burlington. He also designed an eco-machine to treat sewage from a small town in Fuzhou, China. "Ecological design" is the name John gives to what he does. "Life on Earth is kind of a box of spare parts for the inventor," he says. "You put organisms in new relationships and observe what's happening. Then you let these new systems develop their own ways to self-repair."

questions.text: What can we learn about John from the first two paragraphs?
options: A. He was fond of traveling.
B. He enjoyed being alone.
C. He had an inquiring mind.
D. He longed to be a doctor.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段，John小时候喜欢探索房子周围的树林，观察自然如何解决问题；第二段说他大学学习后回到观察自然并提出问题——为什么某些植物能捕捉有害细菌，哪些昆虫能帮助分解有机物。由此可推断John有善于探究的头脑。A选项喜欢旅行、B选项喜欢独处、D选项渴望成为医生均与原文不符。

questions.text: Why did John put the sludge into the tanks?
options: A. To feed the animals.
B. To build an ecosystem.
C. To protect the plants.
D. To test the eco-machine.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段，John给自己设定的任务是去除污泥中的有害物质。他建造了一系列玻璃纤维罐，放入沼泽中的动植物，几周后加入污泥。第四段说他对结果感到惊讶——生态机器中的动植物把污泥当作食物吃掉了，几周后只剩下干净的水。由此可知John把污泥放入罐中是为了测试生态机器的净化效果。A选项喂动物、B选项建立生态系统、C选项保护植物均不是主要目的。

questions.text: What is the author's purpose in mentioning Fuzhou?
options: A. To review John's research plans.
B. To show an application of John's idea.
C. To compare John's different jobs.
D. To erase doubts about John's invention.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段，多年来John承担了许多大项目：他开发了一个类似温室的设施处理南伯灵顿1600户家庭的污水，还设计了一台生态机器处理中国福州一个小镇的污水。作者提到福州是为了展示John的生态设计理念在实际中的应用。A选项回顾John的研究计划、C选项比较John的不同工作、D选项消除对John发明的疑虑均与原文不符。

questions.text: What is the basis for John's work?
options: A. Nature can repair itself.
B. Organisms need water to survive.
C. Life on Earth is diverse.
D. Most tiny creatures live in groups.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段John所说"You put organisms in new relationships and observe what's happening. Then you let these new systems develop their own ways to self-repair"可知，John的工作基础是自然能够自我修复。他把生物放在新的关系中，让新系统发展出自我修复的方式。B选项生物需要水生存、C选项地球上的生命多种多样、D选项大多数微小生物群居生活均不是John工作的基础。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读C
items.passage: The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism, including a detailed exploration of what it asks and why it works, and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy in your own life. To do so, I divided the book into two parts. In part one, I describe the philosophical foundations of digital minimalism, starting with an examination of the forces that are making digital minimalism so necessary. I then argue that digital minimalism is not just about reducing your screen time, but about rethinking your relationship with technology in a more intentional way. Part one concludes by introducing my suggested method for adopting this philosophy: the digital declutter. This process requires you to step away from optional online activities for thirty days. At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities that you believe will provide real value to your life. In the final chapter of part one, I'll guide you through carrying out your own digital declutter. In doing so, I'll draw on an experiment I ran in 2018 in which over 1,600 people participated, as well as the many stories I've heard from readers who have adopted this practice. The second part of this book takes a closer look at some ideas that will help you cultivate (培养) a sustainable digital minimalism lifestyle. In these chapters, I examine issues such as the importance of solitude (独处) and the role of high-quality leisure activities. You can view these practices as a toolbox meant to aid your efforts to build a minimalist lifestyle that works for your particular circumstances.

questions.text: What is the book aimed at?
options: A. Teaching critical thinking skills.
B. Advocating a simple digital lifestyle.
C. Solving philosophical problems.
D. Promoting the use of a digital device.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism... and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy in your own life"可知，本书的目标是倡导数字极简主义，并教读者如何在生活中采用这一理念，即倡导简单的数字生活方式。A选项教授批判性思维技能、C选项解决哲学问题、D选项推广数字设备的使用均与原文不符。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "declutter" in paragraph 3 mean?
options: A. Clear-up.
B. Add-on.
C. Check-in.
D. Take-over.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段后文"This process requires you to step away from optional online activities for thirty days. At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities"可知，这个过程要求你在30天内远离可选的在线活动，然后只加回少量精心挑选的有价值的在线活动。由此可推断declutter意为"清理、整理"，与clear-up意思相近。B选项附加、C选项登记、D选项接管均不符合语境。

questions.text: What is presented in the final chapter of part one?
options: A. Theoretical models.
B. Statistical methods.
C. Practical examples.
D. Historical analyses.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"In the final chapter of part one, I'll guide you through carrying out your own digital declutter. In doing so, I'll draw on an experiment I ran in 2018 in which over 1,600 people participated, as well as the many stories I've heard from readers"可知，第一部分的最后一章指导读者进行自己的数字清理，并借鉴了2018年1600多人参与的实验以及读者的故事。由此可知这一章呈现的是实际案例。A选项理论模型、B选项统计方法、D选项历史分析均与原文不符。

questions.text: What does the author suggest readers do with the practices offered in part two?
options: A. Use them as needed.
B. Recommend them to friends.
C. Evaluate their effects.
D. Identify the ideas behind them.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段"You can view these practices as a toolbox meant to aid your efforts to build a minimalist lifestyle that works for your particular circumstances"可知，作者建议读者把这些做法视为一个工具箱，帮助自己建立适合个人情况的极简主义生活方式，即根据需要使用这些做法。B选项推荐给朋友、C选项评估效果、D选项识别背后的理念均与原文不符。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D
items.passage: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the "wisdom of crowds" effect. The experiment of estimation he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate. This effect capitalizes on the fact that when people make errors, those errors aren't always the same. Some people will tend to overestimate, and some to underestimate. When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a fairly accurate estimate. In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people's estimates be independent. But a new study led by Joaquin Navajas offered an interesting twist (转折) on this classic phenomenon. The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals. The study also found that the average accuracy could increase even if the estimates were not fully independent. In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion. Did they tend to go with the most confident member? Or did they follow the member who had the most convincing argument? The researchers found that the most convincing argument was the most important factor in the group's decision. Although the studies led by Navajas have limitations and many questions remain, the potential implications for group discussion and decision-making are enormous.

questions.text: What is paragraph 2 of the text mainly about?
options: A. The methods of estimation.
B. The underlying logic of the effect.
C. The causes of people's errors.
D. The design of Galton's experiment.
questions.explanation: 第二段解释了群体智慧效应的原理：当人们犯错时，错误并不总是相同的，有些人倾向于高估，有些人倾向于低估，当足够多的错误被平均后，它们相互抵消，产生相当准确的估计。用更专业的术语来说，群体智慧要求人们的估计是独立的。因此第二段主要讲的是这一效应的底层逻辑。A选项估计方法、C选项人们犯错的原因、D选项高尔顿实验的设计均只是段落的部分内容，不能概括主旨。

questions.text: Navajas' study found that the average accuracy could increase even if ________.
options: A. the crowds were relatively small
B. there were occasional underestimates
C. individuals did not communicate
D. estimates were not fully independent
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"The study also found that the average accuracy could increase even if the estimates were not fully independent"可知，Navajas的研究发现，即使估计不完全独立，平均准确性也能提高。A选项人群相对较小、B选项偶尔有低估、C选项个体不交流均与原文不符。

questions.text: What did the follow-up study focus on?
options: A. The size of the groups.
B. The dominant members.
C. The discussion process.
D. The individual estimates.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion"可知，后续研究试图更好地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么，即关注讨论过程。A选项小组规模、B选项主导成员、D选项个体估计均不是后续研究的重点。

questions.text: What is the author's attitude toward Navajas' studies?
options: A. Unclear.
B. Dismissive.
C. Doubtful.
D. Approving.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段"Although the studies led by Navajas have limitations and many questions remain, the potential implications for group讨论和决策是巨大的"可知，作者认为尽管Navajas的研究有局限性且仍有许多问题，但对群体讨论和决策的潜在影响是巨大的。由此可推断作者对这些研究持赞成态度。A选项不清楚、B选项轻视的、C选项怀疑的均与原文不符。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读A
items.passage: Yellowstone National Park offers a variety of ranger programs throughout the park, and throughout the year. The following are descriptions of the ranger programs this summer. Experiencing Wildlife in Yellowstone (May 26 to September 2) Whether you're hiking a backcountry trail (小径), camping, or just enjoying the park's amazing wildlife from the road, this quick workshop is for you and your family. Learn where to look for animals and how to behave safely around them. Junior Ranger Wildlife Olympics (June 5 to August 21) Kids can test their skills and compare their abilities to the animals of Yellowstone. Stay for as little or as long as your plans allow. Meet in front of the Visitor Education Center. Canyon Talks at Artist Point (June 9 to September 2) From a classic viewpoint, enjoy Lower Falls, the Yellowstone River, and the breathtaking colors of the canyon (峡谷) while learning about the area's natural and human history. Discover why artists and photographers continue to be drawn to this special place. Meet on the upper platform of Artist Point. Photography Workshops (June 19 & July 10) Enhance your photography skills — join Yellowstone's park photographer for a hands-on program to inspire new and creative ways of enjoying the beauty and wonder of Yellowstone. 6/19 — Waterfalls & Wide Angles: meet at Artist Point 7/10 — Wildflowers & White Balance: meet at Washburn Trailhead in Chittenden parking area.

questions.text: Which of the four programs begins the earliest?
options: A. Photography Workshops.
B. Junior Ranger Wildlife Olympics.
C. Canyon Talks at Artist Point.
D. Experiencing Wildlife in Yellowstone.
questions.explanation: 根据各项目的时间：Experiencing Wildlife in Yellowstone为5月26日至9月2日，Junior Ranger Wildlife Olympics为6月5日至8月21日，Canyon Talks at Artist Point为6月9日至9月2日，Photography Workshops为6月19日和7月10日。比较可知Experiencing Wildlife in Yellowstone开始最早。A、B、C选项开始时间均晚于D选项。

questions.text: What is the short talk at Artist Point about?
options: A. Works of famous artists.
B. Protection of wild animals.
C. Basic photography skills.
D. History of the canyon area.
questions.explanation: 根据Canyon Talks at Artist Point部分"enjoy Lower Falls, the Yellowstone River, and the breathtaking colors of the canyon while learning about the area's natural and human history"可知，在艺术家点的讲座可以欣赏下瀑布、黄石河和峡谷令人惊叹的色彩，同时了解该地区的自然和人类历史。A选项著名艺术家作品、B选项野生动物保护、C选项基本摄影技巧均与原文不符。

questions.text: Where will the participants meet for the July 10 photography workshop?
options: A. Artist Point.
B. Washburn Trailhead.
C. Canyon Village Store.
D. Visitor Education Center.
questions.explanation: 根据Photography Workshops部分"7/10 — Wildflowers & White Balance: meet at Washburn Trailhead in Chittenden parking area"可知，7月10日的摄影工作坊在Washburn Trailhead集合。A选项Artist Point是6月19日工作坊的集合地点；C、D选项均不是7月10日工作坊的集合地点。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读B
items.passage: Turning soil, pulling weeds, and harvesting cabbage sound like tough work for middle and high school kids. And at first it is, says Abby Jaramillo, who with another teacher started Urban Sprouts, a school garden program at four low-income schools. The program aims to help students develop science skills, environmental awareness, and healthy lifestyles. Jaramillo's students live in neighborhoods where fresh food and green space are not easy to find and fast food restaurants outnumber grocery stores. "The kids literally come to school thinking vegetables are awful, dirt is awful, insects are awful," she says. Though some are initially scared of the insects and turned off by the dirt, most are eager to try growing their own vegetables. Urban Sprouts' classes, at two middle schools and two high schools, include hands-on experiments such as soil testing, flower-and-seed dissection, tastings of fresh or dried produce, and lessons in composting (堆肥). Students design gardens, take care of them, and then harvest and cook what they grow. Program evaluations show that kids eat more vegetables as a result of the classes. "We have students who say they went home and talked to their parents and now they're eating different foods," Jaramillo says. She adds that the program's benefits go beyond nutrition. Some students get so interested in gardening that they bring home seeds to start their own vegetable gardens. Besides, working in the garden can be a calming and stress-relieving activity for kids who live in noisy, crowded neighborhoods.

questions.text: What do we know about Abby Jaramillo?
options: A. She used to be a health worker.
B. She grew up in a low-income family.
C. She owns a fast food restaurant.
D. She is an initiator of Urban Sprouts.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"Abby Jaramillo, who with another teacher started Urban Sprouts, a school garden program at four low-income schools"可知，Abby Jaramillo和另一位老师一起创办了Urban Sprouts校园花园项目，即她是该项目的发起人。A选项曾是健康工作者、B选项在低收入家庭长大、C选项拥有快餐店原文均未提及。

questions.text: What was a problem facing Jaramillo at the start of the program?
options: A. The kids' parents distrusted her.
B. Students had little time for her classes.
C. Some kids disliked garden work.
D. There was no space for school gardens.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段Jaramillo所说"The kids literally come to school thinking vegetables are awful, dirt is awful, insects are awful"以及"Though some are initially scared of the insects and turned off by the dirt"可知，孩子们来学校时认为蔬菜、泥土、昆虫都很糟糕，有些孩子起初害怕昆虫、厌恶泥土。由此可推断项目开始时面临的问题是有些孩子不喜欢园艺工作。A选项家长不信任她、B选项学生没时间上课、D选项没有校园花园空间原文均未提及。

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the impact of the program?
options: A. Far-reaching.
B. Predictable.
C. Short-lived.
D. Unidentifiable.
questions.explanation: 根据最后两段，项目评估显示孩子们因为这些课程吃更多蔬菜，有些学生回家和父母谈，现在吃不同的食物；项目的好处超出了营养范围，有些学生对园艺非常感兴趣，带回家种子开始自己的菜园，园艺活动还可以成为生活在嘈杂拥挤社区的孩子们的平静和减压活动。由此可推断该项目的影响是深远的。far-reaching意为"深远的、广泛的"，符合语境。predictable可预测的、short-lived短暂的、unidentifiable无法识别的均不符合。

questions.text: What can be a suitable title for the text?
options: A. Rescuing School Gardens
B. Experiencing Country Life
C. Growing Vegetable Lovers
D. Changing Local Landscape
questions.explanation: 全文围绕Urban Sprouts校园花园项目展开，该项目让原本讨厌蔬菜、泥土和昆虫的孩子们通过亲手种植蔬菜，逐渐喜欢上蔬菜和园艺，吃更多蔬菜，甚至在家开始自己的菜园。因此"Growing Vegetable Lovers"（培养蔬菜爱好者）最适合作为文章标题。A选项拯救校园花园、B选项体验乡村生活、D选项改变当地景观均只是文章的部分内容，不能概括全文主旨。

items.title: 2023 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C
items.passage: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world. The image of the reader, and the relationship between reader, book and text, are repeated themes in the history of art. This book offers a wide-ranging selection of works that show how artists have pictured the act of reading over the centuries. In this "book of books," artworks are selected and arranged in a way that emphasizes these connections between different eras and cultures. We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, readers in libraries, and people reading in public spaces. The artworks invite us to think about how we relate to books and how reading shapes our lives. Books themselves may be used symbolically in paintings to demonstrate the intellect (才智), wealth or faith of the subject. Before the wide use of the printing press, books were treasured as rare and valuable objects. The invention of printing made books more available, but they were still important symbols of learning and culture. Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated. From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader. Of course, the e-reader offers convenience, but the printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, "off-line" activity.

questions.text: Where is the text most probably taken from?
options: A. An introduction to a book.
B. An essay on the art of writing.
C. A guidebook to a museum.
D. A review of modern paintings.
questions.explanation: 文章开头介绍了《Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers》这本书的内容、主题和编排方式，后文讨论了书籍在艺术中的象征意义和纸质书的价值。由此可推断这篇文章最可能来自一本书的引言/介绍。B选项关于写作艺术的散文、C选项博物馆指南、D选项现代绘画评论均不符合文章体裁。

questions.text: What are the selected artworks about?
options: A. Wealth and intellect.
B. Home and school.
C. Books and reading.
D. Work and leisure.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"The image of the reader, and the relationship between reader, book and text, are repeated themes in the history of art. This book offers a wide-ranging selection of works that show how artists have pictured the act of reading over the centuries"可知，所选艺术品展示了几个世纪以来艺术家如何描绘阅读行为，即关于书籍和阅读。A选项财富和才智只是书籍在绘画中的象征意义之一；B选项家庭和学校只是阅读场景的一部分；D选项工作和休闲与原文不符。

questions.text: What do the underlined words "relate to" in paragraph 2 mean?
options: A. Understand.
B. Paint.
C. Seize.
D. Transform.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段，艺术品的选择和排列方式强调了不同时代和文化之间的联系，我们看到孩子在家或学校学习阅读、图书馆里的读者、公共场所阅读的人们。这些艺术品邀请我们思考我们如何与书籍建立联系，以及阅读如何塑造我们的生活。relate to在此处意为"理解、与……建立联系"，与understand意思相近。B选项绘画、C选项抓住、D选项转变均不符合语境。

questions.text: What does the author want to say by mentioning the e-reader?
options: A. The printed book is not totally out of date.
B. Technology has changed the way we read.
C. Our lives in the 21st century are networked.
D. People now rarely have the patience to read.

items.passage: As cities balloon with growth, access to nature for people living in urban areas is becoming harder to find. If you're lucky, there might be a pocket park near where you live, but finding a place to experience true wildness within a city is rare. Past research has found health and wellness benefits of nature for humans, but a new study shows that wildness in urban areas is extremely important for human well-being. The research team focused on a large urban park. They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park. The researchers then examined these submissions, coding (编码) experiences into different categories. Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a "nature language" began to emerge. After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often: "presence," "time," "discovery," "flight," "tolerance," and "spirit." Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them. For example, the experience of walking through a forest may be described as "presence" — the feeling of being fully in the moment. A child chasing a butterfly may be described as "flight" — the joy of movement and freedom. "We're trying to generate a language that helps bring the human-nature interactions back into our daily lives. And for that to happen, we also need to protect nature so that we can interact with it," said Peter Kahn, the lead researcher.

items.passage: Live with roommates? Have friends and family around you? Chances are that if you’re looking to live a more sustainable lifestyle, not everyone around you will be ready to jump on that bandwagon. I experienced this when I started switching to a zero waste lifestyle five years ago, as I was living with my parents, and I continue to experience this with my husband, as he is not completely zero waste like me. I’ve learned a few things along the way though, which I hope you’ll find encouraging if you’re doing your best to figure out how you can make the change in a not-always-supportive household. Zero waste was a radical lifestyle movement a few years back. I remember showing my parents a video of Bea Johnson, sharing how cool I thought it would be to buy groceries with jars, and have so little trash! A few days later, I came back with my first jars of zero waste groceries, and my dad commented on how silly it was for me to carry jars everywhere. It came off as a bit discouraging. Yet as the months of reducing waste continued, I did what I could that was within my own reach. I had my own bedroom, so I worked on removing things I didn’t need. Since I had my own toiletries (洗漱用品), I was able to start personalising my routine to be more sustainable. I also offered to cook every so often, so I portioned out a bit of the cupboard for my own zero waste groceries. Perhaps your household won’t entirely make the switch, but you may have some control over your own personal spaces to make the changes you desire. As you make your lifestyle changes, you may find yourself wanting to speak up for yourself if others comment on what you’re doing, which can turn itself into a whole household debate. If you have individuals who are not on board, your words probably won’t do much and can often leave you feeling more discouraged. So here is my advice: Lead by action.

items.passage: A machine can now not only beat you at chess, it can also outperform you in debate. Last week, in a public debate in San Francisco, a software program called Project Debater beat its human opponents, including Noa Ovadia, Israel’s former national debating champion. Brilliant though it is, Project Debater has some weaknesses. It takes sentences from its library of documents and prebuilt arguments and strings them together. This can lead to the kinds of errors no human would make. Such wrinkles will no doubt be ironed out, yet they also point to a fundamental problem. As Kristian Hammond, professor of electrical engineering and computer science at Northwestern University, put it: “There’s never a stage at which the system knows what it’s talking about.” What Hammond is referring to is the question of meaning, and meaning is central to what distinguishes the least intelligent of humans from the most intelligent of machines. A computer works with symbols. Its program specifies a set of rules to transform one string of symbols into another. But it does not specify what those symbols mean. Indeed, to a computer, meaning is irrelevant. Humans, in thinking, talking, reading and writing, also work with symbols. But for humans, meaning is everything. When we communicate, we communicate meaning. What matters is not just the outside of a string of symbols, but the inside too, not just how they are arranged but what they mean. Meaning emerges through a process of social interaction, not of computation, interaction that shapes the content of the symbols in our heads. The rules that assign meaning lie not just inside our heads, but also outside, in society, in social memory, social conventions and social relations. It is this that distinguishes humans from machines. And that’s why, however astonishing Project Debater may seem, the tradition that began with Socrates and Confucius will not end with artificial intelligence.

items.passage: According to the Solar Energy Industry Association, the number of solar panels installed(安装)has grown rapidly in the past decade, and it has to grow even faster to meet climate goals. But all of that growth will take up a lot of space, and though more and more people accept the concept of solar energy, few like large solar panels to be installed near them. Solar developers want to put up panels as quickly and cheaply as possible, so they haven’t given much thought to what they put under them. Often, they’ll end up filling the area with small stones and using chemicals to control weeds. The result is that many communities, especially in farming regions, see solar farms as destroyers of the soil. “Solar projects need to be good neighbors,” says Jordan Macknick, the head of the Innovative Site Preparation and Impact Reductions on the Environment(InSPIRE)project. “They need to be protectors of the land and contribute to the agricultural economy.” InSPIRE is investigating practical approaches to “low-impact” solar development, which focuses on establishing and operating solar farms in a way that is kinder to the land. One of the easiest low-impact solar strategies is providing habitat for pollinators(传粉昆虫). Habitat loss, pesticide use, and climate change have caused dramatic declines in pollinator populations over the past couple of decades, which has damaged the U.S. agricultural economy. Over 28 states have passed laws related to pollinator habitat protection and pesticide use. Conservation organizations put out pollinator-friendliness guidelines for home gardens, businesses, schools, cities—and now there are guidelines for solar farms. Over the past few years, many solar farm developers have transformed the space under their solar panels into a shelter for various kinds of pollinators, resulting in soil improvement and carbon reduction. “These pollinator-friendly solar farms can have a valuable impact on everything that’s going on in the landscape,” says Macknick.

questions.explanation: 根据第一段"We look forward to welcoming you as we showcase the creativity of the Harvard arts community through performances, art exhibitions and art-making activities"可知，ARTS FIRST通过表演、艺术展览和艺术创作活动来展示哈佛艺术社区的创造力，即它呈现的是娱乐性活动。A选项油画展览过于片面；B选项为所有年龄段提供艺术课程原文未提及；D选项是主要旅游景点与原文不符。

questions.text: Which program will you join if you're interested in drawing pictures?
options: A. Light Awash in Watercolor.
B. Spineless Artists: Invertebrate Creativity.
C. Wheel Throwing.
D. Knitting and Pom-Pom Making.
questions.explanation: 根据Light Awash in Watercolor部分"Learn about the materials and qualities of watercolor paint... Try your hand at some of the painting tricks"可知，该活动涉及水彩画材料和绘画技巧，适合对绘画感兴趣的人。B选项无脊椎动物创意、C选项陶艺拉坯、D选项编织绒球均与绘画无关。

questions.text: What can you do together with Javier Marin?
options: A. Practice a traditional dance.
B. Make handcrafts.
C. Visit a local museum.
D. Feed invertebrates.
questions.explanation: 根据Spineless Artists部分"Join Javier Marin... to learn how insects and other invertebrates dance, inspire fashion, and craft amazing structures"可知，与Javier Marin一起可以了解无脊椎动物如何激发时尚并制作令人惊叹的结构，即制作手工艺品。A选项练习传统舞蹈只是了解昆虫如何舞蹈，不是自己练习；C选项参观当地博物馆、D选项喂养无脊椎动物原文均未提及。

items.title: 2024 全国甲卷 阅读B
items.passage: Animals can express their needs using a lot of ways. For instance, almost all animals have distinct vocals (声音) that they rely on to either ask for help, scare away any dangerous animals or look for a mate. Unlike most animals, however, cats have learned to use meowing (喵喵叫) almost only for communication with humans. Cats have many heightened senses, but their sense of smell is quite impressive. They use their noses to assess their environment and look out for any signs of danger. They will sniff out specific areas to find food, and they can recognize other cats by their smell. A pet cat will also use its sense of smell to determine whether a situation is safe or not. Dogs are known for their impressive fetching habit, but cats take this behavior up a notch. Many cats will find random objects outside and bring them to their owners. This is a very old habit that's based on their natural instinct (本能) to hunt. By bringing you a "gift," your cat is showing you that it considers you part of its family and wants to share its success with you.

questions.text: What can be learned about cats' meowing from the first paragraph?
options: A. It's a survival skill.
B. It's taught by mother cats.
C. It's hard to interpret.
D. It's getting louder with age.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段，几乎所有动物都有独特的声音，用于求助、吓跑危险动物或寻找配偶。然而与大多数动物不同，猫学会了几乎只在与人类交流时使用喵喵叫。由此可知猫的喵喵叫是一种生存技能，用于与人类交流以满足需求。B选项由母猫教授、C选项难以解释、D选项随年龄变大声音均与原文不符。

questions.text: How does a pet cat assess different situations?
options: A. By listening for sounds.
B. By touching familiar objects.
C. By checking on smells.
D. By communicating with other cats.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段"A pet cat will also use its sense of smell to determine whether a situation is safe or not"可知，宠物猫利用嗅觉来判断环境是否安全，即通过检查气味来评估不同情况。A选项通过听声音、B选项通过触摸熟悉物体、D选项通过与其他猫交流均与原文不符。

questions.text: Which best explains the phrase "take... up a notch" in paragraph 3?
options: A. Perform appropriately.
B. Move faster.
C. Act strangely.
D. Do better.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段，狗以其令人印象深刻的捡东西习惯而闻名，但猫把这种行为"take up a notch"。后文说许多猫会在外面找到随机物品并带给主人，这是基于它们狩猎本能的古老习惯。由此可推断猫把这种行为做得更好、更进了一步，与D项意思相近。A选项表现恰当、B选项移动更快、C选项行为奇怪均不符合语境。

questions.text: What is a suitable title for the text?
options: A. Tips on Finding a Smart Cat
B. Understanding Your Cat's Behavior
C. Have Fun with Your Cat
D. How to Keep Your Cat Healthy
questions.explanation: 全文围绕猫的行为展开：第一段讲猫的喵喵叫，第二段讲猫的嗅觉，第三段讲猫给主人带礼物的习惯。因此"Understanding Your Cat's Behavior"（了解你的猫的行为）最适合作为文章标题。A选项找到聪明猫的技巧、C选项和猫一起玩、D选项如何保持猫的健康均只是文章的部分内容，不能概括全文。

items.title: 2024 全国甲卷 阅读C
items.passage: The Saint Lukas train doesn't accept passengers — it accepts only the sick. The Saint Lukas is one of five government-sponsored medical trains that travel to remote towns in central and eastern Russia. Each stop lasts an average of two days, and during that time, the doctors on board provide basic medical care and treatment to people who otherwise have no access to health care. "People started queuing to make an appointment early in the morning," says Emile Ducke, a German photographer who traveled with the staff of the Saint Lukas for a two-week trip in November through the Krasnoyarsk region. Russia's public health care service has been in serious need of modernization. The government has struggled to come up with measures to address the problem, particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River. The Krasnoyarsk region, where Ducke traveled, is a vast area about the size of Alaska, but it has a much smaller population. Many people live in remote villages hundreds of miles from the nearest hospital. The annual arrival of the Saint Lukas is another attempt to improve the situation. For 10 months every year, the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock (补给). Doctors see up to 150 patients every day. The train's equipment allows for basic checkups. "I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants working and living in such little space but still staying focused and very concerned," says Ducke. "They were the best chance for many people to get even a basic checkup."

questions.text: How is the Saint Lukas different from other trains?
options: A. It runs across countries.
B. It reserves seats for the seniors.
C. It functions as a hospital.
D. It travels along a river.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"The Saint Lukas train doesn't accept passengers — it accepts only the sick"和"the doctors on board provide basic medical care and treatment"可知，圣卢卡斯号列车不接受普通乘客，只接收病人，车上的医生提供基本医疗服务，即它起到医院的作用。A选项跨国运行、B选项为老年人预留座位、D选项沿河行驶均与原文不符。

questions.text: What can we infer from paragraph 3 about Krasnoyarsk?
options: A. It is heavily populated.
B. It offers training for doctors.
C. It is a modern city.
D. It needs medical aid.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段，俄罗斯公共医疗服务急需现代化，政府在努力解决这个问题，尤其是在伏尔加河以东较贫困的农村地区。Ducke旅行的克拉斯诺亚尔斯克地区面积与阿拉斯加相当，但人口少得多，许多人住在距离最近医院数百英里的偏远村庄。由此可推断该地区需要医疗援助。A选项人口密集与原文相反；B选项为医生提供培训、C选项是现代化城市均与原文不符。

questions.text: How long can the Saint Lukas work with one supply?
options: A. About a year.
B. About ten months.
C. About two months.
D. About two weeks.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"For 10 months every year, the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock"可知，列车在两周内停靠约八个车站，然后返回地区首府进行补给。因此一次补给可以维持约两周的工作。A选项约一年、B选项约十个月（这是每年工作的总时长，不是一次补给的时长）、C选项约两个月均与原文不符。

questions.text: What is Ducke's attitude toward the Saint Lukas' services?
options: A. Appreciative.
B. Doubtful.
C. Ambiguous.
D. Cautious.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Ducke所说"I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants working and living in such little space but still staying focused and very concerned"和"They were the best chance for many people to get even a basic checkup"可知，Ducke对医护人员在狭小空间内工作和生活但仍保持专注和关怀印象深刻，并认为他们是许多人获得基本检查的最好机会。由此可推断Ducke对圣卢卡斯号的服务持赞赏态度。B选项怀疑、C选项模棱两可、D选项谨慎均与原文不符。

items.title: 2024 全国甲卷 阅读D
items.passage: "I didn't like the ending," I said to my favorite college professor. It was my junior year of undergraduate, and I was doing an independent study on Victorian literature. I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was frustrated by the ending. Prof. Gracie smiled and said, "Maybe you should read some of her other novels. You'll find that she has a variety of endings." This was an aha moment for me, and I never thought about endings the same way again. From then on, if I wanted to read an ending guaranteed to be happy, I'd pick up a love romance. If I wanted an ending that made me think, I'd choose a literary novel. If I wanted an ending that scared me, I'd go for horror. I learned that endings are as individual as the stories themselves. But writing the end — that's hard. It's hard for writers because endings carry so much weight with readers. You have to balance creating an ending that's unpredictable, but doesn't seem to come from nowhere. An ending should feel satisfying, even if it's not what the reader expected. That's why this issue (期) of Writer's Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending for whatever kind of writing you're doing. If it's short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six types of endings you can use. If you're writing a novel, Elizabeth Sims offers advice on crafting the perfect finish. And if you're writing creative nonfiction, we have tips for ending your piece with impact. This issue won't tell you what your ending should be — that's up to you and the story you're telling — but it might provide what you need to get there.

questions.text: Why did the author go to Prof. Gracie?
options: A. To discuss a novel.
B. To submit a book report.
C. To argue for a writer.
D. To ask for a reading list.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段，作者对George Eliot的小说《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》的结局感到沮丧，于是对最喜欢的大学教授说"我不喜欢这个结局"。由此可知作者去找Gracie教授是为了讨论一本小说。B选项提交读书报告、C选项为一位作家辩护、D选项请求阅读清单均与原文不符。

questions.text: What did the author realize after seeing Gracie?
options: A. Writing is a matter of personal preferences.
B. Readers are often carried away by character.
C. Each type of literature has its unique end.
D. A story which begins well will end well.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段，教授建议作者阅读Eliot的其他小说，会发现她有各种各样的结局。这是作者的顿悟时刻，从此作者学会了根据想要的结局类型选择不同类型的小说——爱情小说保证快乐结局，文学小说引人深思，恐怖小说令人害怕。由此可知作者意识到每种类型的文学都有其独特的结局。A选项写作是个人偏好问题、B选项读者常被人物吸引、D选项开头好的故事结局也好均与原文不符。

questions.text: What is expected of a good ending?
options: A. It satisfies readers' taste.
B. It fits with the story development.
C. It is usually positive.
D. It is open for imagination.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"You have to balance creating an ending that's unpredictable, but doesn't seem to come from nowhere. An ending should feel satisfying, even if it's not what the reader expected"可知，好的结局需要在不可预测与不突兀之间取得平衡，即使出乎读者意料也应令人满意，即好的结局应与故事发展相契合。A选项满足读者品味（原文说即使不是读者期待的也应令人满意，并非一味满足品味）、C选项通常积极、D选项开放想象均与原文不符。

questions.text: Why does the author mention Peter Mountford and Elizabeth Sims?
options: A. To give examples of great novelists.
B. To stress the theme of this issue.
C. To encourage writing for the magazine.
D. To recommend their new books.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段，本期《作家文摘》旨在帮助读者弄清楚如何为各种类型的写作写出最好的结局。短篇小说方面，Peter Mountford分解了六种可用的结局类型；长篇小说方面，Elizabeth Sims提供了打造完美结尾的建议。作者提到这两位作家是为了说明本期杂志的主题——帮助各类创作者写出更好的结局。A选项举例说明伟大小说家、C选项鼓励为杂志写作、D选项推荐他们的新书均与原文不符。

items.title: 2024 北京 阅读A
items.passage: The Language Exchange Programme allows students in pairs to communicate in two different languages they wish to share and learn each week. Students record short entries after each partner meeting noting their language progress and questions that arise. Requirements for completion: • One welcoming session on the second Friday of the term • 18 weekly one-hour pair meetings • Weekly progress reports for all pair meetings • At least three pair-teacher meetings • One five-minute final video Sign up! The sign-up and registration process is as follows: • Students sign up and indicate the languages they can share and languages they are interested in learning. • Based on the information entered by each student, potential pairs are identified. • Proficiency (熟练) levels are confirmed through coursework or placement tests. • Once a pair has been determined to be suitable, the students will be contacted individually with a special permission number to register for the programme. Reminders: Signing up for the programme does not automatically mean that you will be able to register and participate. Pairs are matched by languages of interest and proficiency levels. Since there are many factors involved in the matching process, not every student who signs up will be matched.

questions.text: In the programme, students will _________.
options: A. chair daily meetings
B. evaluate the exchange
C. meet teachers each week
D. practise their language skills
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"The Language Exchange Programme allows students in pairs to communicate in two different languages they wish to share and learn each week"可知，在这个项目中，学生两人一组每周用两种不同的语言进行交流，即练习语言技能。A选项主持日常会议、B选项评估交流、C选项每周见老师均与原文不符。

questions.text: To complete the programme, students are required to _________.
options: A. development tests
B. participate in pair meetings
C. welcome new students
D. work on weekly videos
questions.explanation: 根据Requirements for completion部分"18 weekly one-hour pair meetings"可知，为了完成该项目，学生需要参加18次每周一小时的配对会议。A选项发展测试、C选项欢迎新生、D选项每周制作视频均不是完成项目的要求。

questions.text: What do students need to do during the registration?
options: A. Indicate their languages of interest.
B. Select their own coursework.
C. Make individual contact.
D. Choose their partners.
questions.explanation: 根据Sign up部分"Students sign up and indicate the languages they can share and languages they are interested in learning"可知，学生在注册期间需要表明他们可以分享的语言以及有兴趣学习的语言。B选项选择自己的课程、C选项单独联系、D选项选择搭档均与原文不符。

items.title: 2024 北京 阅读B
items.passage: When I was a little girl, I liked drawing, freely and joyously making marks on the walls at home. In primary school, I learned to write using chalks. Writing seemed to be another form of drawing. I showed my work proudly. In secondary school, art was my favourite subject. Since I loved it so much I thought I was good at it. For the art O-level exam I had to present an oil painting. I found it difficult, but still hoped to pass. I failed, with a low grade. I'd been over-confident. Now I'd been declared talentless. But other channels of creativity stayed open: I went on writing poems and stories. Still, I went to exhibitions often. I continued my habitual drawing, which I now characterised as childish doodling (涂鸦). In my 30s, I made painter friends and learned new ways of looking at art. Though these new friends were abstract painters using oil paints, or were printmakers, I didn't join them. Oil painting remained a closed door. One night, in my early 40s, I dreamed that a big woman in red approached me, handed me a bag of paints, and told me to start painting. The dream felt so authoritative that it shook me. It was a form of energy, giving me back something I'd lost. The next day I bought oil paints and began. Although I have enjoyed breaking my decades-long taboo about working with oil paints, I have discovered I now prefer chalks and ink. I let my line drawings turn into cartoons I send to friends. It all feels like play. Becoming a successful painter calls for being resolute. I realised I was always afraid of wanting too much. That dream reminded me that those fears and desires could encourage me to take risks and make art.

questions.text: How did the author feel about the result of the art exam?
options: A. Scared.
B. Worried.
C. Discouraged.
D. Wronged.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段"I failed, with a low grade. I'd been over-confident. Now I'd been declared talentless"可知，作者油画考试不及格，成绩很低，被宣布为毫无天赋。由此可推断作者对美术考试的结果感到气馁。discouraged气馁的，符合语境。A选项害怕的、B选项担心的、D选项受委屈的均不符合。

questions.text: In her 30s, the author _________.
options: A. avoided oil painting practice
B. sought for a painting career
C. fancied abstract painting
D. exhibited child paintings
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"In my 30s, I made painter friends and learned new ways of looking at art. Though these new friends were abstract painters using oil paints, or were printmakers, I didn't join them. Oil painting remained a closed door"可知，作者30多岁时结交了画家朋友，但没有加入他们，油画仍然是一扇关闭的门。由此可知作者在30多岁时避免了油画练习。B选项寻求绘画事业、C选项喜欢抽象画、D选项展示儿童画均与原文不符。

questions.text: Which word would best describe the author's dream?
options: A. Confusing.
B. Empowering.
C. Disturbing.
D. Entertaining.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"The dream felt so authoritative that it shook me. It was a form of energy, giving me back something I'd lost"可知，这个梦给作者的感觉是如此权威，震撼了作者，它是能量的一种形式，让作者找回了失去的东西。由此可推断作者的梦是赋予力量的。empowering赋予力量的，符合语境。A选项令人困惑的、C选项令人不安的、D选项有趣的均不符合。

questions.text: What can we learn from this passage?
options: A. Actions speak louder than words.
B. Hard work is the mother of success.
C. Dreams are the reflections of realities.
D. Creative activities involve being confident.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段"Becoming a successful painter calls for being resolute. I realised I was always afraid of wanting too much. That dream reminded me that those fears and desires could encourage me to take risks and make art"可知，成为成功的画家需要有决心，作者意识到自己总是害怕想要太多，那个梦提醒作者恐惧和欲望可以鼓励自己冒险和创作。由此可推断创作活动需要自信。A选项行动胜于言语、B选项努力是成功之母、C选项梦是现实的反映均不是文章的主要启示。

items.title: 2024 北京 阅读C
items.passage: The notion that we live in someone else's video game is irresistible to many. Searching the term "simulation hypothesis" (模拟假说) returns numerous results that debate whether the universe is a computer simulation — a concept that some scientists actually take seriously. The 18th-century philosopher Kant argued that the universe ultimately consists of things-in-themselves that are unknowable. While he held the notion that objective reality exists, he said our mind plays an active role in shaping our experience of reality. If empirical (实证的) experience fails to reveal reality, reasoning won't reveal reality either since it relies on concepts and words that are contingent on our social, cultural and psychological conditions. So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation. And then, we can shift our inquiry from "Is the universe a computer simulation?" to "What useful models can we build to understand the universe?" Now that we are in the information age, we have new concepts such as the computer, information processing, virtual reality, and simulation. Unsurprisingly, these new concepts inspire us to build new models of the universe. There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation. All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries. And the computer simulation metaphor is just one of these tools. It can be imagined that comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the "computer simulation" metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.

questions.text: What does the author intend to do by challenging a hypothesis?
options: A. Make an assumption.
B. Illustrate an argument.
C. Give a suggestion.
D. Justify a comparison.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation. And then, we can shift our inquiry from 'Is the universe a computer simulation?' to 'What useful models can we build to understand the universe?'"可知，作者通过质疑模拟假说，提出建议：应该把探究从"宇宙是否是计算机模拟"转向"我们能建立什么有用的模型来理解宇宙"。因此作者的意图是给出建议。A选项做出假设、B选项说明论点、D选项证明比较合理均不符合。

questions.text: What does the phrase "contingent on" underlined in Paragraph 2 probably mean?
options: A. Accepted by.
B. Determined by.
C. Awakened by.
D. Discovered by.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段"reasoning won't reveal reality either since it relies on concepts and words that are contingent on our social, cultural and psychological conditions"可知，推理也不能揭示现实，因为它依赖于那些由我们的社会、文化和心理条件所决定的概念和词语。contingent on意为"取决于、由……决定"，与determined by意思相近。A选项被接受、C选项被唤醒、D选项被发现均不符合语境。

questions.text: As for Kant's argument, the author is _________.
options: A. appreciative
B. doubtful
C. unconcerned
D. disapproving
questions.explanation: 根据第二段作者引用康德的观点，并在第三段基于康德的观点进行推理"So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation"可知，作者对康德的论点持欣赏态度，认为其观点为自己的论证提供了基础。appreciative欣赏的、赞赏的，符合语境。B选项怀疑的、C选项不关心的、D选项不赞成的均不符合。

questions.text: It is implied in this passage that we should _________.
options: A. compare the current models with the previous ones
B. continue exploring the classical models in history
C. stop arguing whether the universe is a simulation
D. turn simulations of the universe into realities
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation. All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries. items.passage: Franz Boas's description of Inuit (因纽特人) life in the 19th century illustrates the probable moral code of early humans. Here, norms (规范) were unwritten and rarely expressed clearly, but were well understood and taken to heart. Dishonest and violent behaviours were disapproved of; leadership, marriage and inheritance were governed by widely understood rules. The similarity of moral virtues across cultures is striking, even though the relative ranking of the virtues may vary with a social group's history and environment. Typically, cruelty and cheating are universally condemned, while honesty and fairness are praised. These universal norms far pre-date the concept of any moralising religion or written law. Instead, they are rooted in the similarity of basic human needs and our shared mechanisms for learning and problem-solving. The mechanism involves a repurposed reward system originally used to develop habits important for self-care. Our brains use the system to acquire behavioural patterns regarding safe routes home, efficient tool use, and social norms that make group living possible. Social norms are thus internalised because they are rewarding to follow. Social benefits are accompanied by social demands: we must get along, but not put up with too much. Hence self-discipline is advantageous. In humans, a greatly enlarged brain boosts self-control, just as it boosts our capacity for language and planning. This enlarged brain, with its enhanced self-control, allows us to develop the complex moral codes that govern our societies.

items.passage: When I was a little girl, I liked drawing, freely and joyously making marks on the walls at home. In primary school, I learned to write using chalks. Writing seemed to be another form of drawing. I shaped individual letters into repeating lines, which were abstract forms, delightful but meaningless patterns. In secondary school, art was my favourite subject. Since I loved it so much I thought I was good at it. For the art O-level exam I had to present an oil painting. I found it difficult, but still hoped to pass. I failed, with a low grade. I’d been over-confident. Now I’d been declared talentless. But other channels of creativity stayed open: I went on writing poems and stories. Still, I went to exhibitions often. I continued my habitual drawing, which I now characterised as childish doodling (乱画). In my 30s, I made painter friends and learned new ways of looking at art. However, I couldn’t let myself have a go at actually doing it. Though these new friends were abstract painters using oil paints, or were printmakers or sculptors, I took oil painting as the taboo (禁忌) high form I wasn’t allowed to practice. One night, in my early 40s, I dreamed that a big woman in red approached me, handed me a bag of paints, and told me to start painting. The dream felt so authoritative that it shook me. It was a form of energy, giving me back something I’d lost. Accordingly, I started by experimenting with water colours. Finally, I bought some oil paints. Although I have enjoyed breaking my decades-long taboo about working with oil paints, I have discovered I now prefer chalks and ink. I let my line drawings turn into cartoons I send to friends. It all feels free and easy. Un-anxious. This time around, I can accept my limitations but keep going. Becoming a successful painter calls for being resolute. I realised I was always afraid of wanting too much. That dream reminded me that those fears and desires could encourage me to take risks and make experiments.

items.passage: The notion that we live in someone else’s video game is irresistible to many. Searching the term “simulation hypothesis” (模拟假说) returns numerous results that debate whether the universe is a computer simulation — a concept that some scientists actually take seriously. Unfortunately, this is not a scientific question. We will probably never know whether it’s true. We can, instead, use this idea to advance scientific knowledge. The 18th-century philosopher Kant argued that the universe ultimately consists of things-in-themselves that are unknowable. While he held the notion that objective reality exists, he said our mind plays a necessary role in structuring and shaping our perceptions. Modern sciences have revealed that our perceptual experience of the world is the result of many stages of processing by sensory systems and cognitive (认知的) functions in the brain. No one knows exactly what happens within this black box. If empirical (实证的) experience fails to reveal reality, reasoning won’t reveal reality either since it relies on concepts and words that are contingent on our social, cultural and psychological histories. Again, a black box. So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation. And then, we can shift our inquiry from “Is the universe a computer simulation?” to “Can we model the universe as a computer simulation? ” Modelling reality is what we do. To facilitate our comprehension of the world, we build models based on conceptual metaphors (隐喻) that are familiar to us. In Newton’s era, we imagined the universe as a clock. In Einstein’s, we uncovered the standard model of particle (粒子) physics. Now that we are in the information age, we have new concepts such as the computer, information processing, virtual reality, and simulation. Unsurprisingly, these new concepts inspire us to build new models of the universe. Models are not the reality, however. There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation. All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries. And the more tools we have, the more effective and insightful we can become. It can be imagined that comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the “computer simulation” metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.

Dishonest and violent behaviours were disapproved of; leadership, marriage and interactions with other groups were loosely governed by traditions. Conflict was often resolved in musical battles. items.passage: Humans have evolved (进化) to spend long periods doing physical exercise. But why doesn't everyone enjoy exercising? The complexity of the human brain is to blame. Evolving an ability doesn't automatically mean we'll want to use it. While physical exercise isn't that bad, it's still typically unpleasant. It has to be: you're pushing your body to its physical limits. Another issue is that the human brain is highly sensitive to wasted effort. Studies have shown that it calculates the effort required for actions and tends to stop us from squandering vital resources on activities that don't bring immediate rewards. The thing is, regular exercise to get "in shape" requires constant and considerable effort — all for gradual progress and uncertain rewards. So, your brain's tendency to ask, "Is it worth it?" will be working against you. Thankfully, the human brain is a complex organ. It isn't ruled by its more primitive drives. While many species' thought processes are limited to "Food, eat it!", "Danger, run!", "Pain, avoid!", we've evolved beyond that. Our brains can form multiple long-term goals and ambitions. So how does the brain process motivation? The self-discrepancy (自我差异) theory suggests we have several "selves" active in our minds at any given time: our "actual" self, our "ideal" self, and our "ought" self. Your "actual" self is who you are right now. Your "ideal" self is who you want to become. And your "ought" self is the self that does what you ought to be doing to become your "ideal" self. As far as your brain is concerned, there are processes that discourage exercise, and processes that encourage it. Ideally, you'll end up putting more weight on the latter than the former.
