C. Most people have the habit of doing physical exercise.
D. Most people do physical exercise for comfort and pleasure.
questions.explanation: 根据前两段，人类进化出长时间进行体育锻炼的能力，但进化出能力不自动意味着我们想使用它，锻炼通常是不愉快的，因为你在把身体推向极限。由此可推断有些人不喜欢把自己逼得太紧。A选项有些人生来身体比别人弱、C选项大多数人有体育锻炼的习惯、D选项大多数人为了舒适和快乐进行体育锻炼均与原文不符。

questions.text: Which is closest in meaning to the underlined word "squandering" in Paragraph 3?
options: A. Conserving.
B. Mixing.
C. Misusing.
D. Sharing.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"the human brain is highly sensitive to wasted effort. Studies have shown that it calculates the effort required for actions and tends to stop us from squandering vital resources on activities that don't bring immediate rewards"可知，人类大脑对浪费精力高度敏感，研究表明它会计算行动所需的努力，并倾向于阻止我们把重要资源浪费在没有即时回报的活动上。squandering意为"浪费、挥霍"，与misusing意思相近。A选项保存、B选项混合、D选项分享均不符合语境。

questions.text: What is the author's purpose in writing Paragraph 4?
options: A. To raise a question.
B. To provide a definition.
C. To make a comparison.
D. To further explain a point.
questions.explanation: 第三段指出人脑对浪费精力很敏感，第四段进一步说明定期锻炼需要持续不断的努力，进步缓慢且回报不确定，所以大脑会问"值得吗？"这会对你不利。由此可知第四段的目的是进一步解释第三段的观点。A选项提出问题、B选项提供定义、C选项进行比较均不符合。

questions.text: According to the author, how are humans different from many other species?
options: A. Humans are able to picture a favorable future.
B. Humans benefit more from painful experiences.
C. Humans care more about immediate rewards.
D. Humans are skilled at avoiding dangers.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段"While many species' thought processes are limited to 'Food, eat it!', 'Danger, run!', 'Pain, avoid!', we've evolved beyond that. Our brains can form multiple long-term goals and ambitions"可知，许多物种的思维过程仅限于"食物，吃了它！""危险，跑！""疼痛，避免！"，而人类已经进化到超越了这一点，大脑能够形成多个长期目标和抱负。由此可知人类与其他物种的不同在于人类能够设想有利的未来。B选项人类从痛苦经历中获益更多、C选项人类更关心即时回报、D选项人类善于避免危险均与原文不符。

questions.text: According to the self-discrepancy theory, who presents the most active "ought" self?
options: A. A footballer dreaming of becoming a movie star.
B. A student eating potato chips while watching TV.
C. A professional dancer performing at a theatre.
D. A swimmer training to win an Olympic medal.
questions.explanation: 根据第六段"your 'ought' self is the self that does what you ought to be doing to become your 'ideal' self"可知，"应该"自我是做你应该做的事情以成为"理想"自我的那个自我。D选项一个为赢得奥运奖牌而训练的游泳运动员最能体现"应该"自我——他在做应该做的事情（训练）以成为理想自我（奥运奖牌得主）。A选项梦想成为电影明星的足球运动员、B选项边看电视边吃薯片的学生、C选项在剧院表演的专业舞者均不能最好地体现"应该"自我。

items.title: 2024 天津第一次 阅读Passage 2
items.passage: Staring at the bookcases in my study, packed with so many great books that had remained unread, I heard a loud voice in my head — "Shame on you! How can you leave these masterpieces unread?" The first book I picked up was Montaigne's Essays. To my surprise I discovered in the margins (页边空白) what clearly was my own faded hand-writing. So I was actually reading it again, but what I was rereading was not only the text but also my earlier self. Clearly, my way of reading the text had shifted, and I myself had changed over the years. This raised the larger question of rereading. It comes in many forms. There's voluntary rereading, the result of a conscious decision to return to a work. A devoted teacher might also wish to refresh his closeness to a work, and thus avoid teaching through the same old written notes with soporific (让人瞌睡的) effects. Contrarily, there's involuntary rereading. The original reading was either forgotten or so totally absorbed that the new chance encounter with the text produced surprise and astonishment. My reaction to Montaigne was of this kind. Then there are what one might call subconscious (潜意识的) rereadings, those that occur without the specific act of reading, much as the memory of a tune can keep coming back to the mind without its actual playing. This form of remembered contact with a book can accompany us during a lifetime and continue to strengthen and shape us. All of these ways of reading are valuable. Renewed contact with a novel or a poem can activate the search for a better knowledge of the self. The new reading, a form of revision, uncovers the change in ourselves as well as in our understanding of the text. Rereading makes it possible for us to see the world around us, ourselves included, in a new light.

questions.text: What did the author find when reading Montaigne's Essays?
options: A. He still couldn't understand it.
B. He had made notes in it.
C. It was a brand new copy.
D. It was his favorite work.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段"To my surprise I discovered in the margins what clearly was my own faded hand-writing"可知，作者在页边空白处发现了明显是自己褪色的笔迹，即他曾在书里做过笔记。A选项他仍然不能理解、C选项这是一本全新的书、D选项这是他最喜欢的作品均与原文不符。

questions.text: According to the author, what could be a purpose of voluntary rereading?
options: A. To improve the quality of teaching.
B. To learn from admirable characters.
C. To collect details for writing novels.
D. To help making important decisions.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"A devoted teacher might also wish to refresh his closeness to a work, and thus avoid teaching through the same old written notes with soporific effects"可知，一位敬业的教师可能希望重新建立与作品的亲密关系，从而避免用同样陈旧的书面笔记教学而产生让人瞌睡的效果。由此可推断自愿重读的一个目的是提高教学质量。B选项向令人钦佩的人物学习、C选项为写小说收集细节、D选项帮助做出重要决定均与原文不符。

questions.text: According to Paragraph 4, involuntary rereading can bring about?
options: A. Unexpected reading experience.
B. Total concentration on new books.
C. Changed preferences for books.
D. Enhanced reading skills.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"the new chance encounter with the text produced surprise and astonishment"可知，非自愿重读时，与文本的新的偶遇产生了惊讶和惊奇，即意外的阅读体验。B选项完全专注于新书、C选项改变了对书的偏好、D选项提高阅读技能均与原文不符。

questions.text: What can be learnt about subconscious rereading?
options: A. It prevents memory from fading.
B. It helps make who we are.
C. It involves actual reading.
D. It works best with poetry and music.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段"This form of remembered contact with a book can accompany us during a lifetime and continue to strengthen and shape us"可知，这种与书的记忆性接触形式可以伴随我们一生，并继续加强和塑造我们。由此可推断潜意识重读有助于塑造我们是谁。A选项它防止记忆消退、C选项它涉及实际阅读（与原文without the specific act of reading相反）、D选项它最适合诗歌和音乐均与原文不符。

questions.text: What could be the best title for the passage?
options: A. Accessing Masterpieces through Rereading
B. Rereading: Voluntary or Involuntary?
C. Rereading: Pursuit of Truth
D. Transformative Power of Rereading
questions.explanation: 全文围绕重新阅读展开，介绍了重读的三种形式，最后指出重读使我们能够以新的眼光看待周围的世界，包括我们自己。重读具有改变读者对作品、自我及世界认知的力量。因此"Transformative Power of Rereading"（重读的变革力量）最适合作为文章标题。A选项通过重读接触杰作、B选项重读：自愿还是非自愿、C选项重读：追求真理均不能准确概括全文主旨。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读A
items.passage: HABITAT RESTORATION TEAM Help restore and protect Marin's natural areas from the Marin Headlands to Bolinas Ridge. We'll explore beautiful park sites while conducting invasive (侵入的) plant removal, winter planting, and seed collection. Habitat Restoration Team volunteers play a vital role in preserving the biodiversity of these unique ecosystems. GROUPS Groups of five or more require special arrangements and must be confirmed in advance. Please review the List of Available Projects and fill out the Group Project Request Form. AGE, SKILLS, WHAT TO BRING Volunteers aged 10 and over are welcome. Read our Youth Policy Guidelines for youth under the age of 15. Bring your completed Volunteer Agreement Form. Volunteers under the age of 18 must have the parent/guardian approval section signed. We'll be working rain or shine. Wear clothes that can get dirty. Bring layers for changing weather and a raincoat if necessary. Bring a personal water bottle, sunscreen, and lunch. No experience necessary. Training and tools will be provided. Fulfills (满足) community service requirements. UPCOMING EVENTS

questions.text: What is the aim of the Habitat Restoration Team?
options: A. To discover mineral resources.
B. To develop new wildlife parks.
C. To protect the local ecosystem.
D. To conduct biological research.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段第一句"Help restore and protect Marin's natural areas from the Marin Headlands to Bolinas Ridge"可知，该团队旨在恢复和保护马林县的自然区域，即保护当地生态系统。A选项发现矿产资源、B选项开发新野生动物园、D选项进行生物研究均与原文不符。

questions.text: What is the lower age limit for joining the Habitat Restoration Team?
questions.explanation: 根据AGE, SKILLS, WHAT TO BRING部分第一句"Volunteers aged 10 and over are welcome"可知，欢迎10岁及以上的志愿者参加，因此最低年龄限制是10岁。A选项5岁、C选项15岁、D选项18岁均与原文不符。

questions.text: What are the volunteers expected to do?
options: A. Bring their own tools.
B. Work even in bad weather.
C. Wear a team uniform.
D. Do at least three projects.
questions.explanation: 根据文中"We'll be working rain or shine"可知，志愿者将风雨无阻地工作，即使天气不好也要参加。A选项错误，因为原文说"Training and tools will be provided"，工具由组织方提供；C选项穿团队制服、D选项至少做三个项目原文均未提及。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读B
items.passage: "I am not crazy," says Dr. William Farber, shortly after performing acupuncture (针灸) on a rabbit. "I am ahead of my time." If he seems a little defensive, it might be because even some of his coworkers occasionally laugh at his unusual methods. But Farber, who practices at the Colorado Holistic Veterinary Clinic, is one of a growing number of veterinarians who use alternative treatments alongside conventional medicine. Farber, a graduate of Colorado State University, started out as a more conventional veterinarian. He became interested in alternative treatments 20 years ago when he suffered from terrible back pain. He tried muscle-relaxing drugs but found little relief. Then he tried acupuncture, an ancient Chinese practice, and was amazed that he improved after two or three treatments. What worked on a veterinarian seemed likely to work on his patients. So, after studying the techniques for a couple of years, he began offering them to pets. Leigh Tindale's dog Charlie had a serious heart condition. After Charlie had a heart attack, Tindale says, she was prepared to put him to sleep, but Farber's treatments eased her dog's suffering so much that she was able to keep him alive for an additional two and a half years. "I'm just grateful," Tindale says. "He gave us more time." Farber is certain that the holistic approach will grow more popular with time, and if the past is any indication, he may be right: Since 1982, membership in the American Holistic Veterinary Medical Association has grown from 30 to over 700. "Sometime soon," says Farber, "alternative medicine will be just medicine."

questions.text: What do some of Farber's coworkers think of him?
options: A. He's odd.
B. He's strict.
C. He's brave.
D. He's rude.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"even some of his coworkers occasionally laugh at his unusual methods"可知，法伯的一些同事偶尔会嘲笑他不同寻常的方法，说明他们认为他很古怪。B选项严格、C选项勇敢、D选项粗鲁均与原文不符。

questions.text: Why did Farber decide to try acupuncture on pets?
options: A. He was trained in it at university.
B. He was inspired by another veterinarian.
C. He benefited from it as a patient.
D. He wanted to save money for pet owners.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段可知，法伯20年前因严重背痛尝试针灸，经过两三次治疗后病情明显好转。他认为对自己有效的方法可能对动物病人也有效，于是在学习技术几年后开始为宠物提供针灸治疗。A选项大学时接受过培训错误，他是毕业后自学的；B选项受其他兽医启发、D选项想为宠物主人省钱原文均未提及。

questions.text: What does paragraph 3 mainly talk about?
options: A. Steps of a chiropractic treatment.
B. The complexity of veterinarians' work.
C. Examples of rare animal diseases.
D. The effectiveness of holistic medicine.
questions.explanation: 第三段讲述了Leigh Tindale的狗Charlie患有严重心脏病，原本准备实施安乐死，但法伯的综合疗法大大减轻了狗的痛苦，使其多活了两年半。这个例子具体说明了综合疗法的有效性。A选项按摩治疗步骤、B选项兽医工作的复杂性、C选项罕见动物疾病的例子均不符合段落主旨。

questions.text: Why does the author mention the American Holistic Veterinary Medical Association?
options: A. To prove Farber's point.
B. To emphasize its importance.
C. To praise veterinarians.
D. To advocate animal protection.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段，法伯确信综合疗法会越来越受欢迎，作者紧接着提到自1982年以来美国综合兽医医学协会的会员从30人增长到700多人，用数据来证明法伯的观点——综合疗法正日益受到认可。B选项强调其重要性、C选项赞扬兽医、D选项倡导动物保护均不是作者提及该协会的目的。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读C
items.passage: Is comprehension the same whether a person reads a text onscreen or on paper? And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material? The answers to both questions are often "no". The reasons relate to the mental processes involved and the limitations of digital devices. When reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it's on paper than onscreen. A large amount of research confirms this finding. The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text. The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper's physical properties. With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages. People often link their memory of what they read to where it appeared on a page. The physicality of paper supports a sense of "being there" with the text, which aids comprehension and recall. But equally important is the mental aspect. Reading researchers have proposed a theory called "shallowing hypothesis (假说)". According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, leading them to process information more superficially. The constant notifications and easy distractions of digital devices further weaken deep reading. Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies — say, assigning an online talk instead of an article by the same person. However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults are given the same content in different formats, those who read the text retain more information and perform better on comprehension tests than those who listen or watch. Digital texts, audio and video all have educational roles, especially when providing resources not available in print. However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn't assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.

questions.text: What does the underlined phrase "shine through" in paragraph 2 mean?
options: A. Seem unlikely to last.
B. Seem hard to explain.
C. Become ready to use.
D. Become easy to notice.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段前文可知，大量研究证实阅读几百字以上的文本时，纸质阅读比屏幕阅读更有成效。后文说当实验者从简单任务（如识别主旨）转向需要思维抽象的任务（如推理）时，纸质阅读的益处就更加"shine through"。结合语境可推断该短语意为"变得显而易见、容易注意到"，与D项意思相近。A项似乎难以持续、B项似乎难以解释、C项变得可以使用均不符合语境。

questions.text: What does the shallowing hypothesis assume?
options: A. Readers treat digital texts lightly.
B. Digital texts are simpler to understand.
C. People select digital texts randomly.
D. Digital texts are suitable for social media.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段"According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, leading them to process information more superficially"可知，浅层化假说认为人们以适合社交媒体的心态对待数字文本，不够严肃，导致对信息的处理更加肤浅，即读者对数字文本持轻视态度。B项数字文本更易理解、C项人们随机选择数字文本、D项数字文本适合社交媒体均与假说内容不符。

questions.text: Why are audio and video increasingly used by university teachers?
options: A. They can hold students' attention.
B. They are more convenient to prepare.
C. They help develop advanced skills.
D. They are more informative than text.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段"Audio and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies"可知，音频和视频比文本更具吸引力，能吸引学生的注意力，因此大学教师越来越多地使用这些技术。B项准备更方便、C项有助于培养高级技能、D项比文本信息量更大原文均未提及。

questions.text: What does the author imply in the last paragraph?
options: A. Students should apply multiple learning techniques.
B. Teachers should produce their own teaching material.
C. Print texts cannot be entirely replaced in education.
D. Education outside the classroom cannot be ignored.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段，作者指出数字文本、音频和视频在教育中都有作用，尤其是在提供纸质资源无法获取的内容时。然而，在需要精神专注和反思的深度学习中，教育者不应假设所有媒介都是一样的。由此可推断，作者认为在教育中纸质文本不能被完全取代。A项学生应运用多种学习技巧、B项教师应自制教材、D项课外教育不容忽视均不是作者在最后一段暗示的内容。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D
items.passage: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records. Today, most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records. Though valuable, these observations may not provide a true picture of global biodiversity, according to a new study. "With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application," said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences. "These observations now outnumber the primary data that comes from physical specimens (标本), and since we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?" Using a global dataset of 1.9 billion records of plants, insects, birds, and animals, Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns. "We were particularly interested in exploring the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data, like the greater likelihood of a citizen scientist to take a picture of a flowering plant instead of the grass right next to it," said Daru. Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage. Moreover, these data are biased and favor certain regions, time periods, and species. This makes sense because the people who get observations are often located near cities and tend to record species that are easy to see and interesting to them. What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity? "Quite a lot," Daru explained. "Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled. To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image."

questions.text: What do we know about the records of species collected now?
options: A. They are becoming outdated.
B. They are mostly in electronic form.
C. They are limited in number.
D. They are used for public exhibition.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"Today, most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records"可知，现在大多数生物多样性记录以照片、视频和其他数字记录的形式存在，即以电子形式为主。A项正在过时、C项数量有限、D项用于公开展览均与原文不符。

questions.text: What does Daru's study focus on?
options: A. Threatened species.
B. Physical specimens.
C. Observational data.
D. Mobile applications.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段Daru所说，这些观察记录的数量已超过物理标本的原始数据，而人们越来越多地使用观察数据来研究物种如何应对全球变化，因此他想知道这些数据是否可用。第四段也提到他特别关注采样中容易产生数据偏差的方面。由此可知Daru的研究聚焦于观察数据的质量和可用性。A项濒危物种、B项物理标本、D项移动应用均不是研究重点。

questions.text: What has led to the biases according to the study?
options: A. Mistakes in data analysis.
B. Poor quality of uploaded pictures.
C. Improper way of sampling.
D. Unreliable data collection devices.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段Daru所说，他们特别关注采样中容易产生数据偏差的方面，比如公民科学家更有可能拍摄开花植物的照片而不是旁边的草。第五段进一步指出，进行观察的人通常位于城市附近，倾向于记录容易看到且感兴趣的物种。由此可知，不当的采样方式导致了数据偏差。A项数据分析错误、B项上传图片质量差、D项数据采集设备不可靠均不是偏差产生的原因。

questions.text: What is Daru's suggestion for biodiversity apps?
options: A. Review data from certain areas.
B. Hire experts to check the records.
C. Confirm the identity of the users.
D. Give guidance to citizen scientists.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Daru的建议，生物多样性应用程序可以利用研究结果告知用户哪些区域采样过度，引导他们前往采样不足的地方甚至物种那里；还可以鼓励用户让专家确认上传图片的鉴定结果。这些建议本质上是给公民科学家提供指导，帮助他们获取更有价值的数据。A项审查特定区域数据、B项雇用专家检查记录（原文是鼓励用户让专家确认，而非应用直接雇用）、C项确认用户身份均不准确。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读A
items.passage: Choice of Walks for Beginner and Experienced Walkers The Carlow Autumn Walking Festival is a great opportunity for the beginner, experienced or advanced walker to enjoy the challenges of Carlow's mountain hikes or the peace of its woodland walks. Walk 1 — The Natural World With environmentalist Éanna Lamhna as the guide, this walk promises to be an informative tour. Walkers are sure to learn lots about the habitats and natural world of the Blackstairs. Date and Time: Saturday, 1st October, at 09:00 Start Point: Scratoes Bridge Walk Duration: 6 hours Walk 2 — Introduction to Hillwalking Emmanuel Chappard, an experienced guide, has a passion for making the great outdoors accessible to all. This mountain walk provides an insight into the skills required for hillwalking to ensure you get the most out of your experience. Date and Time: Sunday, 2nd October, at 09:00 Start Point: Deerpark Car Park Walk Duration: 5 hours Walk 3 — Moonlight Under the Stars Walking at night-time is a great way to step out of your comfort zone. Breathtaking views of the lowlands of Carlow can be enjoyed in the presence of welcoming guides from local walking clubs. A torch is essential. Those who are dressed inappropriately will be refused permission to participate. Date and Time: Saturday, 1st October, at 18:30 Start Point: The Town Hall Walk Duration: 3 hours Walk 4 — Photographic Walk in Kilbrannish Forest This informative walk led by Richard Smyth introduces you to the basic principles of photography in the wild. Bring along your camera and enjoy the wonderful views along this well-surfaced forest path. Date and Time: Sunday, 2nd October, at 11:45 Start Point: Kilbrannish Forest Recreation Area Walk Duration: 1.5 hours

questions.text: Which walk takes the shortest time?
options: A. The Natural World.
B. Introduction to Hillwalking.
C. Moonlight Under the Stars.
D. Photographic Walk in Kilbrannish Forest.
questions.explanation: 根据四种步行方案的Walk Duration部分，Walk 1为6小时，Walk 2为5小时，Walk 3为3小时，Walk 4为1.5小时。比较可知Walk 4——Photographic Walk in Kilbrannish Forest用时最短。A、B、C选项的步行时间均长于Walk 4。

questions.text: What are participants in Walk 3 required to do?
options: A. Wear proper clothes.
B. Join a walking club.
C. Get special permits.
D. Bring a survival guide.
questions.explanation: 根据Walk 3部分"Those who are dressed inappropriately will be refused permission to participate"可知，穿着不当的人将被拒绝参加，因此参与者需要穿合适的衣服。B选项加入步行俱乐部、C选项获得特别许可、D选项携带生存指南原文均未提及。

questions.text: What do the four walks have in common?
options: A. They involve difficult climbing.
B. They are for experienced walkers.
C. They share the same start point.
D. They are scheduled for the weekend.
questions.explanation: 根据四种步行方案的Date and Time部分，Walk 1和Walk 3在周六（Saturday），Walk 2和Walk 4在周日（Sunday），因此四种步行都安排在周末。A选项涉及艰难攀登错误，Walk 4是森林摄影步行；B选项适合有经验的步行者错误，Walk 1和Walk 2适合初学者；C选项起点相同错误，四个起点各不相同。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读B
items.passage: Do you ever get to the train station and realize you forgot to bring something to read? Yes, we all have our phones, but many of us still like to go old school and read something printed. Well, there's a kiosk (小亭) for that. In the San Francisco Bay Area, at least. "You enter the fare gates (检票口) and you'll see a kiosk that is lit up and it tells you can get a one-minute, a three-minute, or a five-minute story," says Alicia Trost, the chief communications officer of BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit). "You choose which length you want and it gives you a receipt-like short story." It's that simple. Riders have printed nearly 20,000 short stories and poems since the program was launched last March. Some are classic short stories, and some are new original works. Trost also wants to introduce local writers to local riders. "We wanted to do something where we do a call to artists in the Bay Area to submit stories for a contest," Trost says. "And as of right now, we've gotten over 300 submissions." The winning stories would go into our kiosks and the winners get a $200 gift card. Ridership on transit (交通) systems across the country has been down the past half century, so could short stories save transit? Trost thinks so. "At the end of the day all transit agencies right now are doing everything they can to improve the rider experience. So I absolutely think we will get more riders just because of short stories," she says. And you'll never be without something to read.

questions.text: Why did BART start the kiosk program?
options: A. To promote the local culture.
B. To discourage phone use.
C. To meet passengers' needs.
D. To reduce its running costs.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段，很多人到火车站发现忘记带读物，虽然有手机但仍喜欢阅读印刷品。BART推出售货亭提供短篇故事打印服务，正是为了满足乘客的阅读需求。A选项推广当地文化是项目的附加效果而非初衷；B选项不鼓励使用手机原文未提及；D选项降低运营成本与原文不符。

questions.text: How are the stories categorized in the kiosk?
options: A. By popularity.
B. By length.
C. By theme.
D. By language.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"it tells you can get a one-minute, a three-minute, or a five-minute story"和"You choose which length you want"可知，售货亭中的故事按长度（1分钟、3分钟、5分钟）分类，乘客可选择想要的长度。A选项按受欢迎程度、C选项按主题、D选项按语言均与原文不符。

questions.text: What has Trost been doing recently?
options: A. Organizing a story contest.
B. Doing a survey of customers.
C. Choosing a print publisher.
D. Conducting interviews with artists.
questions.explanation: 根据第五段Trost所说"We wanted to do something where we do a call to artists in the Bay Area to submit stories for a contest"以及已收到300多份投稿可知，Trost最近在组织故事比赛，呼吁湾区艺术家提交作品参赛。B选项做顾客调查、C选项选择印刷出版商、D选项采访艺术家原文均未提及。

questions.text: What is Trost's opinion about BART's future?
options: A. It will close down.
B. Its profits will decline.
C. It will expand nationwide.
D. Its ridership will increase.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段Trost所说"So I absolutely think we will get more riders just because of short stories"可知，Trost认为短篇故事项目会吸引更多乘客，即BART的乘客量将会增加。A选项将关闭、B选项利润将下降与Trost的乐观态度相反；C选项将扩展到全国原文未提及。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C
items.passage: We all know fresh is best when it comes to food. However, most produce at the store went through weeks of travel and covered hundreds of miles before reaching the table. While farmer's markets are a solid choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more. BMF is an indoor garden system. It can be set up for a family. Additionally, it could serve a larger audience such as a hospital, restaurant or school. The innovative design requires little effort to maintain and uses 90 percent less water than traditional farming. Specifically, it's a farm that relies on new technology. By connecting through the Cloud, BMF is remotely monitored. Also, there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time. Because the system is automated, the plants get exactly what they need, when they need it. Moreover, having a system in the same building where it's eaten means zero emissions (排放) from transporting plants from soil to salad. In addition, there's no need for pesticides and other chemicals that can harm human health. BMF employees live out sustainability in their everyday lives. About half of them walk or bike to work. Inside the office, they encourage recycling and waste reduction by limiting garbage cans and avoiding single-use plastics.

questions.text: What can be learned about BMF from paragraph 1?
options: A. It guarantees the variety of food.
B. It requires day-to-day care.
C. It cuts the farm-to-table distance.
D. It relies on farmer's markets.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段"While farmer's markets are a solid choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more"可知，农贸市场能缩短运输距离，而BMF进一步缩短了从农场到餐桌的距离。A选项保证食物多样性原文未提及；B选项需要日常照料与第二段"requires little effort to maintain"不符；D选项依赖农贸市场与原文意思相反。

questions.text: What information does the convenient app offer?
options: A. Real-time weather changes.
B. Current condition of the plants.
C. Chemical pollutants in the soil.
D. Availability of pre-seeded pods.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段"there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time"可知，这个应用程序实时提供植物生长数据，即植物的当前状态。A选项实时天气变化、C选项土壤中的化学污染物、D选项预播种荚的可用性原文均未提及。

questions.text: What can be concluded about BMF employees?
options: A. They have a great passion for sports.
B. They are devoted to community service.
C. They are fond of sharing daily experiences.
D. They have a strong environmental awareness.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段，BMF员工在日常生活中践行可持续发展：约一半人步行或骑自行车上班，办公室内鼓励回收和减少浪费，限制垃圾桶使用并避免一次性塑料。由此可推断他们有很强的环保意识。A选项热爱运动、B选项致力于社区服务、C选项喜欢分享日常经历均不是本段主旨。

questions.text: What does the text mainly talk about?
options: A. BMF's major strengths.
B. BMF's general management.
C. BMF's global influence.
D. BMF's technical standards.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕BMF的优势展开：第一段讲缩短农场到餐桌距离，第二段讲低维护和节水，第三段讲云技术和自动化，第四段讲零排放和无农药，第五段讲员工的环保实践。因此本文主要介绍BMF的主要优势。B选项综合管理、C选项全球影响力、D选项技术标准均只是文章的部分内容，不能概括全文。

items.title: 2024 新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读D
items.passage: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives, we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence by Catriona Campbell comes in. In the wrong hands, such a book could prove as complicated to process as the computer code (代码) that powers AI but, thankfully, Campbell has more than two decades' professional experience translating the heady into the understandable. She writes from the practical angle of a business person rather than an academic. As we soon come to learn from AI by Design, AI is already super-smart and will become more capable, moving from the current generation of "narrow-AI" to Artificial General Intelligence. From there, Campbell argues, the next step is Artificial Superintelligence, which will be capable of solving any problem we set it. Campbell's point is to wake up those responsible for AI—the technology companies and world leaders—so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it. She explains we are at a "tipping point" and that we need to think very carefully about where AI is heading. She says it is essential that we keep control of artificial intelligence, or risk being sidelined and perhaps even worse. We need to consider AI by Design as a call to arms, and a practical one at that. AI will affect us all, and if you only read one book on the subject, this is it.

questions.text: What does the phrase "In the wrong hands" in paragraph 2 probably mean?
options: A. If read by someone poorly educated.
B. If reviewed by someone ill-intentioned.
C. If written by someone less competent.
D. If translated by someone unacademic.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段后文"such a book could prove as complicated to process as the computer code that powers AI"可知，如果由不恰当的人来写，这本书可能会像驱动AI的计算机代码一样复杂难懂。幸运的是Campbell有二十多年将深奥内容转化为易懂内容的专业经验。由此可推断"In the wrong hands"意为"如果由能力不足的人来写"。A选项如果受教育程度低的人阅读、B选项如果恶意的人评论、D选项如果非学术人士翻译均不符合语境。

questions.text: What is a feature of AI by Design according to the text?
options: A. It is packed with complex codes.
B. It adopts a down-to-earth writing style.
C. It provides step-by-step instructions.
D. It is intended for AI professionals.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段，Campbell有二十多年将深奥内容转化为易懂内容的经验，她从商人的实用角度而非学者角度写作。由此可推断该书采用了务实、接地气的写作风格。A选项充满复杂代码与原文意思相反；C选项提供逐步指导原文未提及；D选项面向AI专业人士与原文不符，该书是写给普通大众的。

questions.text: What does Campbell urge people to do regarding AI development?
options: A. Observe existing regulations on it.
B. Reconsider expert opinions about it.
C. Make joint efforts to keep it under control.
D. Learn from prior experience to slow it down.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段，Campbell的观点是唤醒那些对AI负责的人——科技公司和世界领导人，使他们与开发AI的专家达成共识。她认为我们正处于"临界点"，必须保持对人工智能的控制，否则有被边缘化甚至更糟的风险。由此可知Campbell敦促人们共同努力控制AI。A选项遵守现有法规、B选项重新考虑专家意见、D选项借鉴以往经验减缓发展均不符合原文。

questions.text: What is the author's purpose in writing the text?
options: A. To recommend a book on AI.
B. To give a brief account of AI history.
C. To clarify the definition of AI.
D. To honor an outstanding AI expert.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段引入《AI by Design》这本书，中间各段介绍该书的内容、特点和核心观点，最后一段说"if you only read one book on the subject, this is it"（如果关于这个主题你只读一本书，就是这本）。由此可知作者的写作目的是推荐一本关于AI的书。B选项简述AI历史、C选项阐明AI定义、D选项致敬杰出AI专家均只是文章的部分内容，不是写作目的。

items.passage: Tom Sawyer Play Is an Adventure A 35-minute hand-clapping, foot-stomping musical version of a Mark Twain favorite returns with this Tall Stacks festival. “Tom Sawyer: A River Adventure” has all the good stuff, including the fence painting, the graveyard, the island and the cave. It is adapted by Joe McDonough, with music by David Kisor. That’s the local stage writing team that creates many of the Children’s Theatre of Cincinnati’s original musicals, along with the holiday family musicals at Ensemble Theatre. This year Nathan Turner of Burlington is Tom Sawyer, and Robbie McMath of Fort Mitchell is Huck Finn. Tumer, a 10th-grader at School for Creative and Performing Arts, is a familiar presence on Cincinnati’s stages. He is a star act or of Children’s Theatre, having played leading roles in “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow” and “The Wizard of Oz,” and is fresh from Jersey Production “Ragtime”. McMath is a junior at Beechwood High School. He was in the cast of “Tom Sawyer” when it was first performed and is a Children’s Theatre regular, with five shows to his credit. This summer he attended Kentucky’s Governor’s School for the Arts in Musical Theatre. Note to teachers: Children’s Theatre has a study guide demonstrating how math and science can be taught through “Tom Sawyer.” For downloadable lessons, visit the official website of Children’s Theatre.

items.title: 2024 浙江（1月） 阅读B
items.passage: When was the last time you used a telephone box? I mean to make an actual phone call — not to shelter from the rain. Ages ago, right? The last time I used a phone box for its intended purpose was…2006. I was conducting auditions (试演) for my play in my tiny old shared house in London. Hoping to impress some talented actors to come and work for me for nothing, I spread some throws over the sofas and lit candles to make it seem a bit more ”young professional”. As I rushed outdoors to empty the wastepaper baskets, the door swung shut behind me. Suddenly I was locked outside. My mobile phone was inside, but luckily there was a telephone box across the street. So, I called Directory Assistance, got put through to our landlady’s managing agent, and had a spare key sent to me with just enough time to get back in before the actors arrived. As it has been many years since I last used one, I should hardly be surprised that then are no longer any public telephones near my house. The last one standing has just been turn into a “mini community library”: any passer-by can “borrow” a book from its shelves return it later, or replace it with another title from their own collection. For a few months after the “library” opened, I didn’t bother taking a look, as I had assumed that it would be stuffed full of cheese love stories. Then I noticed fork conducting spring cleans dropping boxes of voluminous books on various subjects there. And these books were free. This unbeatable price-point encouraged me to experiment with dozens of titles that I would never normally consider buying. And I’ve discovered some great books! If I ever get trapped outside my house again, my local telephone box will, sadly no longer be able to connect me with my keys. But it can certainly keep me entertained while I wait for my wife to rescue me.

questions.text: What does the underlined word “it” in the first paragraph refer to?
options: A. The play.
B. The shared house.
C. The sofa.
D. The telephone box.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段第五句“I was conducting auditions (试演) for my play in my tiny old shared house in London.(我当时在伦敦我那狭小的合租房子里为我的剧本进行试演。)”可知，此处是指使“我”的合租房看起来更“年轻专业”一点，所以it代指“合租房”。故选B。

items.title: 2024 浙江（1月） 阅读C
items.passage: On September 7, 1991, the costliest hailstorm (雹暴) in Canadian history hit Calgary’s southern suburbs. As a result, since 1996 a group of insurance companies have spent about $2million per year on the Alberta Hail Suppression Project. Airplanes seed threatening storm cells with a chemical to make small ice crystals fall as rain before they can grow into dangerous hailstones. But farmers in east-central Alberta — downwind of the hail project flights — worry that precious moisture (水分) is being stolen from their thirsty land by the cloud seeding. Norman Stienwand, who farms in that area, has been addressing public meetings on this issue for years “Basically, the provincial government is letting the insurance companies protect the Calgary-Edmonton urban area from hail,” Mr. Stienwan d says, “but they’re increasing drought risk as far east as Saskatchewan.” The Alberta hail project is managed by Terry Krauss, a cloud physicist who works for Weather Modification Inc. of Fargo, North Dakota. “We affect only a very small percentage of the total moisture in the air, so we cannot be cousing drought.” Dr. Krauss says. “In fact, we may be helping increase the moisture downwind by creating wetter ground.” One doubter about the safety of cloud seeding is Chuck Doswell, a research scientist who just retired from the University of Oklahoma. “In 1999, I personally saw significant tornadoes (龙卷风) form from a seeded storm cell in Kansas,” Dr. Doswell says. “Does cloud seeding create killer storms or reduce moisture downwind? No one really knows, of course, but the seeding goes on.” Given the degree of doubt, Mr. Stienwand suggests, “it would be wise to stop cloud seeding.” In practice, doubt has had the opposite effect. Due to the lack of scientific proof concerning their impacts, no one has succeeded in winning a lawsuit against cloud-seeding companies. Hence, private climate engineering can proceed in relative legal safety.

items.title: 2024 浙江（1月） 阅读D
items.passage: The Stanford marshmallow (棉花糖) test was originally conducted by psychologist Walter Mischel in the late 1960s. Children aged four to six at a nursery school were placed in a room. A single sugary treat, selected by the child, was placed on a table. Each child was told if they waited for 15 minutes before eating the treat, they would be given a second treat. Then they were left alone in the room. Follow-up studies with the children later in life showed a connect ion between an ability to wait long enough to obtain a second treat and various forms of success. As adults we face a version of the marshmallow test every day. We’ re not tempted (诱惑) by sugary treats, but by our computers, phones, and tablets — all the devices that connect us to the global delivery system for various types of information that do to us what marshmallows do to preschoolers. We are tempted by sugary treats because our ancestors lived in a calorie-poor world, and our brains developed a response mechanism to these treats that reflected their value — a feeling of reward and satisfaction. But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat. A similar process is at work in our response to information. Our formative environment as a species was information-poor, so our brains developed a mechanism that prized new information. But global connectivity has greatly changed our information environment. We are now ceaselessly bombarded (轰炸) with new information. Therefore, just as we need to be more thoughtful about our caloric consumption, we also need to be more thoughtful about our information consumption, resisting the temptation of the mental “junk food” in order to manage our time most effectively.

questions.text: What did the children need to do to get a second treat in Mischel’s test?
options: A. Take an examination alone.
B. Show respect for the researchers.
C. Share their treats with others.
D. Delay eating for fifteen minutes.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段第四句“Each child was told if they waited for 15 minutes before eating the treat, they would be given a second treat.(每个孩子都被告知，如果他们在吃之前等待15分钟，他们将得到第二次奖励。)”可知，在米歇尔的测试中，孩子们需要在吃之前等待15分钟才能得到第二次奖励。故选D。

questions.text: According to paragraph 3, there is a mismatch between ___________.

B. the shortage of sugar and our nutritional needs

questions.explanation: 根据第三段最后一句“But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.(但是，当我们重塑了我们周围的世界，大大减少了获取卡路里的成本和努力时，我们的大脑仍然和几千年前一样，这种不匹配是我们这么多人努力抵抗我们知道不应该吃的诱人食物的核心原因。)”可知，根据第三段可知，丰富的食物供应和我们不曾改变的大脑之间存在不匹配。故选C。

questions.text: What does the author suggest readers do?
options: A. Absorb new information readily.
B. Be selective information consumers.
C. Use diverse information sources.
D. Protect the information environment.

items.passage: The greening of planes, trains and automobiles Moving goods and people around the world is responsible for a large part of global CO2 emissions. As the world races to decarbonize everything, it faces particular problems with transportation — which accounts for about a quarter of our energy-related greenhouse gas emissions. Here's the breakdown of the emissions in 2018 for different modes of transport. The fuels for transport need to be not just green, cheap and powerful, but also lightweight and safe enough to be carried around. Each mode of transport has its specific fuel needs. Much is still to be settled, but here are some of the solutions to get us going green. This energy transition is global, and the amount of renewable energy the world will need is "a little bit mind-blowing," says mechanical engineer Keith Wipke at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. It's estimated that the global demand for electricity could more than double by 2050. Fortunately, analyses suggest that renewables are up to the task. "We need to speed up the development of green energy, and it will all get used," says Wipke.

questions.text: What percentage of global transport emissions did road vehicles account for in 2018?
questions.explanation: 根据图表信息，道路客运（ROAD PASSENGER）占45.1%，道路货运（ROAD GOODS）占29.4%，两者相加45.1%+29.4%=74.5%，即道路车辆在2018年全球交通排放中占比74.5%。A选项11.6%和D选项86.1%无原文依据；B选项45.1%仅为客运部分，遗漏了货运。

items.passage: In my ninth-grade writing class last year, I met a cowboy who saved his town, a strict father who demanded his son earn straight A's, and a modern-day Juliet who died of heartbreak after her parents rejected the love of her young life. More than once, I found myself wondering just how my students, who'd created these people, knew their subjects so well. But things were different for their first essay, which was about the question: "Why is writing important?" Most of the essays filled less than one page, and few contained a sentence that could be interpreted as a thesis statement. I was shocked. Then I realized that the problem was the question itself. They could have written pages on the necessity of computers, but writing, in and of itself, simply didn't strike them as important. This would have to change. As a new unit started, I asked everyone to write a persuasive piece on a health-related topic of their choice. This time they found the exercise much more interesting. For the next two assignments, a personal-narrative unit followed by a creative-writing workshop, I only required that the piece meet the specifications of its genre and that it contain a thesis. The results were staggering. The students took on diverse topics and turned in stories, 10 to 20 pages each, with characters that broadened my view and touched my heart. I walked into class believing that writing is important as a means of communication. However, my students demonstrated something more important to me. When the final bell rang in June, I walked away with a yearbook full of messages about writing's most powerful significance — the ability to connect people, to put us in another's skin, to teach us what it means to be human.

questions.text: Who are the people mentioned at the beginning of paragraph 1?

questions.explanation: 根据第一段'my students, who'd created these people'可知，牛仔、严厉的父亲和现代版朱丽叶都是学生在写作中创造出来的虚构人物。A选项九年级学生是创作者而非被创造者；B选项学生家长和C选项现代作家均无原文依据。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "staggering" in paragraph 3 mean?

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅰ卷 阅读C
items.passage: While safety improvements might have been made to our streets in recent years, transport studies also show declines in pedestrian mobility, especially among young children. Many parents say there's too much traffic on the roads for their children to walk safely to school, so they pack them into the car instead. Dutch authors Thalia Verkade and Marco te Brömmelstroet are bothered by facts like these. In their new book Movement: How to Take Back Our Streets and Transform Our Lives, they call for a rethink of our streets and the role they play in our lives. Life on city streets started to change decades ago. Whole neighbourhoods were destroyed to make way for new road networks and kids had to play elsewhere. Some communities fought back. Most famously, a Canadian journalist who had moved her family to Manhattan in the early 1950s led a campaign to stop the destruction of her local park. Describing her alarm at its proposed replacement with an expressway, Jane Jacobs called on her mayor to champion "New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through." Similar campaigns occurred in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s as well. Although these campaigns were widespread, the reality is that the majority of the western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car. The number of cars on roads has been increasing rapidly. In Australia we now have over twenty million cars for just over twenty-six million people, among the highest rate of car ownership in the world. We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs. Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can't move safely around our communities? The authors of Movement have it right: it's time to think differently about that street outside your front door.

questions.text: What phenomenon does the author point out in paragraph 1?
options: A. Cars often get stuck on the road.
B. Traffic accidents occur frequently.
C. People walk less and drive more.
D. Pedestrians fail to follow the rules.
questions.explanation: 根据第一段'transport studies also show declines in pedestrian mobility'和'Many parents say there's too much traffic...so they pack them into the car instead'可知，作者指出的现象是行人流动性下降、人们更多选择开车。A选项汽车常堵车、B选项交通事故频发、D选项行人不遵守规则均非第一段所述现象。

questions.text: What were the Canadian journalist and other campaigners trying to do?
options: A. Keep their cities livable.
B. Promote cultural diversity.
C. Help the needy families.
D. Make expressways accessible.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Jane Jacobs呼吁市长捍卫'New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through'可知，她和其他运动参与者旨在阻止公园被高速公路取代，保持城市的宜居性。B促进文化多样性、C帮助贫困家庭、D使高速公路更便捷均与原文不符。

questions.text: What can be inferred about the campaigns in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s?
options: A. They boosted the sales of cars.
B. They turned out largely ineffective.
C. They won government support.
D. They advocated building new parks.
questions.explanation: 根据倒数第二段'Although these campaigns were widespread, the reality is that the majority of the western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car. The number of cars on roads has been increasing rapidly.'可推知，尽管澳大利亚的运动很普遍，但大多数西方城市仍完全围绕汽车重新设计，汽车数量激增，说明这些运动基本上没有效果。A促进汽车销售、C赢得政府支持、D倡导新建公园均无原文依据。

questions.text: What can be a suitable title for the text?
options: A. Why the Rush?
B. What's Next?
C. Where to Stay?
D. Who to Blame?
questions.explanation: 本文批判城市过度追求交通效率（rush through）、忽视行人需求和城市宜居性的现象。最后一段'We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs'点明主旨。A选项'Why the Rush?'质问匆匆通行的规划理念，契合文章主旨。B接下来怎么办、C住在哪里、D怪谁均不能准确概括全文。

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅰ卷 阅读D
items.passage: Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth — they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and even fallen in fresh Antarctic snow. They are even appearing inside humans. Now, new research suggests that a simple, cheap measure may significantly reduce the level of microplastics in water from your tap: boiling and filtering it. In a study published Wednesday in Environmental Science & Technology Letters, researchers from China found that boiling tap water for just five minutes — then filtering it after it cools — could remove at least 80 percent of its microplastics. Crucially, this process relies on the water containing enough calcium carbonate to trap the plastics. In the study, boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate led to an almost 90 percent drop in plastics. But in samples with less than 60 milligrams of calcium carbonate, boiling reduced the level of plastics by just 25 percent. Additionally, the research didn't include all types of plastics. The team focused only on three common types — polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene — and they didn't study other chemicals previously found in water such as vinyl chloride. Still, the findings show a potential path forward for reducing microplastic exposure — a task that's becoming increasingly difficult. Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought. Scientists are still trying to determine how harmful microplastics are — but what they do know has raised concerns. The new study suggests boiling tap water could be a tool to limit intake. "The way they demonstrated how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice," Caroline Gauchotte-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the research, tells New Scientist. "We should be looking into upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics."

questions.text: How does the author present the issue in the first paragraph?
options: A. By quoting an expert.
B. By defining a concept.
C. By giving examples.
D. By providing statistics.
questions.explanation: 第一段列举了微塑料出现在深海、喜马拉雅山、火山岩、海鸟胃里、南极新雪甚至人体内等多个例子，以此说明微塑料已成为全球常见污染源，因此作者是通过举例（giving examples）来呈现问题的。A引用专家、B定义概念、D提供数据均不符合第一段的写作手法。

questions.text: What determines the effectiveness of trapping microplastics in water?
options: A. The hardness of water.
B. The length of cooling time.
C. The frequency of filtering.
D. The type of plastic in water.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段'this process relies on the water containing enough calcium carbonate to trap the plastics'以及硬水（含300mg碳酸钙）去除近90%而软水（低于60mg）仅去除25%的对比可知，决定煮沸截留微塑料效果的是水中碳酸钙含量，即水的硬度。B冷却时间、C过滤频率、D塑料类型均非决定性因素。

questions.text: What does the author try to illustrate by mentioning bottled water in paragraph 4?
options: A. The importance of plastic recycling.
B. The severity of the microplastic problem.
C. The danger in overusing pure water.
D. The difficulty in treating polluted water.
questions.explanation: 第四段指出减少微塑料接触的任务正变得越来越困难，随即提到'Even bottled water...contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought'，连瓶装水的微塑料含量都远超预期，以此说明微塑料问题的严重性。A塑料回收的重要性、C过度饮用纯水的危险、D处理污水的难度均非作者提及瓶装水的意图。

questions.text: What is Gauchotte-Lindsay's suggestion about?
options: A. Choice of new research methods.
B. Possible direction for further study.
C. Need to involve more researchers.
D. Potential application of the findings.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Gauchotte-Lindsay所说'We should be looking into upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics'可知，她肯定了煮沸法的有效性，并建议将研究成果应用于升级饮用水处理厂，这属于研究发现的潜在应用。A新研究方法选择、B进一步研究方向、C需要更多研究者参与均不符合她的建议内容。

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读A
items.passage: English Market Towns to Visit in the UK English market towns come in many shapes and sizes. Each has a personality shaped by the goods and services produced and traded for centuries. But each town has more to do than shop. Hereford, Herefordshire Hereford has remained a lively market town since 1189. Skirting the town square, you'll find lovely shops, eateries, and the Black and White House Museum. The Hereford Cathedral is the most impressive building in town. It's also home to an ancient library. One of the four original copies of the Magna Carta is displayed there. Ludlow, Shropshire Ludlow is known as the Foodie Center of England. Butcher shops, greengrocers, bakeries, and cheese shops line the town square. Bordering the square, the Ludlow Castle is a "must explore" medieval stronghold. The three-day Ludlow Food Festival is held each September. Shrewsbury, Shropshire Getting to Shrewsbury Town Center from London is challenging but worth the anxiety. The River Severn has a significant turn through town, almost making an island of Shrewsbury Town Center. The shape creates a perfect market where goods could be shipped and received using the river as a highway. Flowers are everywhere-hanging baskets, window boxes, and planters-just what you imagine in an attractive English market town. Mevagissey, Cornwall Even if you haven't been to the small fishing village Mevagissey, you've probably seen it in a movie or British TV show. The working harbor took shape in 1774. Fishermen go out to sea daily and sell their fish in harbor-side markets. Don't leave the harbor without a traditional Cornish pie. It's delicious.

questions.text: Where can you find an original copy of the Magna Carta?
options: A. In the Ludlow Castle.
B. In the Foodie Center of England.
C. In the Hereford Cathedral.
D. In the Black and White House Museum.
questions.explanation: 根据Hereford部分'The Hereford Cathedral is the most impressive building in town. It's also home to an ancient library. One of the four original copies of the Magna Carta is displayed there.'可知，《大宪章》原始副本陈列在赫里福德大教堂。A Ludlow城堡、B英格兰美食中心、D黑白屋博物馆均非存放地点。

questions.text: What is a feature of Shrewsbury Town Center?

B. It's almost surrounded by water.
C. It's known for its flower festival.

questions.explanation: 根据Shrewsbury部分'The River Severn has a significant turn through town, almost making an island of Shrewsbury Town Center.'可知，塞文河在镇中转弯，几乎将镇中心变成一座岛，即几乎被水包围。A附近有大岛曲解原文；C以花节闻名无依据；D从伦敦易到达与原文'challenging'矛盾。

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读B
items.passage: Kathy Ho teaches high school inside Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford (LPCH). "Sometimes I don't like saying that I'm a teacher," says Ho. "People get in their minds an idea of what teachers do, but that's not really what it is here." "Here" is room 386, where each year, about 500 LPCH patients also become students. The hospital school is free of parents, doctors, and medical procedures. It's a place of learning. About half of Ho's students stay for a week or less; others are there for more than a year. Most of Ho's students will recover, which means that preparing them to return to school is an increasingly important component of care. Still, in room 386, academics don't come first. Physical health and mental health are the priority. "If you're scared about something and thinking only about that, there's no way you're going to be able to learn," Ho says. "I'm a coach, an adviser, and a comforter, and that's what it means to be a hospital teacher." There are up to 30 students at any given time in Ho's class. She generally works with their regular teachers to get lessons and tests being used at their home schools. Some teachers don't give the kids any assignments; they express sympathy instead. "I feel like it is a disservice to the kids," Ho says. "They think their teachers don't care about their schoolwork." Ho recognizes the psychological benefit of helping kids keep up with their peers outside the hospital. "I actually think the medicine is only a small piece for some problems," says Julie Good, director of pain management services at LPCH. "It's about problem-solving around what it means to have a full life. Those kids have dreams. School can keep those dreams alive by giving kids a way to learn and grow."

questions.text: Who does Ho teach at LPCH?
options: A. Sick children.
B. Young nurses.
C. Medical students.
D. Patients' parents.
questions.explanation: 根据第二段'where each year, about 500 LPCH patients also become students'和'Most of Ho's students will recover'可知，Ho在儿童医院教的是生病的孩子（患者）。B年轻护士、C医学生、D患者家长均不符合原文。

questions.text: What is a characteristic of Ho's job?
options: A. Prioritizing academics.
B. Encouraging innovation.
C. Treating various diseases.
D. Playing multiple roles.
questions.explanation: 根据第三段Ho所说'I'm a coach, an adviser, and a comforter, and that's what it means to be a hospital teacher.'可知，她同时扮演教练、顾问和安慰者多种角色。A优先学业与原文'academics don't come first'矛盾；B鼓励创新无依据；C治疗疾病不是教师的工作。

questions.text: What does the underlined word "it" refer to in paragraph 4?
options: A. Offering regular lessons.
B. Paying extra attention.
C. Assigning no schoolwork.
D. Showing no sympathy.
questions.explanation: 根据第四段'Some teachers don't give the kids any assignments; they express sympathy instead. "I feel like it is a disservice to the kids," Ho says.'可知，it指代上文'some teachers don't give the kids any assignments'，即不给孩子布置作业这件事。A提供常规课程、B额外关注、D不表同情均不符合指代内容。

questions.text: How does the hospital school benefit the students according to Good?
options: A. It eases peer pressure.

questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Good所说'Those kids have dreams. School can keep those dreams alive by giving kids a way to learn and grow.'可知，学校通过给孩子学习和成长的途径让梦想保持活力，即帮助他们生活在希望中。A缓解同伴压力、C免除疼痛、D用故事娱乐均非Good的观点。

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读C
items.passage: When Sonja Detrinidad opened her online shop selling houseplants, she didn't have high hopes for it. But the opposite happened: She was flooded, shipping out 1,200 orders in June of 2020 alone. In the past year, Detrinidad sent out more than 70,000 plants. Her success is just one example of increased time at home leading to an explosion in the houseplant industry. "Plants are in fashion right now," says Dr. Melinda Knuth, a researcher from the University of Florida. "People who live in plant-rich environments report a higher life satisfaction rating," she says. "Adding more nature to our environment can change our mood and how we think." Plants can improve our state of mind in a few ways but the biggest is by decreasing our level of cortisol, the stress hormone in our body. "Students who are around plants perform better academically than students who are in a classroom without plants," says Knuth. "This productivity also translates into the workplace for adults. Our study showed that there was a 30% decrease in sick leave for people who were in plant-rich workplaces." If you're among the groups of people who are enjoying the mental and physical health benefits of surrounding yourself with plants, don't beat yourself up if one (or a few!) doesn't make it. "Doctors practice medicine and lawyers practice law and you should allow yourself the practice it takes to sustain a plant. Tending to plants is an exercise in patience and learning. Be invested in taking care of it, but if it dies, go get another one," Detrinidad says.

questions.text: How was Detrinidad's business when it started?
options: A. It faced tough competition.
B. It suffered a great loss.
C. It got lots of financial support.

questions.explanation: 根据第一段'she didn't have high hopes for it. But the opposite happened: She was flooded, shipping out 1,200 orders in June of 2020 alone.'可知，她原本没抱太大期望，但订单如潮水般涌来，生意出奇地好。A面临激烈竞争、B遭受重大损失、C获得大量资金支持均与原文不符。

B. They purify the environment.

questions.text: What does Detrinidad try to explain by mentioning doctors and lawyers?

B. The meaning of sustainability.
C. The importance of repeated efforts.
D. The value of professional opinions.
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段'Doctors practice medicine and lawyers practice law and you should allow yourself the practice it takes to sustain a plant. Tending to plants is an exercise in patience and learning.'可知，Detrinidad通过类比医生和律师需要不断实践，说明养植物也需要反复练习和尝试，即使养死了也再养一株。A社交技能必要性、B可持续性意义、D专业意见价值均非类比目的。

items.title: 2025 全国Ⅱ卷 阅读D
items.passage: Does your soul die a little every time you throw away unused food? Mine does. Maybe that feeling comes from growing up in South Africa, where the phrase "there are children starving in Africa" was more of an uncomfortable reminder of fact than a prayer at dinner time. Food waste is a growing concern in the restaurant, supermarket, and supply chain industries. From technological solutions to educational campaigns, food producers and sellers are looking for ways to use more of what we're already growing. But last month, one popular New York City restaurant tried a different way: It changed its menu to exclusively offer food that would otherwise be thrown away. For two weeks in March, Greenwich Village's Blue Hill restaurant was renamed wastED, and served items like fried skate cartilage, a juice pulp burger, and a dumpster diver's vegetable salad. Each dish was tailor-made to raise awareness regarding food waste. A study by the Food Waste Alliance determined that the average restaurant generates 33 pounds of food waste for every $1,000 in revenue, and of that waste only 15.7% is donated or recycled. Up to 84.3% is simply thrown out. Restaurants like Silo in the UK have experimented with zero-waste systems, but wastED took the concept to its logical conclusion. It should be noted that none of the items on wastED's menu was technically made from garbage. Instead, all the ingredients used were examples of meat cuts and produce that most restaurants would never consider serving. Things like kale ribs, fish collars, rejected sweet potatoes, and cucumber butts were all re-appropriated and, with the help of a number of good chefs, turned into excellent cuisine. Though wastED received enthusiastic reviews, it was designed from the start as a short-lived experiment; Blue Hill has since returned to its regular menu. Nevertheless, it serves as a reminder that there are many ways to address problems of sustainability, and that you can make an amazing meal out of almost anything.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's early life?
options: A. He witnessed food shortage.
B. He enjoyed the local cuisine.
C. He donated food to Africans.

questions.explanation: 根据第一段'growing up in South Africa, where the phrase "there are children starving in Africa" was more of an uncomfortable reminder of fact than a prayer'可知，作者在南非长大，那里孩子挨饿是事实，由此可推断作者早年目睹过食物短缺。B喜欢当地美食、C给非洲人捐食物、D在家帮忙做饭均无原文依据。

B. To make the public aware of food waste.
C. To test a food processing method.

questions.explanation: 根据第三段'Each dish was tailor-made to raise awareness regarding food waste.'可知，wastED的每道菜都是为了提高人们对食物浪费的认识而量身定制的。A为客人定制菜肴曲解原文；C测试食品加工方法无依据；D改善英国零浪费系统与原文不符。

items.title: 2025 北京 阅读B
items.passage: Throughout our Junior year, my classmates and I have been worried about what colleges will see when they look at our whole life story reduced to a single 200-word essay. Will the golden word "success" form in their minds when they review our achievements? Or will they see the big word "fail" in red? The shadow of this mysterious institution steals away what success means to us. My first step of redefining success began with course registrations. It is a well-known fact, especially in my school, that Junior year is the time of packing many AP classes into the schedule. When asked why they chose so many AP classes, my friends responded: "I don't know." They themselves don't know why they are following the crowd and longing for the pressures of academic difficulty. Therefore, they do not feel the satisfaction of being academically challenged. Completing many courses no longer brings out the feeling of success because more than four AP classes per year is a norm set by top universities. Determined to follow my instincts on what I felt success means, I only chose two classes that I knew I would enjoy. The feeling of success was no longer attached to what grade I received but to the pure joy of learning. Even my failures are attached to a feeling of success; after I take a step back and look at the big picture, I see them as a launching pad for my next big achievement. In the ninth grade, I went in for my first group interview for a leadership position as a shy girl. Not standing a chance against competitive applicants, I came out of the interview with an upset look. Nevertheless, this interview wasn't a wasted opportunity. I talked to one of the senior applicants who answered questions in a way that reflected the faith she had in herself. This year, with an open mind and new knowledge in mind, I walked into another group interview while telling myself I was that cool senior. I managed to secure a leadership position. Ultimately, success came little by little.
